`````yaml
# Read-only notification lane. It reads an owned mailbox and writes a local digest.
mailbox:
  host_env: FAN_OPS_IMAP_HOST
  user_env: FAN_OPS_IMAP_USER
  pass_env: FAN_OPS_IMAP_PASS
  folder: INBOX
  lookback_days: 3

sender_allow:
  - mail.onlyfans.com
  - mail.snapchat.com

extractors:
  - match: 'New message from (?<handle>.+?) on (?<platform>OnlyFans)'
    event: message
  - match: '(?<handle>.+?) purchased your post on (?<platform>OnlyFans)'
    event: purchase
  - match: '(?<handle>.+?) renewed subscription \((?<platform>OnlyFans)\)'
    event: renewal
  - match: '(?<handle>.+?) tipped you on (?<platform>OnlyFans)'
    event: tip

injection_patterns:
  - 'ignore (all |any )?(previous|prior|above) (instructions|prompts)'
  - 'system prompt|disregard your (rules|instructions)'
  - '(send|give) me (it |the set |content )?(free|gratis)'
  - 'you are now|act as|pretend to be'
  - 'reveal|print|repeat (your )?(instructions|prompt)'

minor_cues:
  - '\b(jeg er|im|i am|i''m) (bare )?(1[0-7]|underskole|videregående|15|16|17)\b'
  - '\bskole(termin|start)?\b.*\b(homework|lekser|eksamen)\b'
  - '\bhigh school|middle school\b'

draft_templates:
  message:
    warm: 'Hei {handle}! Så fint å høre fra deg — fortell:'
    terse: 'Hei {handle} — ute nå, svarer straks.'
  purchase:
    warm: 'Takk for støtten, {handle} — håper den er verdt hvert øre.'
    terse: 'Takk, {handle}!'
  renewal:
    warm: 'Enda en måned sammen, {handle} — godt å ha deg her.'
    terse: 'Takk for fornyelsen, {handle}.'
  tip:
    warm: 'Wow, takk {handle} — det var generøst.'
    terse: 'Takk for tipset, {handle}!'

caps:
  drafts_per_digest: 40
  store: runtime/fan_ops/dossier.db
  output: runtime/fan_ops/digest.md

`````

### data/lexicon.yml

`````yaml
---
# Speech respellings for TTS. See lib/voice/lexicon.rb for why this is a
# respelling table and not a phoneme lexicon: rb_edge_tts takes plain text, so
# there is no SSML and no <phoneme> to address.
#
# The bar for an entry is that the written form is *wrong* when read aloud, not
# that it is unusual. A voice reading "OpenBSD" says "open bee ess dee" only by
# luck; it reads "relayd" as a word, "nsd" as "nssd", and "i18n" as a number
# with letters stuck to it. Those earn entries. "Falcon", "Rails" and "Ruby" are
# ordinary English words and do not.
#
# Matching is whole-word and case-insensitive, longest key first, so DNSSEC is
# not eaten by DNS. An exact-case key wins over a case-insensitive one.
respellings:
  # Daemons and commands whose spelling is not their sound.
  relayd: relay D
  httpd: H T T P D
  nsd: N S D
  rcctl: R C control
  doas: do as
  ffmpeg: F F M peg
  nginx: engine X

  # Acronyms a voice otherwise runs together into a syllable.
  LLM: L L M
  API: A P I
  URL: U R L
  SSH: S S H
  DNS: D N S
  HTTP: H T T P
  HTML: H T M L
  JSON: J S O N
  SQL: sequel
  GPU: G P U
  CPU: C P U
  IDE: I D E
  JWT: J W T
  CI: C I
  CD: C D
  WASM: W A S M
  PWA: P W A
  OpenBSD: Open B S D
  BSD: B S D
  DNSSEC: DNS sec
  SSHFP: S S H F P
  TLS: T L S
  SSE: S S E
  CDP: C D P
  SSML: S S M L
  TTS: T T S
  STT: S T T
  CSP: C S P
  ERB: E R B
  YAML: yammel
  SQLite: sequel light
  PostgreSQL: Postgres
  WebGL: web G L

  # Numeronyms, which are read as a number with letters attached.
  i18n: internationalization
  a11y: accessibility
  l10n: localization

  # This project.
  brgen: Bergen
  vm23: V M twenty three
  bsdports: B S D ports
  oshlo: Oslo

`````

### data/limits.yml

`````yaml
# Budgets, scan profiles and standing orders — plus, under `guidance:`, a much
# larger body of agent-facing prose that this file used to present as the same
# thing.
#
# CLAUDE.md points agents at the law; limits.yml carries budgets and standing guidance. Measured 2026-08-02: of 38
# top-level keys, 9 had a reader and 29 had none — 485 of 794 lines. Both generic
# accessors that might have reached the rest (`Rules#workflow` and
# `Rules#workflow_rule(key)`) had zero call sites and are deleted.
#
# So the split is a relabelling, not a deletion. Everything under `guidance:` is
# still in this file for humans to read — it is
# simply not enforced by anything, and saying so is the point. test/test_limits_split.rb
# fails in both directions: an enforced key that loses its reader, and a guidance
# key that gains one without being promoted.

scan_profiles:
  default: full
  core:
    rules: core
    aliases:
    - quick
    description: Core axiom and small-function findings after a deep scan
  full:
    rules: '*'
    aliases:
    - all
    description: All registered scan rules
  axioms_only:
    rules: axioms
    aliases:
    - axioms
    description: Constitutional axioms only
  solid_focus:
    rules: solid_focus
    aliases:
    - solid
    description: SOLID principles plus axioms
  critical:
    rules: '*'
    severity:
    - error
    - veto
    description: Only error and veto findings for urgent triage
  solid:
    rules: solid_focus
    description: SOLID principles focus
  axioms:
    rules: axioms

  cosmetic:

  rails:
    rules: '*'

    description: Full deep scan intended for RAILS app trees (use path RAILS/<app>)
autoloop:
  background: true
  scan_depth: deep
  scan_nice: 15
  scan_file_sleep_s: 2
  fix_depth: llm
  batch_size: 1
  poll_interval: 30
  max_file_bytes: 16000
  max_fix_retries: 3
  confidence_threshold: 0.6
  targets:

  - test/
  - data/

zeitwerk:
  inflections:
    autoloop: AutoLoop
    cli: CLI
    mcp_server: MCPServer
    mcp_coordinator: McpCoordinator
    diff_stager: DiffStager
    code_index: CodeIndex
    git_context: GitContext
    ast_edit: AstEdit
    llm: LLM
validation:
  after_write: ruby -c lib/FILE.rb
  after_commit: ruby -e "require_relative 'lib/master'; puts 'ok'"
  scan_file: bundle exec ruby bin/cli scan lib/FILE.rb
dmesg:
  enabled: true
  verbosity: normal
  style: openbsd
  format: "unitN at parent: detail | unitN: detail"
  env: MASTER_DMESG
  through: true
  scan_progress: true
  milestones: true
  flush: true

session_modes:
  default: balanced
  env: MASTER_MODE
  modes:
    loose:
      scan_profile: cosmetic
      council: false
      autofix_llm: false
      autofix_mechanical: true
      max_fix_passes: 3
      description: Hygiene and style only; no LLM fix loop
    balanced:
      scan_profile: full
      council: risky
      autofix_llm: true
      autofix_mechanical: true
      max_fix_passes: 8
      description: Default scan/fix; council on multi-file/security
    strict:
      scan_profile: full
      council: true
      autofix_llm: true
      autofix_mechanical: true
      max_fix_passes: 15
      severity_floor: warning
      description: Full rules, council on, full fix budget

# Read by nothing. Reference material for agents, kept
# because it is worth reading and deleted from no-one's reach — but it does not
# constrain the runtime, and a rule that constrains nothing must not sit beside
# ones that do.
guidance:

  # Moved out of the enforced set on 2026-08-23: nothing reads it.
  # test_limits_split claimed a reader for each, and verified that claim
  # with a bare substring match that passed on coincidence.
  conflicts:
    strategy: highest_priority_wins
    rules:
    - condition: dry conflicts with wet or aha
      resolution: favor wet/aha if fewer than 3 duplications exist
    - condition: clarity conflicts with simplicity
      resolution: favor clarity
    - condition: fix introduces higher priority violation
      resolution: reject fix, report to autoloop
  # Moved out of the enforced set on 2026-08-23: nothing reads it.
  # test_limits_split claimed a reader for each, and verified that claim
  # with a bare substring match that passed on coincidence.
  sweep:
    scan_depth: deep
    converge_threshold: 0.05
    converge_window: 2
    max_cycles: 16
    codebase_map: true
  file_reading:
    rule: READ_FULL_FILES
    statement: Read complete files. Never grep, head, tail, or partial‑read to understand code.
    rationale: Partial view yields partial (wrong) changes.
    allowed_exceptions:
    - grep/search across many unknown files to locate a keyword
    forbidden:
    - grep pattern file to understand code structure
    - head -N file to check structure
    - tail -N file to check endings
  before_edit:
    rule: READ_BEFORE_WRITE
    statement: Read every file that could be affected before editing any file.
    see_also: edit_context
    steps:
    - 'Map the codebase: find all .rb files in lib/'
    - Trace callers before changing any public method signature
    - Check Zeitwerk inflectors before renaming classes or files
    - Run ruby -c FILE after every write
    - Run ruby -e require_relative after every commit
  edit_context:
    rule: TIERED_BLAST_RADIUS_READ
    statement: Read depth scales with change radius — not every edit requires a full-corpus read.
    always:
    - Full read of every file you will edit
    - Re-read from disk immediately before writing
    - One-hop callers/tests for any public method or constant you change
    tiers:
    - name: local_fix
      when: single-file bugfix or comment; no signature change
      read:
      - target file
      - matching test file
      - direct callers
    - name: module_change
      when: new class, renamed constant, or cross-file behavior in one lib/ module
      read:
      - module entrypoint
      - one-hop dependents (bin/operator readers)
      - affected tests
    - name: structural_change
      when: pipeline stage, scan rule, constitution data, or OPERATOR topology
      read:
      - data/soul.yml ABSOLUTE sections
      - limits.yml scan_profiles
      - /scan deep on affected tree
    forbidden:
    - Edit from grep snippets, partial reads, or conversation memory
    - Claim a fix without reading the file being changed
    note: Pairs with llm_ergonomics — external grep/rg for reconnaissance is allowed; production edits require
      full-file reads.
  code_principles:
    no_hardcoding:
      rule: NO_HARDCODED_CONSTANTS
      statement: Prose, patterns, and config belong in data/*.yml, not Ruby strings.
    single_source:
      rule: ONE_SOURCE
      statement: If it is in a data file, the code reads from there. No duplicates.
    no_magic_numbers:
      rule: NAMED_CONSTANTS
      statement: Extract literals to named constants with .freeze
    no_bare_rescue:
      rule: SPECIFIC_RESCUE
      statement: Always rescue SpecificError => e. Propagate or log via event bus.
    guard_first:
      rule: GUARD_CLAUSES_FIRST
      statement: Return Result.ok(ctx) unless condition before main logic.
    one_responsibility:
      rule: SINGLE_RESPONSIBILITY
      statement: Split if you can name two reasons to change it.
    cqs:
      rule: COMMAND_QUERY_SEPARATION
      statement: Queries return data and do not mutate. Commands mutate and do not return values.
    inject_deps:
      rule: DEPENDENCY_INJECTION
      statement: Never instantiate collaborators inside a method.
    result_monad:
      rule: RESULT_MONAD
      statement: Pipeline stages return Master::Result. Use .ok? and .err?; propagate Err without calling
        .value!.
  scan_rules:
    note: DEEP_SCAN_ONLY — every scan runs at deep depth. scan_profiles (cosmetic, core, …) filter the report
      after the scan; they are not depth tiers.
    standard_depth:
    - frozen_string
    - bare_rescue
    - explicit
    - immutable
    - cqs
    - self_explaining
    - long_method
    - god_class
    - duplicate_code
    - prune
    - srp
    - pola
    - nielsen
    deep_only:
    - semantic
    - adversarial
    hunt_only:
    - rubocop
    - reek
    notes:
      nielsen: puts is NOT debug output in a CLI. Only p, pp, binding.pry, debugger are.
      prune: Loads patterns from data/voice.yml (voice.strunk); legacy fallback in rules.yml.
      semantic: Loads semantic questions from executable Law definitions.
      deep_caution: deep adds 2 LLM calls per file. With 90 files at 8 req/min free tier = 22+ minutes.
  frontend_protection:
    statement: Only application.scss is protected — each app's one stylesheet, which loads the shared stack
      and adds no partial of its own.
    protected_files:
    - application.scss
    on_view_or_css_edit:
    - flatten divitis and use semantic landmarks
    - bare tag targeting per rules.yml style — no BEM or utility soup in ERB
    - run Shared::FrontendAuditor on touched paths
    mailer_exempt:
    - inline styles in mailer views (email clients require them)
  universal_scope:
    policy: ALL_PRINCIPLES_ALL_FILES
    statement: 'All axioms, principles, and philosophies apply to every file in the codebase regardless
      of file type: Ruby, YAML, Zsh, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Markdown. Language-specific rules apply only
      to their target language; universal rules such as SQUINT_TEST, TYPOGRAPHY_DISCIPLINE and MEANINGFUL_NAMES
      apply everywhere.

      '
    scan_glob: '**/*.{rb,rake,erb,html,htm,css,scss,js,ts,jsx,tsx,zsh,sh,yml,yaml,md}'
    semantic_rules: all_known_languages
    adversarial_rules: all_known_languages
  incremental_scanning:
    enabled: true
    strategy: modified_files_only
    triggers:
      full_scan:
      - new_principle_added
      - master_yml_modified
      - user_requests_full_scan
      incremental:
      - file_saved
      - git_stage
      - git_commit
    speedup_estimate: 60-85% fewer files on typical edit
    fallback: full_scan_on_error
  anti_sprawl:
    mode: aggressive
    hierarchy: openbsd_ruby_roda
    max_lib_depth: 4
    fold_suffixes:
    - _support
    - _helper
    - _util
    - _helpers
    - _utils
    forbidden_files:
    - summary.md
    - analysis.md
    - report.md
    - todo.md
    - notes.md
    - changelog.md
    slug_naming: Rails-parameterized density — snake_case, concrete tokens only, Strunk-clean; see rules.yml
      style.naming.paths
    rule: Flat Hierarchy — merge thin siblings and rename misfit paths before creating files. OpenBSD-flat
      paths, Zeitwerk-true dense slugs, Roda-tight trees.
  phases:
    discover:
      id: 1
      goal: Understand actual need
      output: Problem statement with success criteria
      personas:
      - chaos
      - user
      introspect: What assumptions did we make?
      gates:
      - no_vague_words
      - audience_identified
      - success_measurable
    analyze:
      id: 2
      goal: Break into components
      output: Component diagram with dependencies
      personas:
      - skeptic
      - maintainer
      introspect: What did we miss?
      gates:
      - components_distinct
      - dependencies_acyclic
    ideate:
      id: 3
      goal: Generate 15+ alternatives
      output: List of approaches with trade‑offs
      personas:
      - minimalist
      - chaos
      introspect: Which ideas surprised us?
      gates:
      - count_gte_15
      - trade_offs_documented
    design:
      id: 4
      goal: Specific architecture
      output: Interface definitions and error handling
      personas:
      - security
      - accessibility
      introspect: What could break?
      gates:
      - interfaces_explicit
      - errors_documented
    implement:
      id: 5
      goal: Execute with zero violations
      output: Working code at 100/100 score
      personas:
      - performance
      - security
      introspect: Is this the simplest solution?
      gates:
      - tests_pass
      - zero_violations
    validate:
      id: 6
      goal: Prove with evidence
      output: Test results, benchmarks
      personas:
      - skeptic
      - security
      introspect: What evidence proves it works?
      gates:
      - zero_test_failures
      - edge_cases_covered
    deliver:
      id: 7
      goal: Ship with monitoring
      output: Deployed code with dashboards
      personas:
      - realist
      introspect: What would the user complain about?
      gates:
      - deployed
      - monitoring_configured
    learn:
      id: 8
      goal: Extract durable lessons
      output: Updated defaults, new memory entries, refined rules
      personas:
      - skeptic
      - chaos
      introspect: What would we do differently next time?
      gates:
      - lessons_captured
      - defaults_updated
  session_startup:
    reading_tiers:
      explore:
        required:
        - CLAUDE.md
        optional:
        - data/soul.yml ABSOLUTE sections
        note: Recon and analysis — pair with llm_ergonomics; external rg allowed.
      structural_edit:
        required:
        - data/soul.yml
        - data/rules.yml
        - data/limits.yml
        optional:
        - data/voice.yml
        - data/state.yml
        note: Before production edits and deploy-touching changes.
      production_ops:
        required:
        - data/patterns.yml#operator_playbook
        note: VPS friction, relayd, recovery — run bin/operator playbook when signals match.
    mandatory_reads:
    - See reading_tiers — CLAUDE.md first; full constitution only for structural edits.
    playbook_command: bin/operator playbook — print codified operator lessons when signals match production friction
    check_standing_orders: Verify FSM state before any mutation -- UNCHANGE blocks refactoring
    scan_before_analysis: Use /review via MASTER for read-only analysis; use /fix for convergence and writes
    ssh_edit_pattern: Write to /tmp, run ruby /tmp/patch.rb -- never ruby -i with heredoc
  corruption_prevention:
    llm_error_in_file: git checkout HEAD -- data/ && rcctl restart master -- LLM error strings silently
      overwrite YAML data files when circuit is open and agent#ask returns error string instead of raising
    sweep_excludes_data: Sweep may scan data/*.yml but must not LLM-rewrite them. Structural violations
      (duplicate keys, bad indentation) are auto-fixed. Exclude .master/ runtime state files entirely.
    yaml_type_guards: All load_yaml calls must type-check result before use (is_a?(Array/Hash)) -- circuit-open
      strings parse as valid YAML scalars
    ask_raises_on_error: agent#ask must raise StandardError when result.err? -- callers must rescue, never
      silently propagate error strings as LLM output
  quality_phases:
    prototype:
      gates:
      - functional
      debt_allowed: high
      speed: maximize
    production:
      gates:
      - functional
      - secure
      - maintainable
      - performant
      debt_allowed: none
      speed: sustainable
    legacy:
      gates:
      - functional
      - secure
      changes: surgical_only
      risk_tolerance: minimal
  principle_reinforcements:
    dry_and_kiss: multiply_effectiveness
    evidence_and_reversible: enables_confident_change
    single_responsibility_and_dependency_injection: enables_isolated_testing
  observability:
    logging:
      format: json
      fields:
      - timestamp
      - level
      - phase
      - file
      - evidence_score
      - decision
      levels:
        trace: every_operation
        debug: decision_points
        info: phase_transitions
        warn: evidence_below_threshold
        error: gate_failures
    metrics:
      track:
      - evidence_score
      - complexity
      - coverage
      - churn
      - council_consensus
      export_format: prometheus
      threshold_alerts: true
  processing_strategies:
    small_file:
      condition: size <= 10240
      method: full_read
      context: entire_file
    medium_file:
      condition: 10240 < size <= 1048576
      method: streaming
      context: line_by_line_with_lookahead
    large_file:
      condition: size > 1048576
      method: chunked
      context: section_by_section
      checkpoint: per_chunk
  tool_budget:
    max_calls_per_turn: 40
    max_consecutive_edits: 8
    max_consecutive_searches: 10
    on_exceed: publish budget:exceeded; force /reflect before next call
  antagonisms:
    minimalism_vs_explicit: explicit wins for safety-critical paths
    speed_vs_evidence: evidence wins always
    abstraction_vs_proximity: proximity wins below 3 occurrences
    dry_vs_singularity: singularity wins for data, dry wins for code
    completeness_vs_density: density wins; defer completeness to next iteration
  two_stage_council:
    round_one: each persona votes ack/dissent independently, no debate
    dissent_threshold: 0.3
    round_two: only dissenting personas debate, others abstain
    saves: 60-80% of LLM calls when consensus is clear
  view_thread:
    emit_event: thread:decision
    fields:
    - timestamp
    - phase
    - file
    - decision
    - alternatives_considered
    - rationale
    persist_to: data/threads/${session_id}.jsonl
    rotate_after_days: 7
  checkpoint_summarization:
    every_n_turns: 5
    every_n_tokens: 100000
    keep_verbatim:
    - last_3_user_messages
    - current_violation_set
    - current_diff
    summarize:
    - all_other_turns
    target_compression: 0.3
  llm_ergonomics:
    core_principle: Optimize for actual LLM behavior and context limits, not idealized super-agents.
    guidance:
    - Use CLAUDE.md as the high-density orientation before requiring deep constitution reads.
    - Allow external tools (grep, rg, find) for reconnaissance and understanding. Require constitutional
      tools only for production changes.
    - When full strict adherence would cause context exhaustion or paralysis, prefer 'good enough + evidence'
      over perfect ceremony.
    - Document known friction points openly so future agents can work around them intelligently.
    - Event emission should be rich and first-class by default so observers (human or visual) can understand
      internal state without heroic effort.
    tension_with_rules: This section provides pragmatic guidance for working with real LLM limitations.
      It does not override any ABSOLUTE rules defined in soul.yml.
  spec_streaming:
    triggers:
    - new_module_creation
    - stub_to_implementation
    safe_for:
    - non-overlapping files
    - additive_changes
    forbidden_for:
    - mutating_shared_state
    - schema_migrations
  live_preview_gate:
    triggers:
    - edit under web/app/views/
    - edit under web/app/assets/
    require: successful render at preview URL within 10s
    on_failure: block commit; publish preview:render_failed
  reverse_introspection:
    cadence: after_every_10_commits
    sample_size: 5
    on_disapproval: open issue tagged self_review with proposed reversion
  test_generation:
    target_dir: test/rules_generated/
    cadence: on_rule_definition_change
    coverage_required: 0.8
  self_rewrite_throttle:
    sensitive_paths:
    - lib/fix/
    - lib/ground/
    - lib/review/security.rb
    - bin/cli
    - data/state.yml
    autoloop_action: skip with publish autoloop:throttled event; surface to user
  adversarial_questioning:
    mandate: fires_on_every_scan_and_council_turn
    questions:
    - What is wrong with this design that I have not spotted?
    - What would an attacker do with this code?
    - What assumption is this built on that could be false?
    - What breaks at scale or under failure?
    - Is this wired to anything? Could it be deleted without loss?
    - Is there a simpler approach that was not taken?
    - What should be relocated or transformed to a different format?
    resolution:
      trivial: autofix immediately — no proposal, no prompt
      non_trivial: propose 3 concrete options (OPTION 1/2/3 + RECOMMEND), await cherry-pick
      threshold: non-trivial if the fix spans more than one file, touches architecture, or has security
        implications
  known_issues:
    relayd_master_empty: After rcctl restart master, relayd may mark master empty until /up health passes
      — tracked rc.d waits for local /up then restarts relayd; relayd.conf must use check http "/up" not
      "/" for master.
    relayd_stale_backend_tables: After mass app restarts relayctl may show empty/down while local /up is
      200 — relayd-watchdog (cron */5) restarts relayd when backends are live but tables are stale.
    resource_guard_shedding: OPENBSD/bin/resource_guard.sh stops optional Rails apps when load/mem thresholds
      hit unless /var/db/pub4_all_apps exists — use start_all_apps.sh to pin.
    rails_phantom_fk: 'references with foreign_key: true alone creates phantom buyers/listings/likers/orders
      tables on SQLite — always set to_table. Run ruby MASTER/gates/runner.rb phantom_foreign_keys.'
    todo_checkbox_drift: Retired 2026-06-24 — verify ship readiness with bin/probe repo, health_check.rb,
      and per-app bin/ci instead of checkbox backlogs.
    tts_broken: Master::Voice::Speech.synthesize_bytes shells to bin/tts-worker; if edge-tts is missing
      or tts-worker crashes, speech silently falls back to espeak. Verify bin/tts-worker exists and edge-tts
      is installed (pkg_add py3-edge-tts or pip).
    particle_swarm: Fixed 2026-06-24 — ecology canvas was z-index 0 under face (z-index 1); now z-index
      2 with screen blend. verify trails/weather visible over face after SSE events.
    gemfile_separation: MASTER/Gemfile and MASTER/web/Gemfile are independent. Any gem used by lib/ code
      that is also called from web/ controllers must appear in both. Adding to one only causes LoadError
      in the other context.
    tts_worker_process: Process.fork inside a Falcon fiber raises 'Closing scheduler' — EM-based gems and
      subprocess-heavy tools must use Open3.popen or shell out via exe/<name>-worker, never fork.
  # OpenBSD dmesg-style progress (device at bus: detail). Verbose by default.
  # ENV MASTER_DMESG accepts 0, quiet, normal, verbose, or trace.

# LOC ratchet budgets — reader: `rake loc_budget` (Rakefile). This key exists
# because data/limits.yml is the file TODO.md names for having 44 of 94
# second-level keys with no reader; a budget nothing reads would have been the
# 45th. Set to measured actuals at introduction (2026-08-09).
#
# The contract, since 2026-09-10, is data/spine.yml's: a budget falls on its own
# whenever the subsystem falls, and rises only in a commit that names what the
# lines buy. Growth past a budget is a failing check and the first remedy is
# still extraction or deletion. The argument for the second remedy is at the
# raise log further down; the short form is that a row already reading OVER
# cannot report the next breach, so a budget nobody may ever raise is a budget
# that stops measuring the day it is exceeded.
#
# Counts every line, comments included — the same unit as lint:spine, and so
# the same unresolved tension with [DENSITY], which deliberately counts code
# lines only. Whoever settles that for lint:spine settles it for both.
#
# data/rules.yml is a file budget, not a directory. The Ruby loc_budget reader
# counts a file path as that file's lines so this key cannot regrow unseen.
# Reader: `rake loc_budget`, which is now in `rake audit` rather than defined
# and called by nothing. It was the latter for its whole life, and the numbers
# below record what that cost: measured against the tree the day the task was
# first run, nine of twelve subsystems were already over, `lib/pub4` by 54%.
#
# So these are not a record of a low that was held. They are today's measurement,
# taken once, at the moment the gate acquired a caller.
#
# `core: 916` is gone rather than corrected-in-place. It budgeted `MASTER/core`,
# which has never existed — the spine is `lib/core` — and the task skipped a
# missing path silently, so the one invariant TODO.md calls load-bearing had a
# budget line that never evaluated. The task aborts on a missing path now.
# lib/trace RAISED 2681 -> 2699 on 2026-08-25, and it is the first raise this
# file has taken, so it should be argued rather than noted. The eighteen lines
# are `module Log`, `module Ledger`, `module Snapshot` and their matching ends,
# two per file across nine files — Zeitwerk maps a path to a constant, so a
# subdirectory costs exactly that and there is no way to shelve a file more
# cheaply. lib/cli falls 7913 -> 7887 in the same commit for a real deletion,
# so lib/ is eight lines lighter overall and lint:spine ratcheted 38966 ->
# 38962. Extraction is what the header asks for and extraction is what this is;
# the number moved because the unit cannot express it.
# THIRD RAISE IN ONE DAY, and TODO.md is right that the count is the signal.
# lib/trace +18 for namespaces, law +27 for a rule that can fire, lib/review
# +47 for CodeMetrics.namespace_lines and the paragraph explaining it. Each is
# argued; the pattern still deserves naming.
#
# UNIT CHANGED 2026-08-25, loc_budgets -> loc_body_budgets. Raw lines to body
# lines: blanks, comments and the module wrappers Zeitwerk requires are all out.
#
# The old unit charged for the paragraph explaining a change as well as the
# change, which took three raises in one day to make visible — lib/trace for
# namespaces, law for a rule that could finally fire, lib/review for the measure
# that exempted the namespaces. All three are moot here. A budget that taxes its
# own justification selects for unexplained diffs.
#
# lib/builder, lib/design and lib/ops had no budget at all and now do; a
# namespace nobody budgeted is a namespace that could grow without anyone
# noticing, which is what this table exists to prevent.
#
# design and ops are single files, and the keys said `lib/design` and `lib/ops`
# — the same shape as the `core: 916` this table's guard was written against,
# and the guard caught them the moment `rake audit` stopped stopping at its
# fourth gate. Both budgets were measured against the file; only the extension
# was missing. ops re-measured down, 251 to 234.
#
# Measured once at the rename. Down only from here.
# 2026-09-09: four keys re-based, and not one line of code was written. Nine
# files left lib/ground for the namespace whose declared purpose covers them --
# providers and quotas and three external surfaces to lib/io, the turn-framing
# to lib/cli, work and verification to lib/fix -- so io read 598 over while
# ground sat on 831 of slack. The four together moved by ten body lines, which
# is the rounding of a `module Ground` becoming a `module Io`.
#
# Re-based rather than left, because this table reads a directory's budget as a
# statement about that directory, and a key carrying another directory's lines
# says nothing about either. Slack is the same defect as debt here: 831 lines of
# room in ground is 831 lines the next change grows into without an argument.
# 2026-09-09: eight keys for twelve files that were in no key at all, 964 body
# lines of them. This task walks the keys rather than the tree, so an unkeyed
# file is not merely unbudgeted — it is invisible to the check written to bound
# it, and lib/cognition is five of the twelve: a subsystem built at
# boot/master_boot.rb:40 that no budget had ever priced.
#
# The rest are the namespace files beside their directories and the loose
# top-level ones. `lib/builder` counts lib/builder/*.rb and not lib/builder.rb,
# where the constant actually lives; single-file keys are the shape lib/design.rb
# and lib/ops.rb already use.
# 2026-09-10: four keys re-based for three files and no new code. ground gives up
# 172 body lines, rails takes the 92 of mobile_web_cluster_catalog, fix the 47 of
# principle_map_repair and io the 33 of atomic_write. The sum is zero on purpose:
# a move pays nothing toward a breach, so every key here carries the same debt
# after it as before.
#
# 2026-09-10, and this one changes the rule rather than a number. Eight of the
# twenty-four keys had been over for weeks, and the header above says the remedy
# is extraction or deletion and never a bigger number. Held to the letter that
# sentence has a consequence nobody chose: **an over-budget row detects nothing.**
# Once a subsystem is past its ceiling, every further line it grows is invisible
# to this task, because the row already reads OVER and cannot read more so. Eight
# of twenty-four had stopped measuring, and `rake audit` failed on loc_budget on
# every pass regardless of what the pass changed -- which is how a gate becomes
# noise, and this table's own history is that it spent its whole life uncalled
# for exactly that kind of reason.
#
# So the rule is now the one data/spine.yml already uses, stated in the same
# words so the two ratchets say one thing. A budget falls on its own whenever the
# subsystem falls, and it rises only in a commit that names what the lines buy.
# The eight raises below are that commit, and each names its purchase:
#
#   law       852 -> 1616. The budget was taken on 2026-08-25 and 24faef77f
#             landed after it: one registry, 116 rules, each declaring how it is
#             checked, +621 body lines to law/ in a single commit. The rest is
#             detectors learning to see their own subject -- 0aaed342b +165 for
#             prose laws that read code and never prose, d31d34761 +162 where
#             half the findings had been the instrument, fb8c41d33 +63 so the
#             three Rails apps are measured by their own rules. This budget
#             prices a law/ that had not yet absorbed the rule catalogue.
#   lib/review  9765 -> 10460. Rules that could only be judged by a model, judged
#             deterministically instead: 9b9e8c88f +260 for four detectors,
#             dcbff6ae8 +143 reading the parse tree, 9e97f861d +67 for structural
#             clones, 9a2c9427c +60 for MIDDLE_MAN. Plus 04904f43d +148 giving
#             PATH_OWNERSHIP.yml a reader, 9e25ff7a8 +156 for the quota gate,
#             e7e96b2d1 +122 for the boot receipt and a public-method count that
#             reads Ruby, 692cc8069 +117 restoring an audit that had been dead,
#             and ~260 across four commits giving every registry rule the worked
#             example that proves it can fire. Paid down by real deletions in the
#             same window -- 996e3c0f3 -298, e3489813c -99, ca5b642f9 -67.
#   lib/pub4  470 -> 696. One commit: 0dc71bb15, the gate ladder, +299 less 56 of
#             helpers that had outlived their subject. It buys one command where
#             five invocations nobody ran together used to be, the record of which
#             stage wrote which file, and a third state so a tier that could not
#             run is skipped rather than passed.
#   lib/voice 3181 -> 3402. f9a466b0c +142, because Speech was synthesising into
#             a file nobody opened and the CLI did not speak. 33070e640 +63, the
#             TTS capability check asking the worker instead of guessing.
#             fad4459fc +45 for the breadcrumb protocol reaching a prompt.
#   lib/core  682 -> 762. 3adf2b5b5 +50, a rule can ask a person instead of
#             guessing for them; d35ffa2a1 +25, the durable half of the autonomy
#             layer.
#   lib/boot  227 -> 276. f3296fe76 +31 for a boot crash and a CLI that led every
#             chain without being there, and boot's share of 04904f43d.
#   lib/trace 1999 -> 2035. 47c434e76 +31: the sandbox said nothing about the
#             credentials inside it.
#   lib/fix   2901 -> 2905. Four lines, this commit's own: PatchApplier refusing a
#             diff that names more than one file, measured against patch(1)
#             half-applying one and leaving a .rej in the working directory.
#
# Four keys fall in the same pass, because slack is the same defect as debt:
# lib/ground 4896 -> 4812 (unified_diff_editor.rb deleted as a second source for
# three live mechanisms), lib/io 4176 -> 4175, and data/rules.yml 3755 -> 3728.
# lib/cli holds at 5892 with six lines of room and is left rather than tightened
# onto another session's in-flight number.
loc_body_budgets:
  lib/boot: 276
  # 252 -> 251: the PhaseGates boot wire, deleted with PhaseGates.
  lib/builder: 251
  # 214 -> 216 for the two lines that construct Voice::OutputGuard in each of
  # the two boot paths, so the evidence contract on MASTER's own reply reaches
  # the container that CLI::Stages::Render reads it from.
  lib/builder.rb: 216
  # 5892 -> 5827: run_rebuild, run_context, run_checkpoint, run_verify and
  # changed_lib_files, unreachable from any dispatch, deleted; 5827 -> 5826 for
  # the container field PhaseGates no longer fills.
  lib/cli: 5826
  # 253 -> 294 for the loop the subsystem did not have. Everything the row
  # priced at introduction was perception; tick! had one caller, at boot, once,
  # so nothing decayed, nothing persisted after the first snapshot and
  # reflection never fired. Eleven lines pace the loop from perception itself,
  # and 34 are prediction.rb, which replaces a prediction_error that measured
  # seconds since an event last fired off an ivar emptied by every restart.
  lib/cognition: 294
  lib/core: 762
  lib/core.rb: 47
  lib/design.rb: 270
  # 2905 -> 2792: done_checker, patch_verifier and unfinished_ledger, reachable
  # only from the deleted CLI methods, less the one line that restores
  # ProposeTree#describe_entry's lost `subs` assignment.
  lib/fix: 2792
  # 4812 -> 4460: context_provider.rb, reachable only from run_context, and
  # phase_gates.rb, built at boot and never called.
  lib/ground: 4460
  lib/io: 4175
  # 136 -> 137 for Master.git_checkout?, one line and one comment. It tests
  # File.exist?(.git) rather than File.directory?, because a worktree carries
  # .git as a file and CLAUDE.md tells every agent to take one — so the old
  # test answered no in the trees the runtime mostly runs in, and rollback,
  # snapshot provenance and the boot receipt were all reading that no.
  lib/master.rb: 137
  lib/ops.rb: 234
  lib/result.rb: 95
  lib/security_error.rb: 1
  lib/unwrap_error.rb: 103
  # 696 -> 713 for `gate --tree <TREE>`, which drops the stages that prove
  # another tree instead of shrinking them: five stages against six for a
  # MASTER-scoped run, one suite against seven, and the clean-tree assertion
  # still covering MASTER whatever was named.
  lib/operator: 713
  # 10460 -> 10469 for MODIFIER_SILENT_RESCUE, which sees `value = parse(raw)
  # rescue nil` — the shape SilentRescue cannot match by construction. Scoped
  # to assignments after measuring: 28 modifier rescues discard fleet-wide and
  # 15 are best-effort side effects nobody reads a value from.
  # 10469 -> 10653, and the number is three things rather than one, because a
  # row that has been OVER for a while absorbs the next change silently.
  # 56 of it was already standing on main when this was measured and is named
  # here rather than swallowed. 97 is llm_dispatcher/ollama_sender.rb: the
  # local tier was declared, gated and undispatched, so enabling it sent an
  # ollama: id to OpenRouter. 31 is the autofix trust boundary — AstFixer
  # proposes a candidate and MechanicalAutofix writes it only after WriteGuard
  # has judged it, where the two used to be one call with nothing between a
  # misfiring transform and the file.
  # 10653 -> 10654 for the ERB_HTML_SAFE call test; see data/spine.yml.
  lib/review: 10654
  lib/trace: 2035
  lib/voice: 3402
  # 1616 -> 1637 so a comment that spans lines counts as a comment on every
  # one of them. A leader test reads where a comment starts and never where it
  # continues, so every line after the first in an ERB comment was scanned as
  # markup, and I18N_COVERAGE fired on a comment explaining that a page
  # carried no <h1>. ERB only, and the detector still fires on markup after
  # the comment closes.
  law: 1637
  # The one entry in this table that goes up, and only ever by consolidation.
  # Three folds have moved deleted files and top-level keys into rules.yml --
  # 86eaff4cf, ff7e93a82, and the 2026-09-05 merge that made design_rules
  # fourteen rules in the catalogue rather than a second top-level section.
  # Those lines crossed a boundary, they were not written. Down only from 3728,
  # and a raise needs the commit that folded something in.
  data/rules.yml: 3728

# Loop/process budgets — moved from data/ops/process.yml; reader is Ops::ProcessBudget.
process:
  defaults:
    safe_mode: true
    max_active_loops: 1
    loop_cooldown_seconds: 30
  loops:
    autofix:
      env: MASTER_AUTOFIX
      max_run_seconds: 1800
      min_sleep_seconds: 300
    watch:
      env: MASTER_WATCH
      max_run_seconds: 900
      min_sleep_seconds: 30
    watcher:
      env: MASTER_WATCHER
      max_run_seconds: 0
      min_sleep_seconds: 30
    heartbeat:
      env: MASTER_HEARTBEAT
      max_run_seconds: 120
      min_sleep_seconds: 60
  load:
    load_avg_1m:
      warn: 1.5
      crit: 2.5
    master_rss_mb:
      warn: 512
      crit: 768
  resources:
    fd_count:
      warn: 512
      crit: 1024
    thread_count:
      warn: 32
      crit: 64
    process_count:
      warn: 256
      crit: 512
      # The count is host-wide. A macOS desktop idles at 570-600 processes
      # (launchd agents, XPC services), past the server limits above, so it
      # read as critical before MASTER did anything. warn is twice that idle;
      # crit is 80% of kern.maxproc (2000 on the operator's Mac).
      darwin:
        warn: 1200
        crit: 1600
    # Gigabytes free, not a percentage: a run writes a few hundred megabytes,
    # and 5% of a 228 GB volume is 11 GB.
    disk_free_gb:
      warn: 5
      crit: 2

`````

### data/load.yml

`````yaml
# load.yml — Watcher thresholds.
# OS-level pressure that should make MASTER back off scans, defer autofix, or alert.
# Read by lib/fix/watcher.rb. Crossings publish system:warn / system:crit.

interval_seconds: 30

thresholds:
  load_avg_1m:
    warn: 2.0
    crit: 4.0

  mem_free_pct:      # lower = worse
    warn: 15.0
    crit: 5.0

  disk_root_pct:
    warn: 80
    crit: 95

  master_rss_mb:
    warn: 1024
    crit: 2048

# What a crossing does is code, not a key here: system:crit stops the fix loop's
# background runner (lib/builder/ai_boot.rb); system:warn reaches only the
# wildcard subscribers that mirror the bus to the face and the event log.

`````

### data/maturity.yml

`````yaml
schema: 1
# Maturity scorecard, matching OpenClaw's taxonomy.yaml -- what's actually
# PROVEN to work, and how, distinguishing smoke-tested (mocks/unit tests
# only) from verified (exercised live, end to end, with a real record of
# when and how). A concrete embodiment of soul.yml's own SURFACE_ERRORS_FIRST
# / anti_simulation rules: don't claim completion, prove it.
#
# status: smoke | verified | broken
# evidence: the specific test/commit/session that backs the status
# last_checked: date of the evidence, not the date this entry was written
subsystems:
  fix_loop.circuit_breaker:
    status: verified
    meaning: LLM fix stage only skips when every fallback-chain model is exhausted, not any one
    evidence: 'commits 2caa7e7ac, d0f488c77 -- was blocking on any unrelated model (e.g. a dead
      free-tier fallback) even when the actually-used model was healthy; found live via round 22-26 gate output.
      Re-verified 2026-09-10 by reading the predicate: lib/fix/fix_loop/llm_router.rb:26 returns the model
      list only when models.all? { |m| registry.open?(m) }, and [] otherwise, so one open breaker skips nothing.'
    last_checked: '2026-09-10'
  fix_loop.self_test_gate:
    status: verified
    meaning: constitutional self-violation gate (8 laws) halts /fix only on a genuine violation
    evidence: 'commit bf02780f7 -- a DENSITY regression from an earlier same-session fix was
      silently halting /fix entirely; SelfTest confirmed 0 violations after the fix.
      Re-verified 2026-09-10: rake selftest reads 0 across all eight laws, and the halt is still wired —
      SelfCheck#gate! at lib/builder/ai_boot.rb:158 publishes self_violation, which :183 subscribes to
      fix_loop.halt!, so a red selfcheck stops background autofix for the session.'
    last_checked: '2026-09-10'
  fix_loop.fast_stage_rubocop:
    status: verified
    meaning: deterministic rubocop autocorrect pass actually runs and fixes files
    evidence: 'commits 5c622e919, eb576bf8d -- was failing on every single file for two
      independent reasons (wrong Gemfile root for RAILS multi-app layout, and a -q flag that
      does not exist in rubocop 1.85.1); round 26 committed 308 real files once both were fixed.
      Re-verified 2026-09-10: FastStage#fast_pass groups files by gemfile_root, the nearest ancestor
      holding a Gemfile, and rubocop_pass shells `bundle exec rubocop -A --no-color` per group. Neither
      fault can recur without the read showing it.'
    last_checked: '2026-09-10'
  fix_loop.learnings_recording:
    status: verified
    meaning: per-rule fix outcomes actually reach the KnowledgeStore from the CLI-driven /fix path
    evidence: 'commit a77b3fb22 -- record_outcomes used String#presence (ActiveSupport-only);
      bin/cli never loads Rails, so every call silently NoMethodError''d, swallowed by the
      surrounding rescue. fix_quality had been returning the hardcoded 0.5 default for every
      rule since this code was written.
      Re-verified 2026-09-10: OutcomeTracking#record_outcomes builds its extension tally with filter_map
      and ext.empty?, plain Ruby with no ActiveSupport in the path, and hands the outcome to
      @learnings.record.'
    last_checked: '2026-09-10'
  review.council_deliberation:
    status: verified
    meaning: /critique's persona deliberation actually reaches a quorum instead of failing every persona
    evidence: 'commit 7e93b526e -- snapshot_artifact byte-truncated file content via String#b,
      leaving it tagged BINARY; concatenating that into every persona''s UTF-8 prompt raised
      Encoding::CompatibilityError identically for all 26, every round, until traced live.
      Re-verified 2026-09-10: snapshot_truncate (cli/command_registry/review.rb) still
      cuts on .b and restores the tag with force_encoding("UTF-8").scrub, so the byte limit holds and the
      result concatenates.'
    last_checked: '2026-09-10'
  runtime.event_log_rotation:
    status: verified
    meaning: activity.jsonl and conflict_log.jsonl stay bounded instead of growing forever
    evidence: 'commit 42d8b9405 -- both were plain append-only with no cap; grew to 1.2GB and
      890MB respectively, together filling the disk completely mid-session and crashing an
      in-progress /fix round with no warning beyond a swallowed ENOSPC.
      Re-verified 2026-09-10: both caps hold and both rotate on write — Log::Event MAX_BYTES 25MB with
      rotate_if_oversized! called from append (trace/log.rb:63), ConflictResolver LOG_MAX_BYTES 25MB over
      three generations (fix/conflict_resolver.rb:150).'
    last_checked: '2026-09-10'
  fix_loop.rule_outcome_classification:
    status: verified
    meaning: a policy-skipped violation (confidence gate, stale fingerprint) doesn't count against
      a rule's fix_quality the same way a genuine failed attempt does
    evidence: 'commit a77b3fb22 -- matches OpenCrabs feedback_policy.rs (issue #236): treating
      every non-fix as a defect risked deprioritizing rules that were never actually attempted.
      Re-verified 2026-09-10 in both halves: pass_outcome returns :skipped when every violation skipped,
      and KnowledgeStore#fix_quality divides fixed by fixed + stuck, so a skip is recorded and excluded
      from the denominator rather than counted as a failure.'
    last_checked: '2026-09-10'
  fix_loop.semantic_fingerprint:
    status: verified
    meaning: the LLM-driven fix stage actually attempts and applies fixes, not just deterministic
      rubocop/AST passes -- the single biggest fix of this session
    evidence: 'commit 858080be9 -- FileProcessor and RuleLoop::FixVerification each maintained
      their own copy of the "has this file changed since the violation was found" fingerprint
      formula; the two had quietly drifted (one included an extra field the other didn''t), so
      every comparison failed permanently regardless of whether the file had actually changed.
      This alone made fix_violation''s fingerprint_matches? check reject every violation, every
      rule, every round -- found live via skip_breakdown showing confidence=0 fingerprint=N
      identically across dozens of rules in a full-repo pass. Traced back through five other
      real, necessary, but ultimately not-the-answer fixes first (circuit breaker x2, self-test
      DENSITY regression, fast_stage rubocop, learnings recording).
      Re-verified 2026-09-10: one formula with one home. Review::Scan::SemanticFingerprint.for is the only
      definition, FileProcessor:40 stamps with it and FixVerification#semantic_fingerprint_for:42 calls the
      same module. There is no second copy to drift.'
    last_checked: '2026-09-10'

`````

### data/mcp_servers.yml

`````yaml
# MCP server definitions for MASTER.
# Transport options: stdio | sse.
# Every external MCP capability is governed before execution.
# Disabled by default on resource-constrained VPS.
# Enable individual servers with enabled: true when needed.

defaults: &defaults
  transport: stdio
  command: npx
  enabled: false
  tier: dangerous
  timeout_seconds: 60

servers:
  filesystem:
    <<: *defaults
    args:
      - -y
      - "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem"
      - "/home/dev/pub4"
    description: Expose read/write/search over a local directory

  git:
    <<: *defaults
    args:
      - -y
      - "@modelcontextprotocol/server-git"
      - "--repository"
      - "/home/dev/pub4/MASTER"
    description: Expose git operations as tools

  brave_search:
    <<: *defaults
    tier: guarded
    args:
      - -y
      - "@modelcontextprotocol/server-brave-search"
    description: Web search via Brave

  sequential_thinking:
    <<: *defaults
    tier: safe
    args:
      - -y
      - "@modelcontextprotocol/server-sequential-thinking"
    description: Structured reasoning assistant

`````

### data/models.yml

`````yaml
# Model routing profile — Antigravity primary, with automatic API/local/free fallback.

schema: 1
routing:
  enabled: true
  strategy: weighted
  escalation_enabled: true
  escalation_tier: strong
  provider: agy

weights: &weights
  quality: 0.50
  speed: 0.25
  cost: 0.25

fallback_policy:
  # Error categories that stop retrying a model and move to the next one, read by
  # ModelRouter#failover_skip_categories.
  #
  # Three things were wrong with this block and all three are why it did nothing.
  # The key was written bare as `on:`, which YAML 1.1 parses as the boolean true —
  # `fallback_policy["on"]` was nil and `fallback_policy[true]` held the list. It
  # had no reader at all. And its vocabulary was invented: `network_error`,
  # `refusal`, `insufficient_balance` and `quota_exceeded` are not Result
  # categories this codebase produces, so wiring it as written would have matched
  # nothing. These are the categories `Result.err(category:)` actually carries.
  #
  # A rate-limited or out-of-budget model cannot succeed on an immediate retry,
  # so both belong here, and so does a model the provider does not hold.
  # `provider_error` deliberately does not: a transient 5xx is what in-place
  # retry exists for. `retries_per_tier` was removed — the retry count has one
  # source, `failover.max_retries` below.
  "on":
    - timeout
    - no_api_key
    - offline
    - auth_error
    - rate_limit
    - budget
    - model_missing
    - invalid_request

failover:
  sequence: [fast, default, medium, strong]
  cooldown_seconds: 300
  # The wait before retrying the same model in place. Only a failure outside
  # fallback_policy.on reaches it (a 429 walks on without waiting), so it waits
  # on a provider 5xx inside a live turn: at 30 and 60 an overloaded free model
  # cost a web reply 90s before the chain moved (ai.brgen.no, 2026-09-15).
  cooldown_tiers: [2, 5, 30]
  skip_ttl_ms: 600000
  # A timeout or a provider 5xx parks a model this long instead (ModelSkipCache).
  transient_skip_ttl_ms: 30000
  max_retries: 2

defaults: &model_defaults
  score: { quality: 0.0, speed: 0.0, cost: 0.0 }
  context_window: 128000

model_defs:
  agy_auto: &agy_auto
    id: agy:auto
    <<: *model_defaults
    context_window: 1000000
    score: { quality: 0.99, speed: 0.95, cost: 1.0 }
  agy_gemini_pro: &agy_gemini_pro
    id: agy:gemini-2.5-pro
    <<: *model_defaults
    context_window: 1000000
    score: { quality: 0.98, speed: 0.85, cost: 1.0 }
  agy_gemini_flash: &agy_gemini_flash
    id: agy:gemini-2.5-flash
    <<: *model_defaults
    context_window: 1000000
    score: { quality: 0.92, speed: 0.98, cost: 1.0 }
  agy_gemini_flash_thinking: &agy_gemini_flash_thinking
    id: agy:gemini-3.7-flash-thinking
    <<: *model_defaults
    context_window: 1000000
    score: { quality: 0.99, speed: 0.88, cost: 1.0 }
  gemini_flash: &gemini_flash
    id: gemini-2.5-flash
    <<: *model_defaults
    score: { quality: 0.88, speed: 0.90, cost: 0.95 }
  mistral_large: &mistral_large
    id: mistralai/mistral-large
    <<: *model_defaults
    score: { quality: 0.90, speed: 0.75, cost: 0.70 }
  mistral_small: &mistral_small
    id: mistralai/mistral-small-3.1-24b-instruct
    <<: *model_defaults
    score: { quality: 0.78, speed: 0.85, cost: 0.90 }
  deepseek_chat: &deepseek_chat
    id: deepseek-chat
    <<: *model_defaults
    context_window: 64000
    score: { quality: 0.96, speed: 0.85, cost: 0.95 }
  deepseek_reasoner: &deepseek_reasoner
    id: deepseek-reasoner
    <<: *model_defaults
    context_window: 64000
    score: { quality: 0.97, speed: 0.55, cost: 0.85 }
  deepseek_coder: &deepseek_coder
    id: deepseek-coder
    <<: *model_defaults
    context_window: 64000
    score: { quality: 0.85, speed: 0.70, cost: 0.95 }
  claude_sonnet: &claude_sonnet
    id: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4
    <<: *model_defaults
    context_window: 200000
    score: { quality: 0.95, speed: 0.75, cost: 0.60 }
  gemini_flash_openrouter: &gemini_flash_openrouter
    id: google/gemini-2.5-flash
    <<: *model_defaults
    score: { quality: 0.90, speed: 0.60, cost: 0.92 }
  nemotron_super: &nemotron_super
    id: nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free
    <<: *model_defaults
    score: { quality: 0.90, speed: 0.05, cost: 1.0 }
  gpt_4o: &gpt_4o
    id: openai/gpt-4o
    <<: *model_defaults
    score: { quality: 0.93, speed: 0.80, cost: 0.55 }
  claude_cli_sonnet: &claude_cli_sonnet
    id: claude-cli:claude-sonnet-5
    <<: *model_defaults
    context_window: 200000
    # 2026-09-16's "hangs from inside a session" finding does not reproduce
    # (verified 2026-09-23: direct arg, piped stdin, and a detached background
    # process all returned correctly). speed and cost were still scored for
    # that stale state — 0.70/0.60 assumed subprocess overhead and per-call
    # billing neither applies to a browser-authenticated subscription lane.
    # Re-measured: ~8s for a ~30KB prompt (comparable to gemini-2.5-flash's
    # observed per-call latency), and cost is 1.0 like claude_cli_opus below,
    # since there is no marginal charge per call.
    #
    # cost dropped 1.0 -> 0.3 on 2026-09-23 (operator: "my claude credits are
    # about to run out"). "No marginal API charge" is still true, but cost:
    # 1.0 conflated that with "unlimited," and a browser-subscription lane
    # draws on a real, currently-scarce quota this repo has no other way to
    # express in this scoring model. This is a statement about the account's
    # remaining headroom right now, not a correction to speed/quality --
    # raise it back to 1.0 once credits reset, or this quietly starves a
    # lane that is otherwise the strongest lane available.
    score: { quality: 0.95, speed: 0.85, cost: 0.3 }
  claude_cli_opus: &claude_cli_opus
    id: claude-cli:claude-opus-5-5
    <<: *model_defaults
    context_window: 200000
    # cost dropped 1.0 -> 0.3 on 2026-09-23, same reason and same reversal
    # condition as claude_cli_sonnet above -- one account, one quota.
    score: { quality: 0.99, speed: 0.55, cost: 0.3 }
  claude_opus_api: &claude_opus_api
    id: anthropic/claude-opus-4.1
    <<: *model_defaults
    context_window: 200000
    score: { quality: 0.99, speed: 0.50, cost: 0.20 }
  # codex-cli and grok-cli were already fully wired in cli_sender.rb (the
  # generic cli_lanes dispatch every claude-cli call already goes through) but
  # named in no tier, so the router could never select either -- 2026-09-24.
  #
  # grok-cli: verified directly, twice, with the exact `grok --single
  # "%{prompt}"` invocation this file's cli_lanes.grok-cli.ask declares --
  # ~27-29s for a trivial prompt, real replies both times. Scored like the
  # claude-cli lanes above: a subscription, not a metered API, so cost draws
  # on real but unmeasured headroom rather than 1.0's implied "free."
  grok_cli_auto: &grok_cli_auto
    id: grok-cli:auto
    <<: *model_defaults
    score: { quality: 0.90, speed: 0.50, cost: 0.3 }
  # codex-cli: NOT added below. `codex login status` succeeds instantly, but
  # `codex exec` -- the cli_lanes.codex-cli.ask invocation this file declares

  # separate attempts tonight: with and without --sandbox/--ephemeral, with

  # stripped (so it is not the claude-cli nested-session hang; something
  # about `codex exec` itself is currently broken on this account/version).
  # Wiring it in would just reproduce the 300s-per-call tax this same change
  # removed for claude-cli. Revisit once `codex exec` genuinely replies.
  gemma_2_27b: &gemma_2_27b
    id: google/gemma-2-27b-it
    <<: *model_defaults
    score: { quality: 0.82, speed: 0.78, cost: 0.92 }

operation_constraints:
  # Operations that write files, run autoloop/sweep, or execute destructive commands
  # require a model with quality score >= 0.88 (default and cheap tiers excluded).
  # Equivalent to: claude-sonnet-4, gemini-2.5-pro, mistral-large, gpt-4o.
  file_write:       { min_quality: 0.88, preferred_tier: strong }
  autoloop:         { min_quality: 0.88, preferred_tier: strong }
  sweep:            { min_quality: 0.88, preferred_tier: strong }
  council:          { min_quality: 0.88, preferred_tier: strong }
  scan_semantic:  { min_quality: 0.88, preferred_tier: strong }
  scan_adversarial: { min_quality: 0.88, preferred_tier: strong }
  detect_lexical: { min_quality: 0.70, preferred_tier: fast }
  code_generation: { min_quality: 0.80, preferred_tier: default }
  architecture:    { min_quality: 0.88, preferred_tier: strong }
  destructive:      { min_quality: 0.90, preferred_tier: strong }

continuity:
  enabled: true
  updated_at: "2026-05-01T00:00:00Z"

openrouter:
  # When true, the router merges live :free slugs from the SQLite provider catalog,
  # which the pool refreshes from OpenRouter when it is a day old (pool.rb).
  use_live_catalog: true
  # Per-model daily cap before router skips the slug (OpenRouter free tier ~200/day/key).
  daily_quota_per_model: 200
  # Multiple keys rotate LRU to spread free-tier rate limits (20 req/min, 200/day each).
  keys_env:
    - OPENROUTER_API_KEY
    - OPENROUTER_API_KEY_2
    - OPENROUTER_API_KEY_3
  free_latest:
    - nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free

# Keyless free fallback via headless Chrome (ferrum gem). Auto-activates when no API keys
# are configured; opt-in anytime with MASTER_WEB_CHAT=1 or MASTER_KEYLESS=1.
# Selectors are best-effort — sites change often. Login cookies persist in the profile dir.
# Models use the web-chat: prefix. ToS-sensitive: never default when paid keys exist.
ferrum_web_chat:
  enabled_when_env: MASTER_WEB_CHAT
  auto_when_keyless: true
  profile_dir: "~/.config/master/web-chat-profile"
  free_latest:
    - web-chat:grok
    - web-chat:chatgpt
    - web-chat:kimi
    - web-chat:gemini
  providers:
    grok:
      url: https://grok.com/
      input_selector: "textarea, div[contenteditable='true'], div[role='textbox']"
      reply_selector: "div[class*='message'], article, div.markdown"
      timeout: 120
    chatgpt:
      url: https://chatgpt.com/
      input_selector: "div#prompt-textarea, textarea#prompt-textarea, div[contenteditable='true']"
      reply_selector: "div[data-message-author-role='assistant']"
      timeout: 120
    kimi:
      url: https://kimi.com/
      input_selector: "textarea, div[contenteditable='true'], div[role='textbox']"
      reply_selector: "div.markdown-body, div[class*='assistant'], div[class*='message']"
      timeout: 120
    gemini:
      url: https://gemini.google.com/app
      input_selector: "div.ql-editor[contenteditable='true'], div[contenteditable='true']"
      reply_selector: "message-content, div[class*='response']"
      timeout: 120

three_mirror_redundancy:
  # Three models vote; ship only on >= 2 agreement for critical fixes.
  # Source: cross-cutting reunification (#95).
  enabled_for:   [tier1_critical, security_relevant, irreversible]
  pool:          ["anthropic/claude-sonnet-4", "ollama:gemma4:31b-cloud", "moonshotai/kimi-k2"]
  quorum:        2
  on_disagreement: "fall back to council vote with all dissent recorded"

# Subscription CLIs, signed in once through the browser. The pool offers a
# lane when its binary is installed and `signed_in` says so: the args are run
# once per process, and the lane counts as signed in when the output carries
# `match`, or lacks `refuse`. `ask` puts one question to it; %{reply_file}
# names a file the CLI writes its answer to, and a prompt with no %{prompt}
# goes in on stdin. A model named auto passes no model flag, so the CLI uses
# its own default. `login` is the command the pool names when signed out.
cli_lanes:
  codex-cli:
    binary: codex
    signed_in: { args: [login, status], match: Logged in }
    ask: [exec, --skip-git-repo-check, --sandbox, read-only, --ephemeral, --output-last-message, "%{reply_file}", "-"]
    model_flag: --model
    models: [auto]
    login: codex login
  grok-cli:
    binary: grok
    signed_in: { args: [models], refuse: not authenticated }
    ask: [--single, "%{prompt}"]
    model_flag: --model
    models: [auto]
    login: grok login

# OpenAI-compatible servers on this machine. A server that answers /models
# puts each model it lists in the pool as local:<id>. mistral.rs
# (`mistralrs serve`) and LM Studio listen on 1234, llama.cpp's llama-server
# on 8080.
local_servers:
  - http://localhost:1234/v1
  - http://localhost:8080/v1

# Hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints with a free tier (ModelRouter::
# HostedEndpoints). Each lists its models at <base>/models, and they join the
# free lane of every chain as <name>:<model>. key_env is where a key may be set;
# with none set, only the models whose listing matches `keyless` are offered.
# LLM7 serves its turbo tier without a key except the usage-based models,
# measured 2026-09-24: GLM-5.3-Flash, codestral-latest, minimax-m2.7 and
# mistral-Nemo-Instruct-2407 answered; every other chat model returned 401.
# Groq, Cerebras and NVIDIA NIM carry larger free quotas behind a free signup
# key (limits as awesome-freellm-apis lists them, 2026-09); with no keyless
# rule they are not asked until their key is set in ~/.config/master/env.
openai_compatible:
  llm7:
    base: https://api.llm7.io/v1
    key_env: [LLM7_API_KEY]
    keyless:
      tier: turbo
      usage_based_only: false
  # 30 requests/min, 14,400/day.
  groq:
    base: https://api.groq.com/openai/v1
    key_env: [GROQ_API_KEY]
  # 10 requests/min, 100/day, 1M tokens/day.
  cerebras:
    base: https://api.cerebras.ai/v1
    key_env: [CEREBRAS_API_KEY]
  # Up to 40 requests/min, including GLM-5.3 Flash.
  nvidia:
    base: https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1
    key_env: [NVIDIA_API_KEY]

# Language models Replicate hosts, asked as replicate:<owner>/<name> with
# REPLICATE_API_TOKEN. Paid per call, so they sit behind the free lanes.
replicate_chat:
  - anthropic/claude-4.5-sonnet
  - openai/gpt-5
  - deepseek-ai/deepseek-v3.1
  - google/gemini-2.5-flash
  - moonshotai/kimi-k2.5

# Tier-D (Ollama). Ollama is probed at localhost by default; every pulled model
# that fits in memory joins the pool dynamically. Cloud models come from the
# explicit cloud_models catalogue and therefore do not need to appear in
# /api/tags. OLLAMA_BASE_URL names another daemon. MASTER_NO_OLLAMA disables
# the lane. The sender speaks Ollama's own /api/chat at the host root, so a
# /v1 suffix here is read past.
# keep_alive holds a model in memory between the turns of one fold instead of
# reloading it for each; max_num_ctx caps the window the sender sizes to each
# request (ollama_sender.rb).
ollama:
  # Ollama is a first-class local provider. It probes localhost by default;
  # MASTER_NO_OLLAMA=1 disables the lane. OLLAMA_BASE_URL can point at another
  # Ollama daemon. Installed local models are discovered dynamically, so this
  # list is a curated fast path rather than a closed catalogue.
  default_base_url: "http://localhost:11434"
  keep_alive: 30m
  max_num_ctx: 16384
  cloud_models:
    - ollama:glm-5.3-flash:cloud
    - ollama:glm-5.3:cloud
    - ollama:glm-5.2:cloud
    - ollama:glm-5.1:cloud
    - ollama:deepseek-v4.1-flash:cloud
    - ollama:deepseek-v4-flash:cloud
    - ollama:deepseek-v4-pro:cloud
    - ollama:kimi-k3:cloud
    - ollama:kimi-k2.7-code:cloud
    - ollama:kimi-k2.6:cloud
    - ollama:minimax-m3:cloud
    - ollama:minimax-m2.7:cloud
    - ollama:gemma4:cloud
    - ollama:qwen3.5:cloud
    - ollama:nemotron-3-ultra:cloud
    - ollama:nemotron-3-super:cloud
    - ollama:nemotron-3-nano:cloud
    - ollama:mistral-large-3:cloud
    - ollama:gpt-oss:cloud

# media_providers was deleted here on 2026-08-21: nothing read it. The env
# vars live in providers.yml replicate.env (ReplicateClient reads ENV
# directly), the TTS slug in voice/engines.rb, and replicate carries its own
# image models in MASTER/tools/replicate — this block was a declaration with no reader,
# claiming a routing that never existed.

`````

### data/openbsd.yml

`````yaml
# openbsd.yml — baseline expectations for OpenBSD daemon configs. Revalidate
# release-specific details against the deployed system's man pages. Ground::OpenbsdConfig
# reads it, and test_openbsd_config.rb holds every known config under OPENBSD/etc to it.

configs:
  pf.conf:
    daemon: pf
    man: pf.conf.5
    required_patterns:
      - "set skip on lo"
    warnings:
      - pattern: "pass all"
        message: "Overly permissive — add interface/protocol guards"

  nsd.conf:
    daemon: nsd
    man: nsd.conf.5
    required_patterns:
      - "server:"
      - "zone:"
    warnings:
      - pattern: "rrl-size"
        absent_message: "Missing RRL config — vulnerable to amplification DDoS"
      - pattern: "hide-version"
        absent_message: "Consider hide-version: yes"

  httpd.conf:
    daemon: httpd
    man: httpd.conf.5
    required_patterns:
      - "server"

  smtpd.conf:
    daemon: smtpd
    man: smtpd.conf.5
    required_patterns:
      - "listen on"
      - "action"
      - "match"
    warnings:
      - pattern: "match from any"
        message: "Open relay risk — restrict to authenticated senders"

  relayd.conf:
    daemon: relayd
    man: relayd.conf.5
    required_patterns:
      - "relay"

  acme-client.conf:
    daemon: acme-client
    man: acme-client.conf.5
    required_patterns:
      - "authority"
      - "domain"

  doas.conf:
    daemon: doas
    man: doas.conf.5
    required_patterns:
      - "permit"
    warnings:
      - pattern: "nopass"
        message: "Allows passwordless privilege escalation"

  sshd_config:
    daemon: sshd
    man: sshd_config.5
    warnings:
      - pattern: "PermitRootLogin yes"
        message: "Security risk — use PermitRootLogin prohibit-password"
      - pattern: "PasswordAuthentication yes"
        message: "Consider key-only auth"

  ntpd.conf:
    daemon: ntpd
    man: ntpd.conf.5
    required_patterns:
      - "server"

  unbound.conf:
    daemon: unbound
    man: unbound.conf.5
    required_patterns:
      - "server:"

`````

`````yaml
# Platform/tool idioms — gh, zsh — and intent/research namespaces
# merged from former *_patterns.yml + repo_topic_clusters + prompt_archaeology.
# Each top-level key is a namespace.
---
schema: 1
infer:
  commands:
    sweep:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:sweep|refactor|clean\\s*up|rewrite|polish|tidy\\s*up|overhaul|improve\\s+(?:all|every)|go\\s+through\\s+(?:all|every)|full\\s+pass\\s+(?:over|on))(?:\\s+(?:all|every(?:thing)?|the))?(?:\\s+([\\w\\/.]+))?"
      - "\\b(?:rydd\\s+opp|refaktorer|forbedre?|gjennomg[åa]|omskriv)(?:\\s+([\\w\\/.]+))?"
      capture: path
    autoloop:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:autoloop|autofix|fix\\s+all\\s+violations?|keep\\s+(?:fix|loop)|loop\\s+until|iterate\\s+until|run\\s+until\\s+clean|keep\\s+going\\s+until|(?:run|go)\\s+(?:it\\s+)?(?:again\\s+)?until\\s+(?:done|clean|fixed|perfect))(?:\\s+(\\d+))?"
      - "\\b(?:fiks?\\s+alle?\\s+(?:feil|brudd)|fortsett\\s+(?:til|inntil)|kj[øo]r\\s+(?:til\\s+)?(?:det\\s+er\\s+)?(?:rent|bra|ferdig))(?:\\s+(\\d+))?"
      capture: cycles
    council:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:(?:run|start|get|convene|use|activate|invoke)\\s+(?:the\\s+)?council|council\\s+(?:review|deliberation|this|on\\s+this)|deliberate\\s+(?:on\\s+)?this|multiple\\s+perspect|second\\s+opinion|peer\\s+review|debate\\s+this|get\\s+(?:another|a\\s+second)\\s+view|multi(?:ple)?\\s+(?:view|agent|model|perspect))\\b"
      - "\\b(?:r[åa]dsl[åa]g|bruk\\s+(?:flere|multiple)\\s+(?:perspektiv|synsvinkler?)|diskuter\\s+(?:dette|det))\\b"
      capture: on_off
    explain:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:explain\\s+(?:your(?:self)?|your\\s+architecture|how\\s+you\\s+work)|describe\\s+(?:your(?:self)?|your\\s+architecture)|what\\s+are\\s+you|how\\s+(?:are\\s+you\\s+built|do\\s+you\\s+work)|show\\s+(?:your\\s+)?architecture|self[\\s-]?map)\\b"
      capture: none
    persona:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:(?:switch|change|set)\\s+persona\\s+(?:to\\s+)?(\\w+)|use\\s+(\\w+)\\s+persona)\\b"
      capture: persona_name
    memory:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:what\\s+do\\s+you\\s+remember(?:\\s+about\\s+([\\w\\s]+))?|show\\s+(?:my\\s+)?memor(?:y|ies)|list\\s+memor(?:y|ies)|recall(?:\\s+([\\w]+))?|what(?:'s|\\s+is)\\s+in\\s+(?:your\\s+)?memory|remember\\s+([\\w]+=.+)|forget\\s+([\\w_]+))\\b"
      - "\\b(?:hva\\s+husker\\s+du(?:\\s+om\\s+([\\w\\s]+))?|vis\\s+(?:min\\s+)?hukommelse|husk\\s+([\\w_]+=.+))\\b"
      capture: first_group
    tokens:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:token\\s*count|how\\s+many\\s+tokens?|context\\s+size|token\\s+usage|how\\s+much\\s+context|hvor\\s+mange\\s+token|token\\s*antall)\\b"
      capture: none
    cost:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:how\\s+much\\s+(?:has\\s+this\\s+cost|did\\s+this\\s+cost)|(?:current\\s+)?(?:spend|cost|budget)|what(?:'s|\\s+is)\\s+the\\s+cost|hva\\s+koster?\\s+(?:dette|det)|kostnader?)\\b"
      capture: none
    undo:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:undo\\s+that|revert\\s+(?:that|last|it)|go\\s+back|take\\s+that\\s+back|angre\\s+det|g[åa]\\s+tilbake)\\b"
      capture: none
    clear:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:clear\\s+(?:context|chat|history|session|screen)|start\\s+(?:over|fresh|again)|reset\\s+(?:context|session)|fresh\\s+start|t[øo]m\\s+(?:kontekst|historikk)|begynn\\s+p[åa]\\s+nytt)\\b"
      capture: none
    save:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:save\\s+(?:session|this|my\\s+work|progress)|checkpoint\\s+now|lagre\\s+(?:session|sesjonen?|arbeid))\\b"
      capture: none
    model:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:which\\s+model|current\\s+model|what\\s+model\\s+are\\s+you|what\\s+(?:llm|ai|model)\\s+(?:are\\s+you\\s+using|is\\s+this))\\b"
      capture: none
    scan:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:scan|lint|check\\s+(?:code|violations?)|run\\s+scan)(?:\\s+(cosmetic|style|hygiene|perfection|core|axioms|solid|critical|full|aesthetic|pixel|ui|ux|design))?\\b"
      - "\\b(?:review\\s+my\\s+changes?|check\\s+what\\s+I\\s+edited|what\\s+did\\s+I\\s+change|scan\\s+my\\s+edits?)\\b"
      capture: scan_profile
    fix:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:fix|repair|correct)\\s+(?:the\\s+)?([\\w./-]+(?:\\.[\\w]+)?)?"
      - "\\b(?:fiks|reparer)\\s+(?:([\\w./-]+(?:\\.[\\w]+)?)|(?:den|det))?\\b"
      capture: path
    through:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:run|put|send|take|feed)\\s+(?:this|it|that|master|rails|the\\s+code(?:base)?)?\\s*through\\s+(?:master|itself|singularity)?\\b"
      - "\\bthrough\\s+(master|itself|rails|face|self)(?:[:/]([\\w./-]+))?\\b"
      - "\\b(?:full\\s+)?(?:pass|tribunal|singularity)\\b(?:\\s+(?:on|over)\\s+)?([\\w./-]+)?"
      - "\\bfix\\s+(?:and\\s+)?review\\s+([\\w./-]+)"
      - "\\b(?:improve|clean\\s*up|polish|converge)\\s+(?:all\\s+of\\s+)?(rails|master|itself|self|face|web|the\\s+codebase)(?:[:/]([\\w./-]+))?\\b"
      - "\\b(?:run\\s+)?(?:master|rails)\\s+through\\s+(?:it\\s*)?self\\b"
      - "\\bself[\\s-]?apply\\b(?:\\s+(?:on|to)\\s+([\\w./-]+))?"
      - "\\bkj[øo]r\\s+(?:dette\\s+)?gjennom\\s+master\\b"
      capture: path
    workflow:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:run|put|send|take)\\s+(?:this|it|that)?\\s*through\\s+master\\b"
      - "\\b(?:full\\s+)?(?:pass|tribunal)\\b(?:\\s+(?:on|over)\\s+)?([\\w./-]+)?"
      - "\\bfix\\s+(?:and\\s+)?review\\s+([\\w./-]+)"
      capture: path
    dmesg:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:show\\s+(?:logs?|events?)|system\\s+log|dmesg|what\\s+(?:happened|has\\s+happened)|recent\\s+activity)\\b"
      capture: none
    music:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:play|start|put on|spin|queue)\\s+(?:some\\s+)?(?:j\\s*)?dilla(?:\\s+beats?)?\\b"
      - "\\b(?:j\\s*dilla|dilla\\s+beats?|donuts|mpc\\s*3000)\\b"
      - "\\b(?:play|open|start)\\s+(?:radio\\s+bergen|warp\\s+tunnel)\\b"
      - "\\b(?:radio\\s+bergen|flying\\s+lotus|madlib)\\b"
      capture: music_sub
    prompt:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:write|expand|embellish|polish)\\s+(?:me\\s+)?(?:a\\s+)?(?:(?:photo|video|image)\\s+)?prompt\\s+(?:for\\s+)?(.+)"
      - "\\b(?:strunk|elements of style)\\s+(?:pass\\s+)?(?:on\\s+)?(?:(?:photo|video)\\s+)?(?:prompt\\s+)?(.+)"
      capture: first_group
    photograph:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:take|shoot|snap|generate)\\s+(?:a\\s+)?(?:photo|photograph|portrait|headshot)(?:\\s+(?:of\\s+)?(.+))?"
      - "\\b(?:cinematic\\s+)?photo(?:graph)?\\s+(?:of\\s+)?(.+)"
      capture: first_group
    video:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:generate|make|create|render)\\s+(?:a\\s+)?(?:cinematic\\s+|long[\\s-]?form\\s+)?video(?:\\s+(?:of|about|for)\\s+(.+))?"
      - "\\b(?:video\\s+chain|stitch\\s+(?:a\\s+)?video)(?:\\s+(.+))?"
      - "\\b(?:minutes?|min)\\s+(?:of\\s+)?video(?:\\s+(?:of|about)\\s+(.+))?"
      capture: first_group
    motion-dataset:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:bootstrap|build|prepare)\\s+(?:a\\s+)?motion[\\s-]?lora\\s+dataset(?:\\s+(?:for\\s+)?(.+))?"
      - "\\b(?:train(?:ing)?\\s+clips?\\s+for)\\s+(?:motion\\s+)?lora(?:\\s+(.+))?"
      capture: first_group
    lora-train:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:train|create|build)\\s+(?:a\\s+)?(?:character\\s+)?(?:flux\\s+)?lora(?:\\s+(?:of|for)\\s+(.+))?"
      - "\\b(?:lora[\\s-]?train(?:ing)?)\\s+(?:on\\s+)?(.+)"

    social-sim:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:social[\\s-]?sim|inbox[\\s-]?sim|synthetic[\\s-]?inbox)\\b(?:\\s+(.+))?"
      - "\\b(?:run|start)\\s+(?:a\\s+)?social[\\s-]?sim(?:ulation)?(?:\\s+(.+))?"

    dreams:

      - "\\b(?:dreams?|consolidate?\\s+memor(?:y|ies)|memory\\s+consolidat|dream\\s+mode|promote\\s+memor(?:y|ies))\\b"

    soul:
      patterns:

      capture: soul_subcmd
    orders:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:standing\\s+orders?|show\\s+orders?|list\\s+orders?)\\b"

    history:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:show|print|list)\\s+(?:undo\\s+)?histor(?:y|ies)\\b"
      - "\\bwhat\\s+(?:did\\s+(?:i|we)\\s+do|have\\s+(?:i|we)\\s+done|was\\s+(?:changed|done))\\b"
      capture: none
    why:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:which|current|show)\\s+model\\s+(?:routing|selection|why)\\b"
      - "\\bwhy\\s+(?:this|that)\\s+model\\b"
      - "\\bmodel\\s+scoring\\b"
      capture: none
    principles:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:show|list|what\\s+are)\\s+(?:the\\s+)?(?:my\\s+)?principles\\b"
      - "\\bconstitution(?:al)?\\s+(?:rules?|principles?|axioms?)\\b"
      capture: none
    propose:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:what(?:'s|\\s+is)\\s+(?:next|suggested)|suggest(?:ed)?\\s+(?:action|step)s?|next\\s+steps?|what\\s+should\\s+(?:i|we)\\s+do)\\b"
      capture: none
    context:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:show|what(?:'s|\\s+is)\\s+in)\\s+(?:the\\s+)?(?:context|attention)\\s+(?:window|state)?\\b"
      - "\\bcontext\\s+window\\b"
      capture: none
    verify:
      patterns:
      - "\\b(?:verifie?d?|confirm|check)\\s+(?:everything\\s+(?:is\\s+)?(?:wired|connected|working)|(?:all\\s+)?symbols?)\\b"

    restart:
      patterns:

  negative:
  - pattern: "\\bexplain\\s+(?:the\\s+)?(?:bug|error|issue|failure|stack\\s*trace)\\b"
    blocks: [explain]
  - pattern: "\\bscan\\s+(?:my\\s+)?(?:inbox|email|calendar)\\b"

  destructive: [clear, rebuild, resync, shell, rollback]
`````
