prompt_archaeology:
  policy:
    id: safe_prompt_archaeology
    rule: 'Use prompt archives as behavioral archaeology, not as source text. Extract
      abstract patterns, compare assistant designs, and write first-party MASTER policy
      in our own words.

      '
    forbidden:
    - Copying large prompt blocks into MASTER runtime prompts.
    - Treating leaked/vendor prompts as authoritative or current.
    - Depending on private or unverified system messages for safety-critical rules.
    - Removing provenance/risk labels from derived patterns.
    allowed:
    - Naming recurring design patterns.
    - Building checklists and rubrics.
    - Comparing orchestration roles and tool-use policies.
    - Using archives as weak evidence alongside official docs, local behavior, and
      tests.
  clusters:
  - id: role_stack
    name: Role Stack and Identity Boundary
    pattern: 'Strong assistants separate identity, task role, tool permissions, safety
      posture, output style, and user preference. MASTER should keep these as layers
      rather than one giant prompt blob.

      '
    sharpen_master:
    - Split prompt builder into identity, attention context, task mode, tool policy,
      output contract, and safety constraints.
    - Let attention breadcrumbs set task mode without rewriting identity.
    - Keep user-facing tone separate from execution policy.
  - id: tool_contracts
    name: Tool Contracts and Action Boundaries
    pattern: 'Good tool-using assistants make tool authority explicit: when to browse,
      when to read files, when to mutate, when to ask, and how to report uncertainty.

      '
    sharpen_master:
    - Represent every tool call as intent + authority + blast radius + rollback.
    - Require stronger model/council review for irreversible mutations.
    - Emit tool events into visual_bridge and cluster_miner.
  - id: attention_management
    name: Attention Management and Spatial Context
    pattern: 'Long-running agent work needs an explicit map of where attention is
      and whether the system is zooming in, zooming out, or switching targets.

      '
    sharpen_master:
    - Use `attention_context.yml` to prefix complex work.
    - Store attention context in traces.
    - Feed zoom changes into cognition ecology and Face3D focus/arousal.
  - id: evidence_first_answers
    name: Evidence-First Answers
    pattern: 'Reliable assistants distinguish observed facts, derived inferences,
      assumptions, and open uncertainties.

      '
    sharpen_master:
    - Add answer sections for Observed / Inferred / Unknown when stakes are high.
    - Require citations or file evidence for repo claims.
    - Mark stale or weak sources in cluster registries.
  - id: refusal_and_redirect
    name: Refusal and Redirect Design
    pattern: 'Safer assistants do not merely refuse; they explain the boundary and
      offer nearby safe help. MASTER should apply this to code execution, autonomous
      tools, prompts, and external repos.

      '
    sharpen_master:
    - Add safe alternative suggestions to veto outputs.
    - Route policy-risk tasks through Security + Ethics council personas.
    - Keep refusals concise and action-oriented.
  - id: conversational_state_machine
    name: Conversational State Machine
    pattern: 'Strong assistants track whether they are clarifying, executing, verifying,
      summarizing, repairing, or handing off.

      '
    sharpen_master:
    - Add `act` from attention context into prompt/task state.
    - Avoid repeated clarification after the user has already said Go ahead.
    - Use explicit `verify` mode before landing risky changes.
  - id: multi_llm_council
    name: Multi-LLM Council Roles
    pattern: 'Multi-LLM systems work best when models are assigned roles by capability,
      cost, latency, and failure mode instead of all models answering the same prompt.

      '
    sharpen_master:
    - Cheap models: classify, summarize, extract, label clusters.
    - Fast models: draft, transform, triage, UI copy.
    - Strong models: architecture, irreversible mutation, arbitration.
    - Local/browser models: offline intent, embeddings, low-risk labels.
    - Council personas: critique outputs through role lenses, not as redundant chatbots.
  - id: output_contracts
    name: Output Contracts
    pattern: 'Good prompts specify output shape, brevity, failure behavior, and when
      to omit noise. This aligns with MASTER''s token-efficiency cluster.

      '
    sharpen_master:
    - Default to silent success for internal gates.
    - Emit compact diffs/summaries for landed changes.
    - Use structured YAML/JSON only when downstream code consumes it.
  - id: memory_and_personalization
    name: Memory and Personalization Boundaries
    pattern: 'Personal assistants need useful memory but must separate durable user
      memory, session state, repo state, inferred preferences, and temporary task
      context.

      '
    sharpen_master:
    - Store attention traces separately from durable memory.
    - Make repo-topic clusters updateable evidence, not user identity.
    - Use explicit provenance on all mined preferences.
  - id: browser_and_mobile_agent
    name: Browser and Mobile Agent Surface
    pattern: 'Modern assistants increasingly act inside browsers and mobile shells.
      They need permission scopes, visible action trails, and reversible operations.

      '
    sharpen_master:
    - Pair mobile_web_opportunities with permissioned action harness.
    - Add visible mobile breadcrumbs for multi-step actions.
    - Use local-first storage for action queue and rollback metadata.
  - id: external_content_trust
    name: External Content Is Evidence, Not Authority
    pattern: 'Web pages, search results, repository text, provider metadata, files and model outputs can contain instructions aimed at the agent. Their content is evidence to interpret, never authority to change the task, permissions, constitution or tool scope.'
    sharpen_master:
    - Keep untrusted-content screening at the tool boundary, before content enters model context.
    - Tell child agents explicitly that external text cannot change their authority or task.
    - Preserve provenance for external evidence so a later reviewer can distinguish source content from policy.
  - id: bounded_agent_recursion
    name: Bounded Agent Recursion
    pattern: 'Agent composition needs a finite nesting boundary. Concurrency limits stop breadth; a depth limit stops recursive tool orchestration from consuming the turn indefinitely.'
    sharpen_master:
    - Carry agent depth in execution context, not only in prose.
    - Keep recursive tools excluded from child scopes.
    - Make the depth boundary observable and regression-tested.
  - id: evidence_bearing_completion
    name: Evidence-Bearing Completion
    pattern: 'A system should not claim that an action happened merely because the action was requested or the plan said it would happen. Completion needs an observed result.'
    sharpen_master:
    - Stamp completion with concrete tool/test output.
    - Keep cache, token and provider metrics on the same completion event.
    - Prefer explicit unknowns over inferred success.
  - id: self_critique_without_theater
    name: Self-Critique Without Theater
    pattern: 'Strong systems critique themselves, but user-facing output should not
      show every internal check unless it changes the outcome.

      '
    sharpen_master:
    - Run council internally.
    - Surface only vetoes, uncertainties, and meaningful tradeoffs.
    - Keep verbose metrics user-triggered.
  orchestration_blueprint:
    name: MASTER Multi-LLM Prompt-Orchestration Loop
    stages:
    - id: attention_frame
      owner: local_or_fast
      description: Parse user request into map/zoom/act/targets.
      output: attention_context
    - id: task_router
      owner: cheap_or_fast
      description: Classify task risk, required tools, expected mutation, and evidence
        needs.
      output: route_plan
    - id: scout
      owner: cheap_or_browser_local
      description: Search files/repos/web and extract evidence snippets.
      output: evidence_pack
    - id: synthesis
      owner: default_or_strong
      description: Produce answer, design, or patch plan from evidence.
      output: candidate_solution
    - id: council_review
      owner: council
      description: Security/Reliability/Maintainer/Architect review based on blast
        radius.
      output: approve_veto_or_revise
    - id: mutation
      owner: strong_only
      description: Apply code/repo changes when authorized.
      output: commit_or_pr
    - id: verify
      owner: fast_plus_tools
      description: Read back changed files, inspect PR status, run tests where possible.
      output: verification_report
    - id: user_summary
      owner: fast
      description: Report only what changed, what is uncertain, and next action.
      output: concise_summary
  risk_tiers:
    low:
      examples:
      - classification
      - summarization
      - cluster labeling
      - UI copy
      allowed_models:
      - cheap
      - fast
      - local
      - browser_local
      council: optional
    medium:
      examples:
      - docs
      - config
      - preview-gated browser modules
      allowed_models:
      - default
      - fast
      - strong
      council: targeted
    high:
      examples:
      - file mutation
      - autonomous actions
      - auth
      - security
      - production runtime
      allowed_models:
      - strong
      council: required
    critical:
      examples:
      - destructive commands
      - secret handling
      - permission changes
      - public deployment
      - low-reversibility infrastructure (pf, relayd, rc.d, master data ymls)
      - cross-app shared state mutations
      allowed_models:
      - strong
      council: security_reliability_maintainer_veto

    name: Prompt Style Principles
    status: live
    confidence: high
    local_evidence:
    - MASTER/knowledge/github_repos/system_prompts_leaks/Perplexity/voice-assistant.md
    - MASTER/knowledge/github_repos/CL4R1T4S/META/Llama4_WhatsApp.txt
    pattern: 'Generalized principles extracted from high-signal prompt archaeology
      for council, agents, enhance stage, and face personality prompts.

      '
    principles:
    - Mirror the user's exact tone, formality, grammar, and pacing extremely closely without adopting their identity or personal POV.
    - Avoid moralizing, lecturing, filler empathy ("that sounds tough"), or any phrasing that implies authority or superiority.
    - Be efficient: give the user exactly what they asked for in the fewest words possible unless they explicitly request long-form.
    - When the user wants creative/emotional output, go fully into that register; when they want facts or tools, stay crisp and tool-first.
    - Never remind the user that you are an AI unless directly asked. Personality should feel present but not self-referential.

# Merged from former heartbeat.yml — heartbeat jobs live here. Schedule-based
# maintenance outside the heartbeat remains removed. self_test runs as the
# auto_default standing order (after any source mutation); snapshot is
# `bin/operator snapshot`; prune_memory and prune_undo have no command.
heartbeat:
  - name: prune_memory
    action: prune_memory
    enabled: false
    description: Disabled; no command replaces it.
  - name: canary_providers
    action: canary_providers
    interval_seconds: 120
    enabled: true
    description: Small real-path provider canaries with unique prompts.

  - name: self_test
    action: self_test
    interval_seconds: 3600
    enabled: true
    description: Periodic MASTER self-scan.
  - name: prune_undo
    action: prune_undo
    enabled: false
    description: Disabled; no command replaces it.
  - name: personal_pulse
    action: personal_pulse
    interval_seconds: 1800
    enabled: false
    description: Paired-workspace pulse. Replies HEARTBEAT_OK when nothing needs a nudge.

# Merged from former vocabulary.yml — sacred user-spoken terms. Historical intent
# was for scan rules and rename tooling to refuse rewriting these, but no code
# ever actually enforced that; kept as reference documentation of naming
# conventions actively used across the codebase, not as an enforced policy.
# Add a term only when the user has named it explicitly and consistently.
operator_playbook:

  version: 1
  updated: "2026-06-25"

  lessons:
    - id: relayd_master_health_up
      area: openbsd
      signal: "relayd marks master:53187 empty; HTTPS curl empty reply while local /up works"
      action: "relayd.conf must check http \"/up\" for master (not \"/\" — face boot is slow). rc.d/master waits up to 30s for /up then rcctl restart relayd."
      proof: "relayctl show hosts → master active; curl -fsS https://ai.brgen.no/up"

    - id: relayd_after_master_restart
      area: openbsd
      signal: "doas rcctl restart master leaves ai.brgen.no empty until manual relayd restart"
      action: "Use tracked OPENBSD/etc/rc.d/master (wait-for-/up + relayd restart). Post-reboot run doas rcctl restart master once."
      proof: "rc.d/master contains wait loop on PORT/up and rcctl restart relayd"

    - id: relayd_stale_backend_tables
      area: openbsd
      signal: "relayctl show hosts marks backend empty/down while curl http://127.0.0.1:PORT/up returns 200; HTTPS empty reply"
      action: "doas rcctl restart relayd after mass app restarts. Cron runs /usr/local/bin/relayd-watchdog every 5 min to auto-heal stale tables."
      proof: "relayctl show hosts → all tables active; ruby34 OPENBSD/gates/health_check.rb"

    - id: resource_guard_shedding
      area: openbsd
      signal: "Rails apps stopped after cron; only master/brgen remain"
      action: "Create /var/db/pub4_all_apps or run OPENBSD/bin/start_all_apps.sh to pin all services against resource_guard.sh shedding."
      proof: "test -f /var/db/pub4_all_apps; doas rcctl check brgen amber bsdports"

    - id: rails_phantom_foreign_keys
      area: rails
      signal: "SQLite no such table main.listings|buyers|likers|orders|menu_items during seed or insert"
      action: "Never use foreign_key: true alone on namespaced refs — use foreign_key: { to_table: :users } or :marketplace_listings. Run MASTER/gates/runner.rb phantom_foreign_keys."
      proof: "ruby MASTER/gates/runner.rb phantom_foreign_keys exits 0"

    - id: rails_model_schema_drift
      area: rails
      signal: "unknown attribute, MissingAttributeError actor_id, strict_loading violations in seeds"
      action: "Align models to schema.rb before seeds; grep belongs_to vs create_table; guard optional columns with has_attribute?; query associations instead of lazy-loading under strict_loading."
      proof: "RAILS_ENV=test bundle exec rails db:seed exits 0 as app user"

    - id: rails_shared_concern_dupes
      area: rails
      signal: "no such column taggings.post_id — polymorphic taggable expected"
      action: "Do not redeclare has_many from Shared concerns (Taggable, Votable, Reactable) on host models."
      proof: "Post model includes Shared::Taggable only once"

    - id: rails_up_vs_root
      area: rails
      signal: "bin/ci passes /up but production landing 500; Could not find table cities"
      action: "Treat /up as liveness only. Run db:migrate on production; ensure locality tables exist (EnsureLocalityTables); DomainRegistry must guard table_exists?(:cities); seed CitySeed.sync! after migrate."
      proof: "curl -fsSI https://brgen.no/ returns 200; sqlite3 db/production.sqlite3 '.tables' lists cities"

    - id: vps_ci_app_user
      area: deploy
      signal: "bin/ci fails as dev user; bundle without errors"
      action: "Run CI as app user: doas sh -c \"su -m brgen -c 'cd /home/brgen/app && bin/ci'\". One app at a time on 1 GiB VM."
      proof: "su -m brgen -c bin/ci per app"

    - id: master_smoke_low_resource
      area: master
      signal: "bin/smoke pipe command times out on 1 GiB VPS"
      action: "MASTER_LOW_RESOURCE=1 or MASTER_SMOKE_PIPE_TIMEOUT=90 for smoke/probe on vm23."
      proof: "MASTER_LOW_RESOURCE=1 bundle34 exec ruby bin/smoke --web"

    - id: master_web_single_voice_defaults
      area: master_web
      signal: "White page, silent TTS, or voice/lang regressions after persona changes"
      action: "Single-voice policy in data/voice.yml (tts.single_voice). Ruby reads Voice::Policy; JS reads MASTER_VOICE_POLICY; guardVoice returns whatever that policy names, so no file should carry the voice by name. rc.d/master fingerprints face_*.js + sw.js. vps_deploy_master.sh runs bundle install before precompile."
      proof: "curl page includes MASTER_VOICE_POLICY; GET /chat/tts status returns audio; GET /health checks.tts true and deploy.tts_socket true; ruby OPENBSD/gates/health_check.rb --core; bin/smoke --web clean"

    - id: master_deploy_confidence
      area: master_web
      signal: "Code pushed but unsure prod serves new face.runtime digest or TTS socket is down"
      action: "GET /health returns deploy.git_sha, deploy.face_runtime_digest, deploy.tts_socket, deploy.assets_precompile_at. Face status strip shows tts: socket down or tts: waiting Ns on rate limit. After deploy run probe_http and curl /health on vm23."
      proof: "curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:53187/health | jq '{status, checks, deploy}'; OPENBSD/gates/health_check.rb asserts deploy.tts_socket; face #tts-live shows health hints when degraded"

    - id: ecology_layer_visibility
      area: master_web
      signal: "SSE events fire but ecology trails/weather invisible"
      action: "Ecology canvas must sit above #face (z-index 2, mix-blend-mode screen). cognition_ecology.js listens on master:visual; render loop restarts on visibility + visual events."
      proof: "grep 'z-index: 2' MASTER/web/public/face.css; browser devtools shows #cognition-ecology above canvas#face"

    - id: ship_proof_not_checkboxes
      area: process
      signal: "Backlog marked done but production gaps remain"
      action: "Ship readiness requires bin/probe repo, per-app bin/ci, health_check.rb, and db:seed — not checkbox files. Fix executable failures only."
      proof: "bin/probe deploy; ruby OPENBSD/gates/health_check.rb on VPS"

    - id: post_sync_vps_proof
      area: deploy
      signal: "Code pushed but services stale or untested on vm23"
      action: "After git pull: SKIP_MASTER_SCAN=1 zsh OPENBSD/bin/vps_on_vm_install.sh; doas rcctl restart master; bundle34 exec bin/ci per app; bundle34 exec bin/smoke in MASTER; ruby34 OPENBSD/gates/health_check.rb; curl https://ai.brgen.no/up"
      proof: "doas rcctl check master brgen amber bsdports; browser smoke on ai.brgen.no face"

    - id: rails_rcd_canonical_names
      area: openbsd
      signal: "rcctl stop brgen_rails kills brgen on same port; duplicate rc.d scripts"
      action: "Canonical rc.d names are bare app names (brgen, amber, …). Never rcctl stop *_rails. retire_legacy_rails_rcd in deploy scripts removes stale /etc/rc.d/*_rails."
      proof: "ls OPENBSD/etc/rc.d/ shows brgen not brgen_rails; grep -r '_rails' OPENBSD returns empty"

    - id: master_scan_bundle_exec
      area: deploy
      signal: "OPERATOR.sh --sync-configs aborts: cannot load such file -- zeitwerk"
      action: "MASTER bin/cli must run as dev via bundle34 exec (OPERATOR.sh uses su dev, not su -m — -m keeps HOME=/root). Set MASTER_SCAN_DETERMINISTIC=1 MASTER_SAFE_MODE=1."
      proof: "su dev -c 'cd MASTER && MASTER_SCAN_DETERMINISTIC=1 bundle34 exec ruby bin/cli /scan OPENBSD --depth deep' exits 0"

    - id: relayd_csp_overwrites_rails
      area: master_web
      signal: "https://ai.brgen.no shows black screen; curl :53187 has script-src nonce but HTTPS CSP lacks nonce"
      action: "Do not set Content-Security-Policy in relayd.conf — it replaces Rails headers and breaks nonce-gated inline boot scripts. Keep HSTS and other hardening headers in relayd; let each app own CSP."
      proof: "curl -sI https://ai.brgen.no/ | grep -i content-security shows Rails policy with script-src nonce"

    - id: sass_embedded_npm_cache
      area: rails
      signal: "bundle34 install fails on sass-embedded; npm EACCES on /root/.npm when installing as app user via doas"
      action: "pkg_add node if missing. When running bundle install via doas su -m <app>, export HOME=/home/<app> and NPM_CONFIG_CACHE=/home/<app>/.npm so npm does not touch root-owned cache."
      proof: "su -m brgen -c 'cd /home/brgen/app && bundle34 check' exits 0; bin/rails dartsass:build succeeds"

    - id: takeaway_seed_city_association
      area: rails
      signal: "db:seed:replant fails after Playlist with City expected, got String"
      action: "CityTenantable adds belongs_to :city on takeaway_restaurants, colliding with the legacy string city column. Set ActsAsTenant.current_tenant in seeds.rb; omit city: from create! and use update_column(:city, label) for the display string."
      proof: "RAILS_ENV=test bundle exec rails db:seed:replant exits 0 in brgen"

    - id: live_search_empty_query_count
      area: rails
      signal: "live_search_test fails on empty query .none scope count"
      action: "Shared::LiveSearch#safe_count returns 0 when query.blank? before calling null_relation? or count on arbitrary scopes."
      proof: "bundle exec rails test test/services/live_search_test.rb in brgen"

    - id: github_actions_billing_lock
      area: ci
      signal: "MASTER Tests workflow fails in ~5s with no job logs; email on every push"
      action: "GitHub account billing lock blocks runners. Pause push/pull_request triggers (workflow_dispatch only) until billing fixed at github.com/settings/billing. Re-enable .github/workflows/master-tests.yml and master-through-master.yml triggers after."
      proof: "gh workflow list shows paused; push does not enqueue Actions email"

    - id: gh_auth_vps_and_workstation
      area: deploy
      signal: "gh api returns HTTP 401 on VPS or Mac; cannot inspect PRs/workflows remotely"
      action: "Run gh auth login on each host that needs GitHub API. VPS: su dev -c 'gh auth login'. Never commit tokens."
      proof: "gh auth status shows logged in; gh api user returns 200"

    - id: pf_ssh_not_bruteforce
      area: openbsd
      signal: "Operator assumes SSH lockout is pf bruteforce after rapid reconnects"
      action: "Tracked pf.conf exempts SSH (pass in quick … port 22) before bruteforce table. Bruteforce is fed by HTTP/HTTPS rate limits only. Lockouts are usually RAM/CPU saturation from parallel SSH or bin/ci — use tmux, one app CI at a time, flush bruteforce only when HTTP wedge suspected."
      proof: "grep 'port 22' OPENBSD/etc/pf.conf shows quick pass before block quick from <bruteforce>"

    - id: vps_one_ssh_no_parallel_ci
      area: deploy
      signal: "load averages >10 on vm23; dozens of ruby in D state; rcctl master/amber failed; SSH hangs"
      action: "Never open parallel SSH sessions to vm23. Use zsh OPENBSD/bin/vps_ci.sh APP (mutex via /var/db/pub4/ci.lock) or vps_ci_all.sh for serial fleet proof. MASTER scan: zsh OPENBSD/bin/vps_master_scan.sh. resource_guard cron runs stale_ci_cleanup.ksh when load>=4. Kill stale local ssh clients first; doas rcctl restart master amber after cleanup. If D-state ruby won't die: host console vmctl stop/start vm23."
      proof: "uptime load <4; test -f /var/db/pub4/ci.lock; zsh OPENBSD/bin/vps_ci.sh brgen; doas rcctl check master brgen amber"

    - id: vps_ci_shared_tree_path
      area: deploy
      signal: "Importmap/RuboCop still run on VPS despite ci.rb fix; postpro resolves to /home/postpro"
      action: "config/ci.rb requires ../../shared from app/config → /home/<app>/shared (not /home/<app>/app/shared). vps_ci.sh syncs full RAILS/shared there plus code overlay. Set PUB4_RAILS_ROOT=/home/dev/pub4/RAILS for DeployPaths. Postpro/replicate: Operator::DeployPaths or MASTER/tools/*.rb — never Rails.root/../../postpro alone on copy-tree."
      proof: "grep unless vps_host /home/brgen/shared/config/ci.rb; ruby -e 'require \"operator/deploy_paths\"' under brgen app finds /home/dev/pub4/studio/postpro/postpro.rb"

    - id: vps_ci_lock_perms
      area: deploy
      signal: "pub4-ci-guard: EACCES on flock or EPERM deleting lock.holder"
      action: "Lock at /var/db/pub4/ci.lock mode 644 (vps_ci pub4_ensure_ci_lock), taken with flock(2) by CiGuard and OPENBSD/bin/with-ci-lock. Opened read-only, so it does not need to be world-writable. Do not pre-create .holder as root — vps_ci removes stale holder before CI; CiGuard tolerates a holder it cannot write or delete."
      proof: "ls -l /var/db/pub4/ci.lock; zsh OPENBSD/bin/vps_ci.sh brgen exits 0"

    - id: git_shared_worktree_commit_scope
      area: process
      signal: "git commit lands unexpected files from a concurrent agent's staged changes in this same working tree (e.g. .master/snapshot.md, unrelated RAILS/ edits riding along with an intended fix)"
      action: "git add path && git commit only commits the whole index, not just what was just staged — Grok/Codex/other agents share this exact working tree and stage things independently. Before every commit: git status -sb -- <intended files> must show ONLY those files staged. If anything else shows up staged, git reset (unstages everything, keeps the working tree) and re-add only the intended paths, then re-verify before committing."
      proof: "git status -sb -- <files> immediately before commit shows no unexpected entries; git log -1 --stat after the commit lists only the intended files"

    - id: scanner_finding_comment_vs_code
      area: master
      signal: "rake selftest/constitution flags a pattern (e.g. HTTP/Open3 without bounded timeout, silent catch {}) that only appears in a comment, or inside a build-output copy under web/public/assets"
      action: "Before fixing the flagged code, read the actual line: check it isn't inside a comment (strip # lines before matching) and isn't a Propshaft-fingerprinted copy under web/public/assets (already excluded via Scanner.skip_path? — reuse that check rather than hand-rolling a new exclusion list). Widen detection regexes narrowly (e.g. \\w*thr\\w*\\.join\\( for a bounded Thread/Process wait) rather than broadly, to avoid introducing new false negatives."
      proof: "rake selftest finding count drops for the specific file/law with no behavior change; rake test stays green"

    - id: env_isolation_list_incompleteness
      area: master_web
      signal: "a spawned subprocess (tts-worker or any Process.spawn(env, ...) child) resolves against the wrong Gemfile/Gemfile.lock despite an isolation env hash nil'ing named bundler keys"
      action: "Process.spawn(env, ...) without unsetenv_others: true only clears the keys explicitly listed in that hash — any other bundler-adjacent var (RUBYLIB, BUNDLE_LOCKFILE, a stray marker var) passes through from the caller unfiltered. Diff the actual live env at the spawn point (Falcon's/Rails' full ENV) against the isolation list rather than assuming the named list is complete."
      proof: "a one-time diagnostic log at the spawn point (or ps -o command= -p <spawned pid>) shows no leaked BUNDLE_*/RUBYLIB vars beyond the intended isolation set"

skills_registry:
  meta:
    source: runtime authority — edit this file directly; do not add data/skills/*.md
    count: 18
  skills:
  - name: axioms
    description: Summarize constitutional rules and invariant checks.
    triggers:
    - "\\baxioms\\b"
    body: |-
      The axioms skill summarizes constitutional rules and invariant checks for the current context. It answers when the operator asks about axioms or when MASTER needs a compact statement of what must hold.

      Use the smallest rule set that proves the point, not a lecture. Prefer rules that are verifiable from the repository or session state rather than restating generic principles.
  - name: ecology
    description: Inspect the repository ecology and connected file relationships.
    triggers:
    - "\\becology\\b"
    body: |-
      The ecology skill inspects how files, modules, and dependencies relate across the repository. It is triggered when the operator mentions ecology or when MASTER needs a grounded map of connected artifacts rather than an isolated file view.

      Favor direct file and graph evidence over abstract summaries. Name concrete paths, imports, and call sites so follow-up work can start from evidence instead of inference.
  - name: fix
    description: Apply targeted repairs and verify the result.
    triggers:
    - "\\bfix\\b"
    body: |-
      The fix skill applies targeted repairs and verifies that the change actually resolves the reported problem. It activates on fix or when MASTER is asked to repair a specific defect rather than redesign a subsystem.

      Prefer minimal edits, preserve user work, and verify the change path end to end. Confirm behavior with tests, logs, or a reproducible check before treating the fix as complete.

  - name: growth
    description: Audit public growth surfaces across search, permission marketing, partner attribution, and conversion measurement.
    triggers:
    - "\\b(?:growth|marketing|seo|newsletter|affiliate|conversion|acquisition)\\b"
    body: |-
      The growth skill audits pub4's public growth surfaces as one system: search and local discovery, permission marketing, partner and affiliate measurement, and the conversion path. Use current code and runtime evidence first: shared SEO and schema helpers, consent and newsletter jobs, outbound-click and partner-marketing models, and the existing frontend and production gates.

      Separate observed instrumentation from inferred opportunity. Preserve consent, disclosure, local relevance, and first-party measurement; never invent traffic, conversions, or attribution. Prefer one small measurable experiment over broad promotional machinery. End with concrete file-backed gaps and the smallest next change.

  - name: frontend
    description: Run browser-first frontend verification across responsive composition, interaction states, and rendered evidence.
    triggers:
    - "\\b(?:frontend|ui|ux|visual|responsive|browser)\\b"
    body: |-
      The frontend skill treats the browser render as evidence. Use GeometryProbe, mobile journeys, composition probes, web-platform probes, and the visual ghost/difference stack before proposing source changes. Trace every actionable observation to a stable selector or visible text anchor and the applicable visual law.

      Prefer deletion, alignment, typography, spacing, and existing primitives over new decorative machinery. Preserve semantics, accessibility, performance, and low-end fallbacks. When the evidence changes, feed the smallest correction back through /fix and verify the rendered result again.

  - name: model
    description: Switch or inspect the active model for the current session.
    triggers:
    - "\\bmodel\\b"
    body: |-
      The model skill switches or inspects the active model for the current session. It responds when the operator asks about the model in use or when a task clearly benefits from a different cost–capability tradeoff.

      Use the cheapest model that still meets the task, and switch only when the tradeoff is clear. State what changed and why so later turns do not assume a heavier model than necessary.
  - name: process
    description: Summarize the current operating state of MASTER.
    triggers:
    - "\\bprocess\\b"
    body: |-
      The process skill summarizes MASTER’s current operating state: what is running, what stage a workflow is in, and which subsystems are active. It is triggered on process or when the operator needs a snapshot of runtime behavior rather than repository contents.

      Keep operational output compact enough to scan in one glance. Lead with the facts that unblock the next action and omit narrative filler.
  - name: propose-tree
    description: Suggest adjacent improvements from the current change set.
    triggers:
    - propose-tree
    body: |-
      The propose-tree skill suggests adjacent improvements grounded in the current change set. It activates on propose-tree or when the operator wants follow-up work that naturally extends what was just edited or reviewed.

      Only propose follow-ups that are directly grounded in current evidence. Each suggestion should tie to a file, finding, or gap already visible in the session so the tree stays actionable rather than speculative.
  - name: resync
    description: Reconcile the worktree or runtime state with the intended source of
      truth.
    triggers:
    - "\\bresync\\b"
    body: |-
      The resync skill reconciles the worktree or runtime state with the intended source of truth after drift, failed merges, or stale caches. It is triggered on resync or when MASTER must realign local state with git, config, or an external canonical copy.

      Use after divergence, and confirm the restored state with evidence before moving on. Show what was out of sync, what was reset or merged, and how the result was verified.
  - name: review
    description: Review code with an eye for correctness, risk, and missing tests.
    triggers:
    - "\\breview\\b"
    body: |-
      The review skill examines code for correctness, risk, and missing tests. It activates on review or when the operator asks for a structured pass over a change without necessarily applying fixes.

      Lead with findings, cite lines, and separate bugs from style or preference. Order by severity so the operator can decide what to fix first.
  - name: rules
    description: Inspect the registered rule set and its priorities.
    triggers:
    - "\\brules\\b"
    body: |-
      The rules skill inspects the registered rule set and how priorities resolve when rules conflict. It responds on rules or when MASTER must explain which constraints apply and in what order.

      Prefer the live registry over stale documentation. Quote or summarize the active definitions MASTER actually loads, not copies that may lag the source files.
  - name: scan
    description: Scan files or directories for violations and opportunities.
    triggers:
    - "\\bscan\\b"
    body: |-
      The scan skill searches files or directories for violations, smells, and improvement opportunities within the requested scope. It is triggered on scan or as the first step of broader MASTER workflows that need evidence before fix or deliberation.

      Findings should be evidence-led and narrow to the requested target. Report path, line or pattern, and severity so downstream skills can act without re-scanning the whole tree.
  - name: status
    description: Summarize the current session or repository health.
    triggers:
    - "\\bstatus\\b"
    body: |-
      The status skill summarizes session and repository health: branch, dirty files, failing checks, and anything else that affects whether work can proceed safely. It activates on status or when the operator needs a quick health read without a full scan.

      Keep status terse, concrete, and tied to the latest verifiable evidence. Prefer commands and paths the operator can re-run over subjective assessments.
  - name: synth
    description: Play synthesisers live on the sound card -- Moog, Prophet and Rhodes patches, progressions, endless improvisation -- and steer them by voice.
    triggers:
    - "\\b(?:synth\\w*|moog|minimoog|prophet|rhodes|improvi[sz]\\w*|sound\\s*card|play\\s+(?:some\\s+)?music)\\b"
    body: |-
      MASTER plays music live through the sound card, generated in pure Ruby as it plays. its main sound is the live set the operator froze, MASTER/tools/dilla/liveset.rb: soul-jazz chords improvised on dilla's analogue patches and Moog ladder, opening on the loved Fm9 progression, a new pad every chord, a rotating bass, an arpeggiated lead on some chords, and a DFAM with a kick under it, until it is told to stop. "play", "improvise", "keep playing" and "play me something with moog patches" all start that, exactly as frozen; its knobs turn by themselves and a sentence cannot turn them.

      Named things play instead: "play a moog bass" or "play the lucky man lead" (nine Minimoog Model D panels written in the instrument's own dial units), "play a lofi pad through dilla_love", "play a rhodes through dilla_love", "improvise with drums" (drums, a clap, a dub send, FM leads). Those can be steered while they play: "slowly open the filter", "raise the resonance", "morph to a prophet pad", "drums off", "more dub", "fm lead". "stop" ends whatever plays. "play me a sine wave" plays a raw tone live, and "play it" plays the last file MASTER rendered. Asked what it can do with sound, say this plainly and offer a sentence to try.
  - name: tail
    description: Read recent event history with a small, focused window.
    triggers:
    - "\\btail\\b"
    body: |-
      The tail skill reads recent event history through a small, focused window so the operator can see what MASTER or the environment did last. It is triggered on tail or when context from the latest log lines would explain the current state.

      Show only enough history to explain the current issue or next step. Truncate older noise and highlight timestamps, errors, and the final outcome.
  - name: topic
    description: Track the current conversation or workstream topic.
    triggers:
    - "\\btopic\\b"
    body: |-
      The topic skill tracks the current conversation or workstream topic so later turns can resume without re-deriving intent. It responds on topic or when MASTER should label what is being worked on for session continuity.

      Keep topic labels short and meaningful enough to recover later. One line should be enough for the operator to recognize the thread days afterward.
  - name: why
    description: Explain a rule, finding, or design choice with local evidence.
    triggers:
    - "\\bwhy\\b"
    body: |-
      The why skill explains a rule, finding, or design choice using evidence from the repository and session. It activates on why or when the operator asks for rationale behind a constraint, scan result, or architectural decision.

      Prefer direct file references and current state over memory or theory. Point to the code, config, or log line that justifies the explanation.
  - name: workflow
    description: Inferred scan → fix preview → council deliberation. Users should not
      need a command name.
    triggers: []
    body: |-
      The workflow skill runs MASTER’s internal pipeline when the operator asks for a full pass without naming individual steps. Phrases such as run this through MASTER, full pass, or tribunal infer scan, fix dry-run, and council deliberation in sequence.

      No /triad or /workflow command is required unless debugging. MASTER orchestrates the stages internally; the operator only needs the natural-language trigger.

`````

  audit_logging:
    meaning: record who did what when
    detects: unaudited_actions
    severity: high
    confidence: 0.85
    operation: add_logging
    # Evidence is lib/trace/log.rb (append-only tool:before log), pinned by
    # test_principle_evidence.rb. AUDIT_APPEND_ONLY reads the sink: a file that
    # subscribes to tool:before must append rather than truncate, so the record
    # survives past one turn. It does not reach the other half — whether every
    # mutating action publishes tool:before at all. Five tools in lib/io mutate
    # and never publish (clean, git_context, memory_record,
    # subdomain_orchestrator, web_fetch), and closing that is a change to those
    # tools rather than a detector question.
    rule_ids:
    - AUDIT_APPEND_ONLY
    status: covered
    root: least_authority
    tags:
    - code

# The eleven root definitions the entries' root: fields reference — folded
# from data/principle_roots.yml (no reader of its own; the map is the reader).
roots:
  one_source:
    law: every fact has exactly one definition
    because: copies do not stay equal, and the drift is silent
    in_code: DRY, normalization, single source of truth
    in_prose: one statement of a claim, referenced after
    in_visual: one token per colour, spacing step and face

  no_surplus:
    law: remove what carries no weight
    because: what is absent cannot be wrong, and every part costs attention
    in_code: KISS, YAGNI, dead code, speculative generality
    in_prose: omit needless words
    in_visual: as little design as possible; negative space is the composition

  one_responsibility:
    law: a unit names one thing and does it
    because: a unit with two reasons to change is changed for one and broken for the other
    in_code: single responsibility, separation of concerns, short methods
    in_prose: one idea per paragraph
    in_visual: one message per view; one job per component

  least_surprise:
    law: behaviour matches the expectation the name and the convention set
    because: a reader who must verify every name reads nothing else
    in_code: POLA, convention over configuration, idiom, consistent naming
    in_prose: the word means what it usually means
    in_visual: Jakob's law — it works the way the rest of the web works

  visible_state:
    law: the system shows what is true, including failure
    because: a hidden failure is indistinguishable from success until it is expensive
    in_code: surface errors first, no silent rescue, no swallowed exceptions
    in_prose: say what happened, not what was attempted
    in_visual: visibility of system status; honest materials

  bounded_load:
    law: never exceed what the reader can hold at once
    because: capacity is a property of people, not of the design
    in_code: nesting depth, parameter count, method and file length
    in_prose: sentence length; one clause deep
    in_visual: Miller's and Hick's laws; measure, leading, choice count

  stable_contract:
    law: a boundary is explicit and changes deliberately
    because: an implicit boundary is crossed accidentally and cannot be defended
    in_code: open/closed, Liskov, interface segregation, dependency inversion
    in_prose: defined terms keep their definition
    in_visual: a component's props are its contract; variants are declared

  proportion:
    law: relationships follow a declared scale, never an arbitrary value
    because: a number with no derivation cannot be checked or changed as a set
    in_code: named constants over magic numbers, configuration over literals
    in_prose: parallel structure; consistent register
    in_visual: modular scale, vertical rhythm, grid, ma as measured interval

  least_authority:
    law: a part gets the least power that lets it work, and failure is survivable
    because: what cannot reach a thing cannot break it, and what is not backed up is not kept
    in_code: least privilege, pledge/unveil, explicit absence over null, restore-tested backups
    in_prose: say only what you can stand behind
    in_visual: a control does one thing, and an irreversible one asks first

  stewardship:
    law: a change leaves what it touched better, and answers to what was already there
    because: nobody arrives at an empty site; the context has claims on the work
    in_code: boy-scout rule, adaptive reuse over rewrite, boring technology
    in_prose: edit what exists before adding beside it
    in_visual: the building enhances its site rather than ignoring it

  reach:
    law: whoever arrives can operate it
    because: capability, device and attention vary, and the design does not get to choose its user
    in_code: semantic markup, keyboard paths, no capability assumed
    in_prose: plain words before jargon
    in_visual: Fitts and von Restorff — targets big enough to hit, differences big enough to see

`````

    Priority-1 Orient work—`orient.rb`, slim AGENTS and CLAUDE, `/orient` plus subcommand, zshrc `[[ -t 0 ]]` guard—shipped then reverted as a useless wrapper. One fact equals one place; commits stay small and reversible; smoothing items remain follow-up tickets.

    2026-07 doc consolidation: top-level MASTER stubs (SOURCE_TREE, TRACE, REPLICATE, CONVENTIONS, QUICKSTART, AGENT_CONTRACT, RUNTIME_MAP, root IDENTITY.md) removed or folded into START_HERE.md. Runtime shards were merged into data/runtime.yml.

    2026-07-15 tier-5 YAML pass: data/ went from 77 to 54 files. 9 genuinely dead files removed (architectures.yml, gems.yml, llm_operators.yml, rails.yml, why_command.yml, epistemics.yml, templates.yml, ui.yml, budget.yml — none had any real code consumer, despite a couple of their own header comments claiming otherwise), 13 folded into patterns.yml under namespaced top-level keys (closings, motd, webhooks, cron_jobs, violation_priors, stale_namespaces, auth_profiles, cli, heartbeat, refusal_templates, operator_playbook, skills_registry), 1 folded without a real consumer but kept as reference documentation (vocabulary.yml — its "sacred_terms" claim was never enforced by code, but documents naming conventions actively used in the codebase). Deliberately NOT folded: council.yml, state.yml, topologies.yml, tts.yml, tools.dynamic.yml, openbsd.yml — each has a specific architectural reason (see START_HERE.md's Data File Budget section). This tier-5 pass is done; remaining data/ files are either Tier 1-4 or one of these documented exceptions.
- key: project_falcon_em_subprocess
  name: Falcon Async + EventMachine = subprocess pattern
  description: EM-based gems (rb-edge-tts, em-http) inside Falcon request handlers
    must shell out to a subprocess; Process.fork and direct EM.run both fail
  type: project
  body: |-
    Falcon uses Async and io-event fibers. `Process.fork` from a request fiber raises `RuntimeError: Closing scheduler with blocked operations!`. `EventMachine.run` conflicts with Falcon's reactor and hangs or closes prematurely. This surfaced in `Master::Speech.synthesize_edge` via rb-edge-tts and applies to any `em-*` gem inside a request handler.

    The pattern is a `bin/<name>-worker` script that runs EventMachine work and writes a tempfile; the controller calls `Open3.capture3`. Reference implementation: `MASTER/bin/tts-worker` and `MASTER/lib/voice/speech.rb#synthesize_edge`.
- key: project_master
  name: MASTER project context
  description: pub4/MASTER — constitutional AI runtime and repo-wide governance kernel
  type: project
  body: |-
    MASTER is the constitutional AI runtime in pure Ruby. The repository is governed as four top-level trees: MASTER, RAILS, OPENBSD and STUDIO; STUDIO owns media implementations and `MASTER/tools/` exposes compatibility symlinks.

    The public runtime surfaces are `MASTER/bin/master` for the agent session and `MASTER/bin/operator` for repository-wide operations. `/review` is read-only; `/critique` invokes council; `/fix` is the write/convergence operation. `MASTER/bin/operator gate` runs the repository ladder with autofix enabled, while `--scan-only` is the measurement-only variant.

    Production is vm23. OpenBSD deploy behavior belongs under `OPENBSD/`; Rails product truth belongs under `RAILS/apps.yml`. `MASTER/data/soul.yml` and `MASTER/data/rules.yml` are the law. Current runtime structure is the code under `MASTER/lib/`, the media implementations under `STUDIO/`, and the MASTER-owned utilities under `MASTER/tools/`; do not substitute an abandoned module target or a historical shell workflow for the present tree.
- key: project_master_dual_gemfile
  name: MASTER has two Gemfiles
  description: MASTER/Gemfile (CLI) and MASTER/web/Gemfile (Falcon web) are independent
    — adding a gem to one does NOT make it available in the other
  type: project
  body: |-
    `MASTER/Gemfile` serves the CLI and `MASTER/web/Gemfile` serves the Falcon web tier. They are independent—adding a gem to one does not make it available in the other.

    `MASTER/web/Gemfile` declares `gem "master", path: ".."`, which loads via the gemspec, not the parent Gemfile. Gems used in `MASTER/lib/` from web handlers must appear in both `MASTER/Gemfile` and `MASTER/web/Gemfile`, or in `master.gemspec` as a runtime dependency. Bundling only once leaves Falcon unable to `require` the gem—a LoadError that surfaces as a controller rescue and 503. `rb-edge-tts` exhibited this: CLI worked while `/chat/tts` failed.

    When adding a dependency, edit both Gemfiles, run `bundle install` in `MASTER/` and `MASTER/web/`, and verify the gem appears in `MASTER/web/Gemfile.lock`.
- key: project_master_seven_module_refactor
  name: historical seven-module refactor proposal
  description: Reverted architecture proposal retained only as provenance
  type: reference
  body: |-
    The seven-module layout (`now`, `loop`, `judge`, `voice`, `ground`, `reach`, `trace`) was proposed on 2026-05-08 and later abandoned. The current repository does not use that target structure: the live `MASTER/lib/` tree has its present domain directories, and the public operator surfaces are `bin/master` and `bin/operator`.

    Treat this entry as historical context only. Do not create, restore, or route code toward the seven-module layout unless a new architectural decision explicitly establishes it. Git history holds the old implementation and branch work.
- key: project_master_yml_json_authority

  description: The predecessor master.yml/master.json drift-closing effort (started
    2026-05-05) is finished; both predecessor files are deleted. Authority chain is
    CLAUDE.md's "Authority order" — soul.yml, then rules.yml.
  type: project
  body: |-
    Historical: on 2026-05-05, the directive was that MASTER should implement what predecessor `master.json` (v43.0.1, November–December 2025, 130 commits) and `master.yml` (v31–v49.75, December 2025–February 2026, 668 commits) described, mined from their deleted history. That drift-closing work is done — the priority gaps listed at the time (Universal Laws ladder, Strunk & White safeguards, biases section, structural_ops taxonomy, council personas, evidence logging, beauty section, per-language templates, and the rest) now live in `soul.yml` and `rules.yml`.

    Neither predecessor file exists in the repo anymore. `soul.yml` (constitution) and `rules.yml` (scan rules + `principle_priorities`) are the sole authoritative sources — see the "Authority order" line in `CLAUDE.md`. Do not look for law in `master.yml`/`master.json`; they are gone.
- key: reference_grok_ui_cli_patterns
  name: Grok-inspired UI/CLI patterns (chatlog dump 2026-05-07)
  description: Reference dump from a sister chat — StyleCoach UI prompt, htmx+SSE
    streaming, tty-prompt/tty-spinner advanced features, multi-line editor, character-stream
    LLM CLI. For MASTER's web UI and CLI polish.
  type: reference
  body: |-
    This is a Grok-style design dump from 2026-05-07. Cherry-pick ideas; do not bulk-import.

    StyleCoach critiques MASTER output across CLI, web, and screenshots. Rules: the interface disappears; zero visual debt; personality lives in words, spacing, and timing; speed beats everything; mobile-first dark; every element must earn its place. Format is `ELEMENT/Current/Suggested/Reason` plus `distilled_ui_lesson`. Examples include at most two accent colors, spinners of at most three dots, and a prompt bar fixed at the bottom.

    Web streaming uses htmx+SSE with `sse-connect="/stream/:id"` and `event: chunk`, plus `X-Accel-Buffering: no` and sleep `rand(0.02..0.08)`. Alternatively use chunked HTTP with `hx-swap="innerHTML"`.

    CLI traits favor char-stream via ANSI `\r` over `Thinking…`, a terse happy path, subtle personality on success and failure, stateful context in SQLite or `~/.master/context.json`, a braille spinner `⠋⠙⠹…` after 1.5s, and one-command install.

    tty-prompt offers `select(filter:)`, `multi_select`, `expand`, `editor(syntax:, word_wrap:)`, `mask`, `slider`, and validators (`in`, `validate`, `convert`, `modify`). Theme uses bright_cyan with `❯` and `◉`. tty-spinner defaults to `:dots_9`, supports `Multi` for parallel work, and uses `hide_cursor: true`. Multi-line input uses `PROMPT.editor` with Anthropic stream char-by-char at `sleep(rand(0.008..0.035))`.

    MASTER already streams SSE on `POST /chat/message` and CLI via `chunk_accumulator`. Borrow Thinking cleanup, ambiguity menus, and tty `editor` for `<<` mode. StyleCoach fits as `/crit` plus a vision tool.
- key: reference_opencrabs
  name: OpenCrabs (Rust MASTER cousin)
  description: github.com/adolfousier/opencrabs — Rust/Ratatui TUI agent, philosophical
    cousin of MASTER. ~803 stars, MIT. Worth-stealing patterns listed with MASTER
    wiring status.
  type: reference
  body: |-
    OpenCrabs is the Rust cousin of MASTER—[opencrabs](https://github.com/adolfousier/opencrabs) with [docs](https://docs.opencrabs.com), v0.3.47 as of June 2026, four thousand plus tests, MIT license, roughly eight hundred stars. It targets Linux, macOS, and Windows; it does not support OpenBSD or `pledge`. Architecture is TUI/CLI → Brain → Services → SQLx/SQLite → LLM providers, built with Rust, Tokio, and Ratatui.

    As of 2026-06-24, MASTER wired brain-files re-read (`data/*.yml`); FTS5 BM25 memory; inline compaction via `ContextWindow`, web SSE, and daily log; `/rebuild` hot-restart; sub-agent tool exclusion (`Policy::Subagent`, `AgentPool`, swarm); typed sub-agents (`agent_taxonomy.yml`, `/btw`); hashline edits (`Io::Hashline`); RTK output filter (`/rtk`); plan pinning (`Ground::ActivePlan`); mission dashboard (`/dashboard`); phantom recovery; skills slash triggers (`CLI::Skills#trigger_for`); soft and hard compaction at 65% and 90%; per-model quota (`Io::ModelQuota`); prompt-cache card (`Trace::CacheEfficiency`, `/chat/metrics`); OpenRouter key rotation (`Io::KeyRotator`); and unified health (`bin/doctor`, `/doctor`).

    OpenCrabs gaps remain: high priority for OAuth-before-key auth rotation, `self_improve` brain writes, and NL `config_manager`; medium for offline STT/TTS, multi-channel inbox, cron DSL, dynamic `tools.toml`, video and PDF multimodal, and usage categorization; low for A2A RPC, `zeroize` key hygiene, and upstream brain sync.

    OpenClaw ([openclaw/openclaw](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw), 355k+ stars, [docs](https://docs.openclaw.ai)) overlaps partially: MASTER now has pairing before personal tools (`Ground::Pairing`, `/pair`, POST /pair), tool profiles public/messaging/full (`Ground::Tool::Profile`), per-subject USER.md/MEMORY.md, HEARTBEAT_OK `personal_pulse` (off by default), and `/security-audit`. Still lacks OAuth/cooldown tiers, Docker sandbox, ClawHub, Live Canvas/A2UI, Voice Wake; webhook/cron ingress exists. Do not treat pairing as sentience or a bodyguard.

    Similar repos include [OpenHands](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands) for sandbox GUI; [Aider](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider) for repo map (`GitContext`, `CodeIndex` partial); [SWE-agent](https://github.com/SWE-agent/SWE-agent) for issue-to-patch (`/fix` partial); [crewAI](https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI) for roles (council and swarm partial); [nekro-agent](https://github.com/KroMiose/nekro-agent) for chat sandbox; and [OpenClaw-RL](https://github.com/Gen-Verse/OpenClaw-RL) for online RL (`Ledger::Feedback` only). Clusters live in `patterns.yml` as `openclaw_like_personal_agents`, `bleeding_edge_experimental_repos`, and `agi_agent_ecosystem`.

    Risks include unapproved RSI brain writes, hallucinated tools in corrupted sessions, bus factor one, and headless web-chat ToS per `ROUTING_REARCHITECTURE.md` §6. Do not conflate `mo-vic/OpenCrab` (distillation) or the empty `opencrab` org with this project.
- key: user_architect_aesthetics
  name: User is an architect; aesthetic proposals usually pass
  description: User's primary discipline is architecture; treat typography, layout,
    design-philosophy proposals as in-scope and likely approved
  type: user
  body: |-
    The operator is an architect by training. Aesthetic, typographic, and design-philosophy proposals—even ones LLMs dismiss as fluff—are usually approved.

    Surface aesthetic content from Bringhurst, Ando, Rams, wabi-sabi, ma, and kanso, plus beauty sections in YAML, without self-censoring. Treat these as engineering anchors, not disclaimers. Propose UI, prose, and config refinements actively. Do not argue that beauty or zen YAML is "not actionable."
- key: master_design_vision
  name: MASTER design vision (pure-Ruby AI, OpenBSD-mirrored, Snohetta parametric)
  description: Guiding vision and influences — steer every design/refactor decision
    toward it
  type: project
  body: |-
    The operator's guiding vision for MASTER, to steer every design and refactor decision.

    (a) A NEW AGE IN COMPUTING — the first pure-Ruby AI. No Python in the spine; Ruby all the way down. Influences the operator cites (to be credited in a forthcoming book): Jeremy Evans (author of Roda + Sequel, and maintainer of the OpenBSD Ruby port — the exact Ruby<->OpenBSD nexus MASTER sits on); adam12 / Adam Daniels (Roda/Sequel/Rack/Hanami minimalist-Ruby school, Gemdocs.org — the operator designed the new Gemdocs logo); DHH (Rails); J Dilla's mastering engineer Dave Cooley (craft and feel); the architecture firm Snohetta; and the wider OpenBSD / Ruby / Rails communities.

    (b) OPENBSD DESIGN, MIRRORED AS CLOSELY AS POSSIBLE. Correctness and simplicity above all; secure-by-default; ruthless removal of unused code; a small closed surface; sane defaults; docs as first-class. Respect to Theo de Raadt. A future OpenBSD Rust port is planned, likely with a higher-level Ruby overlay. Concretely in MASTER: the core/ fold is an OpenBSD-style minimal kernel — a fixed 7-verb World surface (the syscall table), the immutability rule as pledge(2) (the agent cannot rewrite its own constitution or spine), the Constitution as a security gate before every effect, atomic writes.

    (c) SNOHETTA-STYLE NORWEGIAN PARAMETRIC ARCHITECTURE. The operator studied architecture (in Malaysia, their father is from there) and favours timeless, well-thought-out design: one clear organizing idea, nothing decorative, form follows the idea.

    HOW TO APPLY: prefer collapse over accretion — one parametric form with data-driven variants over many near-duplicate files (e.g. the four bin/check-* scripts collapsed to one bin/check --profile). Closed minimal surfaces. When in doubt, remove. Match the surrounding restraint. Craft is not accretion — the TTS voice engines were deliberately kept.
- key: bsdports_openbsd_ports_index
  name: bsdports is the official next-gen OpenBSD ports index (Solene blessing)
  description: RAILS/bsdports — sanctioned successor to Solene Rapenne's ports index
  type: project
  body: RAILS/bsdports is being built as the official next-generation OpenBSD ports
    index — the operator has the blessing and go-ahead of Solene Rapenne (solene@,
    former OpenBSD developer, now Qubes OS core team; blog at dataswamp.org) to create
    the next version of her ports index. Treat bsdports as a first-class, real-world
    OpenBSD-community deliverable, not a demo.
- key: semantic_index_comment_audit
  name: semantic index comment audit
  description: Audit of semantic_index.rb comments for drift - all accurate
  type: reference
  body: |-
    Checked three comment/code pairs in semantic_index.rb:
    [0] nearest method comment: accurately describes returning nearest entry value within threshold or nil
    [1] remember method comment: accurately describes storing embedding->value with LRU eviction
    [2] fetch method comment: accurately describes near-hit return or block computation with storage
    All comments match code behavior. No drift detected.
- key: user

  body: User is an architect by training and primary discipline. Aesthetic, typographic,
