`````yaml
platform_topology:
  id: platform_topology
  tier: platform
  area: deploy
  status: active
  primary_platform:
    id: brgen.no
    role: primary runtime surface and application umbrella
    responsibilities:
    - orchestration surface
    - runtime observability
    - MASTER integration
    - authentication/session coordination
    - shared search/indexing
    - PWA shell
    - dashboard and replay UI
    - subapp routing
    - SEO authority consolidation
    stack:
    - Rails 8
    - Hotwire
    - Turbo streams
    - Stimulus
    - pure SCSS
    - semantic HTML
    - offline-first PWA shell
    - runtime-event-driven UI
    interaction_model:
      borrow_from: X/Twitter
      patterns:
      - dense feed-first layout
      - persistent left navigation on desktop
      - mobile bottom navigation
      - sticky composer/search
      - cursor-paginated timelines
      - inline media/cards
      - fast optimistic interactions
      - keyboard shortcuts
      - minimal modal friction
      must_not_copy:
      - X branding
      - visual chrome
      - dark-pattern engagement mechanics
    feel_like:
    - civic/social operating surface
    - fast timeline application
    - local/community graph
    - observability-aware PWA
    not_like:
    - AI toy
    - startup dashboard
    - engagement casino
    - decorative social clone
  scss_baseline:
    id: bsdports.org
    role: standard SCSS baseline for all Rails apps
    qualities:
    - OpenBSD-inspired restraint
    - semantic HTML defaults
    - typographic rhythm
    - low-noise navigation
    - minimal chrome
    - sparse color
    - high contrast
    - grepable/printable content
    - fast static-first rendering
    - responsive without framework dependency
    shared_layers:
    - tokens
    - reset/base
    - typography
    - layout grid
    - forms
    - buttons
    - tables
    - flash/status messages
    - navigation
    - code/log rendering
    - accessibility states
    - print styles
  subapps:
    inherit:
    - bsdports SCSS baseline
    - typography system
    - runtime event schema
    - PWA shell
    - auth/session conventions
    - accessibility rules
    - SCSS tokens
    - observability contracts
    rule: operationally separable
  applications:
  - id: bsdports.org
    identity: BSD/OpenBSD ports/packages/research focus
    ui: terminal-informed, sparse color, typography-first, documentation-heavy
    role: source of truth for shared SCSS architecture
  - id: amber
    identity: experimental/research/runtime sandbox
    guarantees: lower operational
    rules:
    - isolate experiments
    - do not leak instability into core runtime
    - preserve replay and telemetry discipline
  - id: blogger_aggregate
    identity: indexing, aggregation, summarization, SEO reinforcement
    architecture:
    - canonical metadata
    - structured data/schema.org
    - sitemap automation
    - RSS/Atom ingestion
    - deduplication
    - semantic tagging
    - replayable ingestion pipeline
  shared_principles:
  - semantic HTML
  - pure SCSS
  - bsdports SCSS baseline
  - Hotwire-first interaction
  - accessibility-first design
  - PWA capability where appropriate
  - replayable runtime telemetry
  - restrained operational aesthetics
  - OpenBSD-inspired clarity
  anti_patterns:
  - Tailwind sprawl
  - hydration-heavy SPA architecture
  - decorative dashboards
  - utility-class soup
  - fake activity animations
  - hidden runtime state
  - frontend-derived truth
  - excessive JS frameworks
  - engagement dark patterns
provider_economy:
  id: provider_economy
  tier: core
  area: routing
  status: active
  principle: The orchestrator owns provider selection; models do not select themselves.
  selection_criteria:
  - capability
  - latency
  - hallucination_rate
  - timeout_rate
  - repair_burden
  - token_cost
  - context_capacity
  - historical_reliability
  routing_tiers:
    cheap_cognition:
      use_for:
      - classification
      - compression
      - retrieval_ranking
      - summarization
      - critique
      - voting
      - lint_reasoning
    expensive_cognition:
      use_for:
      - high_risk_synthesis
      - architecture_decisions
      - irreversible_mutations
      - council_arbitration
      - long_horizon_planning
  quarantine:
    triggers:
    - hallucination_rate_spikes
    - retries_exceed_threshold
    - invalid_structured_outputs_repeat
    - timeout_rate_climbs
    - corruption_incidents_increase
  long_term_direction:
    flow:
    - workflow
    - capability_routing
    - health_scoring
    - quorum
    - replay_analysis
    - repair_feedback
    - adaptive_optimization
    goal: Provider layer becomes a runtime economy, not a static config file
repo_ecology:
  id: repo_ecology
  tier: core
  area: repository
  status: active
  core_principle: A repository is semantic topology, dependency ecology, cognitive geography, architectural history, and organizational memory — not a bag of files
  optimize_for:
  - comprehensibility
  - semantic_coherence
  - navigability
  - architectural_elegance
  - entropy_reduction
  pipeline:
  - scan
  - classify
  - cluster
  - score

routing_architecture:
  id: routing_rearchitecture
  tier: core
  area: routing
  status: applied
  authority: analysis and applied fixes; data/soul.yml and data/rules.yml remain law
  current_path:
  - Master.default_model
  - Ground::Config stored default
  - CLI::Routing::ModelRouter#fallback_chain
  - Review::Agent::ModelSelector#routed_models
  - Review::Agent::FallbackChain#attempt_chat_with_fallbacks
  - Review::LLMDispatcher#send_with_cache
  confirmed_gaps:
  - id: webchat_undefined
    issue: WebChat constant was undefined — free web-chat path dead
    fix: lib/io/web_chat.rb Master::Io::WebChat
  - id: ferrum_config_missing
    issue: model_router dig for ferrum_web_chat block did not resolve
    fix: added ferrum_web_chat block to data/models.yml
  - id: free_tier_unrouted
    issue: curated free tier never routed to
    fix: routes explanation/exploration/fallback_default point at free tier
  - id: opus_missing
    issue: Opus 4.8 not encoded as primary when funded
    fix: primary tier with claude-cli and anthropic opus paths
  - id: vision_broken
    issue: images routed to text-only glm model
    fix: vision_model_for uses vision tier via router
  - id: duplicate_anchors
    issue: ".uniq collapsed cascade to single model"
    fix: de-duplicated free tier anchors
  - id: catalog_disconnected
    issue: CatalogIndex not wired to ModelRouter
    fix: ModelRouter#live_free_models merges live :free slugs
  - id: stale_ids
    issue: invented or stale model identifiers
    fix: refreshed claude-opus-4-8, dropped gpt-5.5-thinking
  - id: overlapping_abstractions
    issue: four pick-a-model abstractions contradicted each other
    fix: ModelRouter selector + CatalogIndex data source consolidated
  - id: no_quota_rotation
    issue: no per-model daily budget or multi-key round-robin
    fix: Ground::KeyRotator multi-key OpenRouter round-robin
  budget_aware_ladder:
  - tier: S
    name: Opus 4.8 primary when funded
    models:
    - claude-cli:claude-opus-4-8
    - anthropic/claude-opus-4.1
    entry: affordable and available
  - tier: A
    name: strong paid-cheap
    models:
    - deepseek-reasoner
    - deepseek-chat
    - gemini-2.5-pro
    - claude-sonnet
    entry: Opus budget gone but funds remain
  - tier: B
    name: OpenRouter free cascade
    models:
    - qwen3-coder
    - deepseek-v3-free
    - nemotron
    - gpt-oss
    - llama
    - gemma
    - glm
    - hermes
    - phi
    entry: budget governor reports zero spendable balance
  - tier: C
    name: headless web-chat
    gate: MASTER_WEB_CHAT env flag — opt-in only, ToS-sensitive
  - tier: D
    name: local Ollama
    gate: env-gated offline fallback
  governor_rules:
  - pick entry tier once at turn start
  - escalate upward only on low confidence for critical operations
  - degrade downward on failure or exhausted quota
  - rotate by least-recently-used within tier
  - skip models in cooldown or over daily quota
  applied_changes:
  - Io::WebChat Ferrum-backed opt-in web chat
  - ferrum_web_chat block in models.yml
  - free tier wired into routes
  - vision routing fixed with vision tier
  - primary tier for Opus subscription and paid paths
  - live_free_models from CatalogIndex
  - KeyRotator multi-key round-robin
  - stale id refresh and free tier de-duplication

style_guides:
  id: style_guides
  tier: policy
  area: engineering
  status: active
  clone_script: tools/clone_style_guides.sh
  knowledge_dir: knowledge/style_guides
  sources:
  - id: ruby
    repo: https://github.com/rubocop/ruby-style-guide
    local: ruby-style-guide
    rubocop: true
    enforce_via:
    - ".rubocop.yml"
    - data/rules.yml#style.ruby
  - id: rails
    repo: https://github.com/rubocop/rails-style-guide
    local: rails-style-guide
    rubocop: rubocop-rails-omakase
    enforce_via:
    - RAILS/shared/.rubocop.yml
  - id: javascript
    repo: https://github.com/airbnb/javascript
    local: javascript
    eslint: true
    enforce_via:
    - web/eslint.config.mjs
    - data/rules.yml#style.html
  - id: css
    repo: https://github.com/airbnb/css
    local: css
    enforce_via:
    - data/rules.yml#style.css
    - RAILS/shared/frontend
  - id: thoughtbot
    repo: https://github.com/thoughtbot/guides
    local: guides
    topics:
    - ruby
    - rails
    - git
    - shell
  - id: normalize
    repo: https://github.com/necolas/normalize.css
    local: normalize.css
    use: css_reset_baseline
  ruby_style_guide:
    frozen_string_literal: always
    string_literals: double
    hash_syntax: modern
    guard_clauses: prefer_early_return
    method_length_max: 15
    line_length_max: 120
    naming: snake_case
    percent_literals: "%w[] %i[] for static lists"
    trailing_commas: multiline_only
  rails_style_guide:
    controllers:
    - thin_controllers_fat_models
    - strong_parameters_require_permit
    - rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    - head_or_redirect_guard_clauses
    views:
    - partials_with_locals
    - dom_id_dom_class
    - tag_and_class_names_helpers
    - no_inline_style_or_script
    - i18n_user_facing_strings
    models:
    - strict_loading_by_default
    - includes_on_association_iteration
    - find_each_for_large_sets
    seo:
    - lang_on_html
    - meta_charset_first
    - viewport_viewport_fit_cover
    - csrf_and_csp_meta_tags
    - canonical_url
    - json_ld_schema_org
    - meta_description_truncate_160
  javascript_style_guide:
    modules: es_modules_preferred
    var: forbidden
    const: default_binding
    semicolons: always
    eqeqeq: always
    arrow_functions: prefer_for_callbacks
    naming: camelCase
  html_css_seo:
    html: semantic_landmarks_bare_tag_targeting
    css: bare_tag_first_rem_units
    a11y: wcag_2_2_aaa_target
    seo: shared/seo_kit_json_ld_canonical
  gates:
  - bin/style_gate
  - bundle exec rubocop
  - RAILS/shared/bin/rubocop

ui_philosophy:
  id: runtime_ui_direction
  tier: ui
  area: web
  status: active
  feel_like:
  - control room
  - courtroom
  - terminal
  - scientific instrument
  not_like:
  - startup dashboard
  - gamified AI toy
  - casino UI
  - neon control panel
  visual_philosophy:
    principles:
    - restraint creates authority
    - whitespace is structure
    - typography is architecture
    - motion communicates state
    - observability beats decoration
    runtime_derived:
    - entropy
    - confidence
    - provider health
    - workflow pressure
    - repair activity
    - replay state
    - orchestration topology
    rule: UI must not invent operational truth
  typography:
    use:
    - readable line lengths
    - visible hierarchy
    - restrained contrast
    - stable rhythm
    - monospace only where semantic
    avoid:
    - tiny gray text
    - decorative font systems
    - excessive uppercase
    - compressed spacing
    - visual noise
  motion:
    should:
    - communicate transitions
    - expose workflow state
    - show repair/retry activity
    - reveal orchestration flow
    - remain interruptible
    avoid:
    - infinite animation
    - ornamental transitions
    - motion without semantic meaning
  rails_hotwire:
    favor:
    - server rendering
    - HTML-first workflows
    - Turbo streams
    - progressive enhancement
    - minimal JS runtime
    - DOM-derived interaction
    avoid:
    - SPA complexity unless necessary
    - duplicated client/server state
    - hydration-heavy architectures
  operational_aesthetic:
    express:
    - determinism
    - inspectability
    - replayability
    - governance
    - confidence under pressure
    note: The interface is part of the runtime philosophy

performance_runtime:
  id: performance_runtime
  tier: core
  area: runtime
  status: active
  invariants:
  - id: classify_concurrency
    rule: I/O and orchestration remain thread-oriented; isolated CPU work may use Ractors.
  - id: measure_optimization
    rule: Runtime optimizations retain before/after timing and output-digest evidence.
  - id: native_boundary
    rule: Native gems are inventoryable and unknown Ractor safety never becomes implicit permission.
  - id: content_addressed_dependencies
    rule: Shared immutable gem artifacts are deduplicated by SHA-256 without replacing Bundler installed state.
  landed_subsystems:
  - path: runtime/compute.rb
    role: serial, thread, and explicit Ractor compute backends
  - path: runtime/jit.rb
    role: adaptive YJIT capability detection and telemetry
  - path: runtime/native_inventory.rb
    role: native-extension and Ractor-safety inventory
  - path: runtime/benchmark.rb
    role: deterministic timing and output-digest comparison
  - path: RAILS/_bundle.sh
    role: content-addressed gem-artifact cache shared by Rails applications

social_frontpage_reference:
  id: social_frontpage_reference
  status: active
  date: 2026-09-30
  purpose: Keep the useful interaction patterns from Reddit, X and TikTok while preserving each pub4 surface's own visual dialect.
  research:
    reddit:
      recommendations: https://support.reddithelp.com/hc/en-us/articles/53416317564820-Changelog-September-10-2026
      communities: https://support.reddithelp.com/hc/en-us/articles/28621027395220-How-to-join-or-leave-a-community
      welcoming: https://support.reddithelp.com/hc/en-us/articles/15484358732692-Welcoming-new-members
      setup: https://support.reddithelp.com/hc/en-us/articles/45959071783316-Changelog-February-4-2026
    x:
      timeline: https://help.x.com/en/using-x/x-timeline
      signup: https://help.x.com/en/using-x/create-x-account
      cookies: https://help.x.com/en/rules-and-policies/x-cookies
      follow_widget: https://help.x.com/en/using-x/add-follow-button-to-website
      recommendations: https://help.x.com/en/rules-and-policies/recommendations
    tiktok:
      for_you: https://support.tiktok.com/en/getting-started/for-you/test-for-you
      desktop: https://newsroom.tiktok.com/new-features-bring-tiktok-magic-to-desktop?lang=en
  rules:
    feed:
      - Put the content stream before explanatory marketing chrome.
      - Keep feed modes only when they change the retrieval set; do not duplicate navigation and sorting.
      - Let behavior improve recommendations instead of forcing a long preference wizard.
    onboarding:
      - Show the product before asking for setup.
      - Keep first-run instruction to one short story with three concrete actions at most.
      - Make dismissal obvious and persistent per surface.
    consent:
      - Necessary storage must be named separately from optional measurement or advertising.
      - Accept, reject and customize must be first-layer peers.
      - Optional technology stays off until explicit consent.
    post_detail:
      - Preserve the post's reading measure and content order.
      - Keep social proof and primary actions close to the content.
      - Use a small auth popover for incidental actions when a full-page login would interrupt reading.
      - Never hide the public content behind authentication when the surface is intentionally guest-open.
    micro_interactions:
      - Prefer native popover/dialog primitives over bespoke overlay state.
      - Keep a 44px interaction floor and visible focus state.
      - Stage live feed arrivals instead of shifting content under the reader.
      - Use explicit labels for sponsored/promotional units and keep their visual grammar native to the feed.
  mapping:
    brgen: feed-first-local-social-posts-with-light-auth-prompt
    amber: editorial-reading-detail-with-light-auth-prompt
    master: treat these as durable UX constraints and evidence sources, not as a mandate to clone another product's colors or chrome
`````

### data/scan_coverage.yml

`````yaml
# Which of MASTER's own Ruby is subject to MASTER's own law.
#
# `Fix::SelfCheck` and `rake constitution` scanned `File.join(root, "lib")` as a
# path literal. `core/` sat beside `lib/` from 2026-07-20 to 2026-08-12, so for
# three weeks the six files that judge every effect were the only files in the
# tree exempt from the law they enforce. Nobody decided that and nothing said it;
# it fell out of a string. The 2026-08-12 merge moved the fold under `lib/` and
# the exemption closed silently, which is the same failure in the other
# direction — a gate's coverage changing without anyone reading a number.
#
# This file is that number. `rake lint:scan_coverage` fails when a top-level
# directory of MASTER holds Ruby and appears in neither list, so a new tree is a
# decision instead of an accident. `roots` is read by Fix::SelfCheck, not just by
# the lint — a coverage manifest nothing loads is the inert-config defect this
# repo already has enough of.
#
# An exemption with no subject is a hole in a gate nobody can see
# (`soul.yml` EXEMPTIONS_EXPIRE), so an `exempt` entry naming a directory that no
# longer exists fails too.
scan_coverage:
  # Scanned by the self-directed gates. Relative to MASTER/.
  roots:
  - lib
  # The rules are subject to the rules. law/ arrived with 85 rules migrated out
  # of rules.yml and was classified as neither, which is the state this file
  # exists to make impossible — 91 Ruby files that no gate looked at, in the one
  # tree whose whole subject is what the gates look at.
  #
  # Scanned rather than exempt because it scans clean: adding it here produces no
  # finding beyond the one constitution.rb already carries. The `bad` fixture in
  # each Law.define does trip the security sweep, which is a different gate and
  # is handled where it belongs, in tools/security_sweep.rb.
  - law
  - plugins
  # Not scanned, and why. A reason is required: the lint fails on a blank one,
  # because "exempt: true" records the exemption without recording the argument,
  # and the argument is the part that rots.
  exempt:
    bin: >-
      Exempt because listing it as scanned would be inert, not because
      nothing reads it. The two entry points into the same scanner
      disagree here: the /scan CLI passes glob "**/*"
      (lib/cli/scan/request.rb) and reads all 29 files in bin/, while
      Fix::SelfCheck calls scan_dir with no override and gets SCAN_GLOB,
      which matches on extension and reaches 1 of 29 -- every executable
      here is extensionless by convention. roots is what SelfCheck reads,
      so moving bin/ there would declare coverage that SCAN_GLOB still
      will not deliver. A full /scan already reports 103 findings across
      18 of these files, gate, check and pub4 among them, and nothing acts
      on them. Closing this means one glob, not one list entry.
    test: >-
      Tests are the instrument, not the subject. Scanning them makes every
      fixture that deliberately contains a violation into a violation, which is
      how a self-scanning gate learns to fail on its own evidence.
    tools: >-
      Standalone scripts run by rake and by hand, outside the Zeitwerk loader and
      outside the runtime. Exempt from SelfCheck only: lib/operator/self_findings.rb
      counts MASTER/tools under its ratchet, so a finding here is measured and
      cannot grow silently.
    web: >-
      A Rails application with its own gates (bin/check --profile=web,
      test:web_ui, test:integration_web). MASTER's scanner law is written for the
      runtime, and applying rules like DENSITY to ERB-adjacent controllers
      produces findings nobody acts on. The face law (FOR_OF, TEMPLATE_LITERALS,
      NO_JQUERY and the rest) is still counted: lib/operator/self_findings.rb reads
      MASTER/web under its ratchet, skipping only generated bundles.
    gates: >-
      Gates are executable instruments, not runtime source. They have their own
      manifest (gates/gates.yml) and runner, and the gate suite is the check that
      governs them. Scanning the instruments with the runtime constitution would
      mix the measuring apparatus into the subject and make every fixture-shaped
      assertion part of the measured corpus.

`````

### data/security.yml

`````yaml
# frozen_string_literal: true

# MASTER security defaults.
# Local-first, zero-listener, explicit pairing, fail-closed tool policy.
#
# The file is split into enforced policy and recorded intent, and the split is
# checked by test/test_security_defaults.rb. Before the split, exactly one key
# here had a reader — tools.custom.require_review_for_destructive — while the
# gateway bind, the dashboard, the session trust tiers, the pairing TTL, the
# ingress rate limit and the five tool deny patterns all read as enforced policy
# and enforced nothing. One was worse than inert: the ingress limit was also
# hardcoded in the controller, so the file and the code could disagree with
# nothing noticing.
#
# Add a top-level key only together with its reader. Anything without one belongs
# under `planned:`, and the test fails either way round.

ingress:
  # Cron/webhook triggers → POST /ingress/cron/:name or /ingress/webhook/:name.
  # Set MASTER_INGRESS_TOKEN in env.
  # Read by MASTER/web/app/controllers/ingress_controller.rb.
  rate_limit_per_minute: 30
  window_seconds: 60

# Per-IP request budgets for the web face, each over its own window. Read by
# MASTER/web/app/controllers/application_controller.rb#web_rate_limit.
web_rate_limits:
  chat: { per_window: 30, window_seconds: 60 }
  tts: { per_window: 30, window_seconds: 60 }
  # Polls of an existing job, not synthesis. pollTTSJob asks every 250ms-1.5s
  # per utterance, and a 429 here drops the client to the browser voice.
  tts_poll: { per_window: 300, window_seconds: 60 }
  read: { per_window: 120, window_seconds: 60 }
  write: { per_window: 60, window_seconds: 60 }

tools:
  custom:
    # Read by lib/cli/destructive_routes.rb#blocking_review?.
    require_review_for_destructive: true
  # Read by lib/ground/tool.rb. public = open internet; messaging =
  # paired visitor (fetch + personal memory, never Shell); full is implicit
  # (authenticated, dangerous only when elevated).
  profiles:
    public:
      - AskLlm
      - WebSearch
      - SubdomainOrchestrator
    messaging:
      - AskLlm
      - WebSearch
      - SubdomainOrchestrator
      - WebFetch
      - MemoryRecord
  # Read by lib/ground/tool.rb (Tool::Domain). The authority domain a standing
  # order acts under and what it may reach. Finance, household and devices wait
  # for the operator's consent, one domain at a time, recorded by /orders consent.
  domains:
    coding: { reach: [commands, callables, exec, memory] }
    research: { reach: [commands, exec, memory] }
    projects: { reach: [commands, callables, exec, memory] }
    security: { reach: [callables, exec] }
    personal: { reach: [exec] }
    wellbeing: { reach: [exec] }
    household: { consent: required, reach: [exec] }
    finance: { consent: required, reach: [exec] }
    devices: { consent: required, reach: [exec] }

# Remote-channel pairing. Read by lib/ground/pairing.rb. Store is .master/
# (gitignored); a path under data/security/ would commit identities.
pairing:
  required_for_remote_channels: true
  code_ttl_seconds: 600
  allowlist_path: ".master/pairing/allowlist.yml"
  # Read by lib/ground/pairing.rb; applied in PairController and chat redeem.
  redeem_per_minute: 8
  redeem_window_seconds: 60

# Intent with no implementation. Nothing reads any of this, and saying so here is
# the point: a policy file whose enforced half cannot be told from its aspirational
# half is how "zero-listener, explicit pairing, fail-closed" came to describe a
# system with none of the three wired.
planned:
  # A local HTTP gateway that does not listen by default. Io::Gateway exists and
  # is instantiated in the live boot, but it takes no bind/port from here. This
  # is not the web face: that is Falcon on 53187, declared in web/ and forwarded
  # by relayd. Nothing has ever listened on 18789.
  gateway:
    listen: false
    bind: "127.0.0.1"
    port: 18789

  dashboard:
    enabled: false
    bind: "127.0.0.1"
    port: 18800

  # Per-session trust tiers. There is no session-trust lookup anywhere. The trust
  # boundary that does exist is in web/app/controllers — visitor chat cannot reach
  # the Fold, closed 2026-07-27.
  sessions:
    main:
      trust: owner
      sandbox: none
    channel_default:
      trust: untrusted
      sandbox: restricted

  # The health route is declared in web/config/routes.rb, not derived from here.
  ingress:
    health_path: "/ingress/health"

  # Risky tool-call shapes to refuse. Implementing these needs a tool-call risk
  # classifier; the one that existed (lib/cli/routing/risk_classifier.rb) was
  # deleted as an orphan on 2026-07-30 precisely because nothing called it. Do not
  # restore it without deciding who calls it — see TODO.md.
  tools:
    custom:
      enabled: true
      require_scope: true
    deny_patterns:
      - "secret_read_then_network"
      - "broad_delete"
      - "ci_permission_edit"
      - "unknown_package_install"
      - "hidden_generated_file"

`````

### data/self_findings.yml

`````yaml
---
# What MASTER's own rules find in MASTER's own tree, and the four sibling trees.
#
# 172 across 2873 files, from the rules that carry a lexical detector.
#
# The corpus is the whole fleet now. It was MASTER plus the shared libs and the
# gates; the three Rails apps were never measured at all, so amber's 345 source
# files had never been read by a rule in their own repo. Adding them cost the
# ratchet a jump from 1 to 158, and the number is honest for the first time.
#
# By tree, at the time of writing: amber 0, bsdports a handful, brgen the rest.
#
# Generated output is not source and is excluded, which matters more here than
# anywhere else: public/assets alone carried 1361 `var` findings in amber, none
# of them in a file anybody typed. service-worker.js is what `npm run build:pwa`
# emits, and db/schema.rb says in its own first line that it is generated.
#
# Lexical only. The full gate's semantic pass blocks on a model call: measured at
# 17 minutes elapsed against 4 minutes of CPU, idle in a TLS read. A number that
# needs a network and a key is a number nobody has. And no number here moves
# when the tree is restructured: COLLAPSE_BEFORE_ADDING, MERGE_BEFORE_MULTIPLY,
# FLAT_HIERARCHY and NO_NEW_FILES have no detector at all.
#
# Roughly half of every finding this counter has ever reported was the
# instrument rather than the tree, and the laws carry that evidence one by one.
# The two that would have caused damage if believed: RUBY_NUMERIC_UNDERSCORE
# fired inside ffmpeg filter strings, where its fix writes 44_100 into
# sample_rates=44100 and breaks every render; USE_THEN never checked that the
# intermediate is used once, and applying it to its own findings introduced
# three NameErrors. Read the law before acting on the count.
#
# 194 -> 154. Twenty-five of those were one file: brgen's static Dilla Lab page
# aliases document.getElementById to `$`, which is the name jQuery takes, so
# NO_JQUERY read twenty-five getElementById calls as jQuery selectors. The
# alias is gone rather than the law, because a helper wearing the name of the
# library a law forbids is a trap for the next reader as much as for the
# scanner. The remaining fifteen are mechanical and behaviour-identical:
# symbol-to-proc, safe navigation, two numeric literals, and seven runs of
# alignment spaces in MASTER/tools/dilla.
#
# The registry_ keys are the second population, added 2026-09-06. Everything
# above this line is the law: 122 rules in law/, applied file by file. The
# RuleDSL registry is 145 more rules, and nothing in this repo counted what they
# find — the row was labelled "what our own rules find in our own trees" and was
# the law's number alone.
#
# The registry number comes through the scanner rather than through a harness,
# and the difference is large: calling each rule directly on every tracked file
# reads 221 at error severity, the scanner reads 108. PathFilter drops what
# nobody authored and each rule sees only the languages it declares, so the
# harness figure was an upper bound on a question nobody asked.
#
# Error severity only. The same run reports 10,147 warnings and 7,997 info, and
# a ceiling nobody can hold is decoration. The two rows do not overlap: a law
# reaches the scanner through LawBridgeRule under its own id, and those fifteen
# findings are dropped from the registry count because they are already members
# above.
# 147 -> 293 and 51 -> 55 on 2026-09-07, and the jump is a corpus, not a
# regression. MASTER/web joined TREES: the primary product's face — a Rails app,
# the WebGL runtime's five source parts, the chat surface — 164 tracked source
# files that no census had ever read. This list started at MASTER's Ruby
# directories and web was never added; rule_audit reaches "a little web JS" and
# measures blindness rather than findings.
#
# The tell was in the silent laws. rule_audit reports rules that fire on
# nothing, and five of its twenty-four — FOR_OF, TEMPLATE_LITERALS, ASYNC_AWAIT,
# FACE_POINT_IS_ONE_PIXEL and NO_JQUERY — have their subject in MASTER/web and
# nowhere else. Five laws written for the face were enforced against no file at
# all, and the count that would have said so was the count that could not see
# them.
#
# The face's build output is excluded rather than counted: face.runtime.js,
# face.modules.bundle.js, face_vision.bundle.js and three.face.module.js are
# 12,019 lines of generated JavaScript that Scanner::PathFilter has always
# skipped by name, and they arrived here as 255 findings about code nobody
# typed until THIRD_PARTY learned them.
#
# What the 146 new law findings are: NULLISH_COALESCING 24, NO_COLUMN_ALIGN 42,
# NO_MULTIPLE_LANGUAGES 17, NO_INLINE_SCRIPT_BLOCK 15, and a long tail. The
# registry's four are three NO_GOD_CLASS in the web app's controllers and
# services, plus one more. Two findings it also turned up were the instrument
# and are fixed rather than recorded: COMPLETION_THEATER read a CSS comment and
# a JS comment as placeholders, because its comment stripper knew `#` and not
# `//` or `/* */`; STALE_NAMESPACE read a comment explaining that
# "Fiber[:master_visitor] is set when a Master::CLI is built" as a use of a
# retired constant. A comment cannot resolve a constant.
#
# 54 -> 56 on the registry row, and like the jump above it is the instrument
# rather than the tree. NO_GOD_CLASS judged one AST node at a time, so a class
# written as a scaffold and reopened — `class Propose; end` at the top of the
# file, the methods in a second block below — was measured twice at half its
# size. The rule graded source layout, and it graded it backwards: the more
# scattered the file, the more lenient the verdict. Summing the blocks by the
# class's full lexical name adds no method-count finding anywhere in the corpus
# and two line-count findings, both true and both previously invisible:
# Master::CLI::Propose is 447 code lines across two blocks and
# Master::Review::RepoEcology 354 across three, against a limit of 300. They are
# recorded rather than exempted, and TODO.md names them as the decompositions
# they are.
# 279 -> 278, and the line is the instrument rather than the tree.
#
# A comment leader reads one line, so law.rb saw where a comment opened and
# never where it continued. An ERB comment here is routinely six lines of prose
# about the markup below it, and every line after the first was read as markup:
# I18N_COVERAGE fired on a comment explaining that a page carried no <h1>,
# because "<h1> at all — two <h2>s" is a `>`, English text and a `<`. The rule
# already refused the opening line and had no way to refuse the rest. Blanking
# the whole `<%# ... %>` span dropped that finding and one NO_INLINE_SCRIPT_BLOCK
# of the same shape, and the detector still fires on markup that follows the
# comment's close — proved on planted cases before the count was believed.
#
# 273 -> 272 on 2026-09-12. One MOBILE_FIRST finding, the last of eighteen in
# RAILS. Fourteen of those carried a marker exempting them from the law; the
# operator ruled the law wins, so seventeen queries were inverted to min-width
# and the eighteenth does not match the detector. rule_audit.silent rose to 40
# in the same pass and for the same reason, which is the trade that row's own
# comment describes.
#
# 233 and 46 measured a tree this one is not. 62000dad0 says so in its own
# message — "the corpus is 2988 files rather than 3182 since RAILS/gates left
# the tree" — and that deletion was reverted by 3dc68629f, which the rebase put
# underneath it. So the last numbers taken over the whole fleet are 66d45f9a2's
# 241 and 49, and those are what this pass is measured against.
#
# 241 -> 230, fourteen findings out and three in, read by diffing the members
# rather than the integers. Out: six NO_COLUMN_ALIGN and two NULLISH_COALESCING
# went with codebase.js; one NULLISH_COALESCING and one I18N_COVERAGE were fixed
# in place; two IMMUTABLE, one NO_MULTIPLE_LANGUAGES and one PROSE_ACTIVE_VOICE
# are RAILS/gates answering its own laws — runner.rb's two mutated constants are
# instance variables, shell_loop_record's per-frame JS is a constant heredoc
# beside the two it already had, and page_simulation's skip-link comment is
# active. In: dilla.rb's at_exit scratch sweep (NEVER_BATCH_DELETE, correct —
# it removes this process's own temporary takes), a passive clause in dilla's
# album comment, and findable_by_slug's worked example.
#
# 49 is where registry was before the deletion, and it holds: livesets read
# sample_worth.json two ways, so one file had two rescues to get wrong; `worth`
# goes through `worth_doc`, which is the read `starred` and `star!` already use.
findings: 230
by_rule:
  BARE_DIV_WRAPPER: 2
  BLANK_LINE_RUN: 1
  GUARD_CLAUSE: 27
  I18N_COVERAGE: 8
  MEANINGFUL_NAMES: 1
  MIGRATION_REMOVE_COLUMN: 1
  NEVER_BATCH_DELETE: 1
  NO_CHANGELOG_COMMENT: 15
  NO_COLUMN_ALIGN: 23
  NO_INLINE_SCRIPT_BLOCK: 15
  NO_INLINE_STYLES: 1
  NO_MULTIPLE_LANGUAGES: 22
  NULLISH_COALESCING: 72
  OPTIONAL_CHAINING: 2
  PROSE_ACTIVE_VOICE: 5
  PROSE_ACTIVE_VOICE_NB: 1
  PROSE_OMIT_QUALIFIERS: 18
  RUBY_NUMERIC_UNDERSCORE: 3
  SAFE_NAVIGATION: 1
  SQUINT_TEST: 2
  USE_THEN: 7
  WHY_NOT_WHAT: 2
finding_members:
  - BARE_DIV_WRAPPER RAILS/brgen/public/dilla/dilla.html:35
  - BARE_DIV_WRAPPER RAILS/brgen/public/dilla/dilla.html:45
  - BLANK_LINE_RUN MASTER/web/app/views/chat/index.html.erb:1
`````

`````yaml
# soul.yml — machine-enforced constitutional schema
# Human-readable narrative lives in SOUL.md.
# ABSOLUTE sections require constitutional override to amend.
# Negotiable sections: soul propose -> soul approve -> bump version.

schema: 1
version: "2.8.0"
persona: anchor
voice: en-US-JennyNeural
language:
  primary: english
  secondary: norwegian
  # English spoken with an American accent. Operator decision 2026-09-12.
  #
  # primary stays english — the words are English; what changed is the mouth.
  # en-US-JennyNeural is an English (United States) neural voice, so `dialect`
  # names the accent it speaks in rather than a variety of English with its own
  # spelling and idiom.
  #
  # This block used to say primary: english while the voice was nb-NO and the
  # dialect was bokmal, so the law described a Norwegian speaker and an English
  # one at once. The three have been kept in step since; they still are.
  dialect: american

research:
  constitutional_ai:
    - https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2212.06719  # Constitutional AI / Anthropic
    - https://github.com/anthropic-ai/constitution-ai
  code_governance:
    - https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2104.07896  # Code Review Best Practices
    - https://github.com/google/styleguide
  linter_patterns:
    - https://github.com/golangci/golangci-lint
    - https://github.com/github/super-linter
  ruby_governance:
    - https://github.com/ruby-on-rails/rails
    - https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop

prompt_ordering:
  - master_identity
  - master_output_format
  - master_meta_instruction
  - master_constitution_absolute
  - master_priority
  - master_constitution_kernel
  # add_disclaimer builds one of these two per persona, and neither was ordered,
  # so ordered_sections dropped both: a medic's standing medical disclaimer and
  # any persona's own. The builder logged it as load-bearing on every boot and
  # nothing read the log. They sit with the refusal policy because all three
  # constrain what the reply may say.
  - master_medical_disclaimer
  - master_special_disclaimer
  - master_refusal_policy
  - master_attention
  - master_style

absolute:
  golden_rule: PRESERVE_THEN_IMPROVE_NEVER_BREAK
  severity_rank: { info: 0, warning: 1, error: 2, critical: 3 }
  sacred_paths:
    - data/
    - data/SOUL.md
    - data/project_context.yml
    - lib/review/scan/
    - bin/cli
  anti_simulation:
    forbidden: [will, would, could, might]
    require_evidence:
      file_read: show content with SHA-256
      modification: show unified diff
      completion: show command output
  protection_tiers:
    ABSOLUTE: abort pipeline
    PROTECTED: emit warning continue
    NEGOTIABLE: allow if explicitly permitted
    FLEXIBLE: negotiate at runtime
# No rules here. All 47 moved to law/practice.rb, which is the one registry:
# 117 rules, each declaring how it is checked — `detect` for a regex, `ask`
# for a question a model answers, `conduct` for a rule about how to work.
#
# They were here because Law::Builder required a detector and none can exist
# for "sweep to convergence" or "one SSH session", so the requirement was
# excluding exactly the rules it could not describe. soul keeps what only
# soul has: the golden rule, sacred paths, anti-simulation, protection tiers.
negotiable:
  style: sentence_case
  # default_model lives once, in providers.yml openrouter.default_model —
  # the copy that stood here had no reader and could only drift.
  tts_voice: en-US-JennyNeural
  language_detection: true
  conflict_resolution:
    strategy: highest_priority_wins
    prompt_user: false

hooks:
  - event: on_violation_found
    action: append_constitutional_violation
    params:
      path: .constitutional_violations.jsonl
  - event: on_fix_applied
    action: publish
    params:
      event: hooks:fix_applied
  - event: on_cost_threshold
    action: warn_cost_threshold
    params:
      warn_at: 0.5
  - event: on_session_start
    action: publish
    params:
      event: hooks:session_start
  - event: on_session_end
    action: publish
    params:
      event: hooks:session_end
  - event: on_phase_transition
    action: publish
    params:
      event: hooks:phase_transition
  - event: on_convergence
    action: publish
    params:
      event: hooks:convergence

evolution_log:
  - version: "2.8.0"
    date: "2026-08-31"
    change: order the two disclaimer sections — the builder built them and prompt_ordering dropped them, so no persona disclaimer ever reached a model
    author: dev
  - version: "2.7.0"
    date: "2026-08-18"
    change: rename absolute.code_rules to absolute.rules — laws and rules are one kind of thing, and a third name for it was noise
    author: dev
  - version: "2.6.0"
    date: "2026-06-28"
    change: add schema pinning and canonical severity ranking
    author: codex
  - version: "1.0.0"
    date: "2026-04-01"
    change: initial SOUL.md constitutional identity
    author: dev
  - version: "2.0.0"
    date: "2026-04-24"
    change: OpenClaw-inspired restructure
    author: dev
  - version: "2.1.0"
    date: "2026-04-27"
    change: restored from sweep corruption
    author: dev
  - version: "2.2.0"
    date: "2026-05-05"
    change: native rubocop autocorrect pre-pass; scanner split into parallel_each, scan_one, stream_progress
`````

`````yaml
# The spine ratchet. `rake lint:spine` fails when lib/ grows past the ceiling,
# and equally when lib/ falls below it and the ceiling was not lowered to match:
# slack the next change grows into is the same defect as debt. This file is the
# reader that keeps the invariant from being decoration.
#
# Two claims, and they are different kinds of number:
#   - core_files is the real invariant. It counts lib/core.rb and lib/core/*.rb,
#     the entrypoint beside the directory, so a glob of lib/core/ alone does not
#     hand out a free concept. A new top-level concept in the fold is a design
#     change, argued for here — not a line-count question, and never a file
#     added because something felt long.
#   - lib_body_ceiling is a budget with a sponsor. It may be raised, but only in
#     a commit that names what the lines buy, and consecutive_raises_allowed
#     caps how many raises may stand before a genuine fall earns the budget
#     back. Raising it to absorb another change's unaccounted growth is how a
#     ceiling stops measuring anything — a good reason is always available,
#     which is why the number needs teeth rather than prose.
#
# The ceiling only falls on its own: `rake lint:spine RATCHET=1` records a new
# low when lib/ shrinks. Raising it is a deliberate edit here. Every raise and
# ratchet is a commit — the history reads there, not in this file.
#
# Body lines are code lines minus Zeitwerk ceremony: a `module` whose body is
# exactly one module or class, and its matching `end`, which map a path to a
# constant and carry no implementation. Counting them would set this ratchet
# against lint:cohesion, which asks for those wrappers. The counter is
# Master::Review::Scan::CodeMetrics.body_lines, shared with lint:spine and
# SmallFunctionsRule so the repo counts code exactly one way.

# by 2,100 in one evening while fourteen were verified by hand; of those, three

# claim. 5,024 of 5,741 name no file this repo owns, 23 name only files that

# pwa_master_contract_test greps the ERB and pwa_offline_test covers the
# offline page, so the two content types went unmeasured. Both are
# load-bearing and invisible in a template — a manifest served as text/html
# installs nothing, and a worker served as anything but JavaScript is refused
# with a console error no deploy sees. It also pins the rescue path, which
# answers with a minimal installing worker rather than a 500, because a 500
# there leaves whatever is installed in place with no way to replace it.
# 2393 -> 2394 for shared/_site_legal.scss. The legal footer carried its type
# system as an inline style element in a partial all three layouts render, so a
# second type system shipped on every page of every app and NO_INLINE_STYLES
# had a finding it could not act on. Five separate passes through TODO.md
# reached that same paragraph independently, which is what a real defect looks
# like from outside.
#
# The move changes nothing a reader sees, and that was the point: measured on
# brgen.no/privacy before and after, .legal-prose is 724.397px wide with
# 32px 20px 64px of padding and its h1 is 28.8px/33.12px either way. The values
# are off this tree's scales — 1.6rem, 1.62 and .12em are on no list in
# design_tokens — and snapping them is a separate decision, because every one
# of those numbers is something somebody sees.
  # 2394 -> 2393, a fall. gates/data/page_sim_inventory.yml and
  # page_sim_report.yml left the index: gates/data/.gitignore already named both
  # under "Outputs, not baselines -- keep out of git", and both were tracked
  # anyway, so every page_simulation run dirtied a shared checkout. Nothing reads
  # them. This row is what caught the first attempt not landing -- it read 2395
  # while the branch claimed the removal, because a path-scoped commit rebuilds
  # its paths from the working tree and put them back.
  # 1980 -> 1932, a fall. Each Rails app compiles from one application.scss, so
  # 72 partials left the index and Operator::ScssRules joined it.
  # 1932 -> 1983: retired reference app adds 51 tracked source/docs files. The pre-existing
  # 47-file overage remains visible; only the named ERITEL addition is paid for.
  RAILS: 1983
  # 106 -> 107 is test/test_githooks.rb. dev/githooks holds the three guards
  # that are the whole defence against a shared index, and nothing tested any of
  # them — a hook that stopped firing looks exactly like a week in which nobody
  # made the mistake. It runs all three through real git in a throwaway
  # repository, because a hook is installed behaviour: a unit test of its logic
  # would not catch a lost chmod or a core.hooksPath pointing elsewhere. It
  # folds into no existing OPENBSD test; every one of those is about the box.
  # 107 -> 108 is test/test_config_drift_gate.rb. The drift gate compared
  # eighteen files, found every one identical, and reported the box clean while
  # a root cron job existed only in the repo — a gate whose blind spot was
  # invisible precisely because it passed. The rewrite that taught it to compare
  # root's crontab as a set of commands needs a test that fails when that
  # comparison is dropped again, and no existing OPENBSD test boots a gate.
  # 111 -> 110: dotfiles/mov.sh left the repo. 2,343 lines of torrent-and-
  # transcode, the largest shell file here, and nothing to do with vm23 — the
  # owner's dotfile, kept because moving it was framed as a growth argument
  # rather than a decision. It was also the single heaviest source of scan
  # findings in the tree, 535 of them, which is what a file nobody deploys and
  # nobody tests contributes to every census that reads the repo.
# 110 -> 111 for test/test_rc_env_export.rb. An rc.d script that sources an env
# file must export it: `.` sets a bare KEY=value unexported, so naming keys
# after it is an allowlist nobody can see. rc.d/brgen carries what that cost —
# VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY sat in /etc/brgen.env for hours while push failed silently —
# and was fixed with `set -a`. The three job workers were not, and they are
# where it matters most, since the classes they run want those same keys. All
# three had it wrong on 2026-09-11, which is what a fix applied to one file of
# a family looks like a month later. It folds into no existing OPENBSD test;
# those are about the box, and this is about the shape of a script.
# 111 -> 112 for test/test_guard_thresholds_documented.rb. OPENBSD/CLAUDE.md
# said "thresholds are now 8/14" for a month after resource_guard.sh moved
# MEM_RESTORE from 14 to 10 on 2026-08-14 — a recalibration the script records
# in full, with the 1550-tick dataset behind it. Anyone reading the doc to
# judge whether the guard was tuned right was reading a number the running code
# had abandoned, and this is the second time that same threshold drifted.
#
# The test allows the doc to name a threshold and refuses to let it name a
# different one from the script, skipping sentences that carry a date because
# those recount what a value WAS. It folds into no existing OPENBSD test:
# test_config_drift_gate compares the box against the repo, and this compares
# the repo's prose against the repo's code.
# 112 -> 113 for shell_syntax_gate.rb. check-openbsd named two shell scripts by
# hand out of 43 and ran zsh -n on both. The deploy path was not among them:
# bin/vps-deploy, vps_ci.sh and deploy_all.sh are what a deploy actually runs, so
# a syntax error in any of the three was discovered by the deploy. resource_guard.sh
# is ksh and a zsh list could not have covered it at all.
#
# The gate reads each script's shebang, which is both the complete set and the
# right parser per file, and a script added tomorrow is covered by having a
# shebang rather than by somebody remembering a list. It replaces the two lines
# it supersedes, so check-openbsd got shorter. All 43 parse today.
# 113 -> 114 for test/test_dns_facts_agree.rb. Four DNS facts were written down
# twice and had already drifted: OPERATOR.sh led its resolver list with 8.8.8.8
# while gates/dns_zones.rb used Cloudflare and Quad9 and had written down why.
# The nameserver IP was a third literal in the gate that checks the delegation
# data/dns.yml renders, so the gate could have passed on both halves of a
# disagreement with the zones it was checking.
#
# The gate reads the policy file now. OPERATOR.sh cannot: its constants are
# sourced before anything runs, and making the deploy script shell out to ruby34
# to boot would put it behind an interpreter it installs. The duplication stays
# and this test is what it costs.
# 114 -> 115 for test/test_vps_deploy_contract.rb. bin/vps-deploy is the
# entrypoint for every production deploy and had no test at all. Running it is
# not an option, so this reads the source for the three promises a reader cannot
# otherwise check: that DEPLOY_ALL is apps.yml plus master, that the order which
# makes the pass survive its own side effects is still that order, and that the
# uid guard exits rather than warns.
#
# Mutation-checked rather than asserted into existence: dropping master fails 2,
# reordering fails 1, turning the root guard into a warning fails 1, and gutting
# the SKIP_CI branch fails 1, with the unmutated source at 0.
# 98 -> 90, locked 2026-09-25. eef2c0afe folded ten console .exp files into
# vps_console.exp and removed bin/tree.sh, whose caller runs tools/tree.rb.
  # 90 -> 92: retired reference deployment adds README.md and bin/preflight.ksh. No other
  # source growth is absorbed by this raise.
  OPENBSD: 92
  # 2026-09-30: STUDIO is restored as the governed media tree. The move transfers
  # 243 source files out of MASTER/tools into STUDIO; the ceiling records that
  # exact observed population and absorbs no additional growth.
  STUDIO: 243
  # 220 -> 222 for lora/seed_media.yml and lora/_toolkit/install_seed_media.rb,
  # the prompt set for every seeded photograph and the script that grades and
  # files what comes back from it. Two files, both named, neither foldable:
  # the prompts are data and the installer is the only thing that writes a
  # catalogue row.
  #
  # This deliberately leaves STUDIO one over. That one is not mine --
  # lib/engine/album_signature.rb is untracked, so raising for it would fit
  # the ceiling to a file nobody has landed.
  # 222 -> 224 for lora/_toolkit/run_seed_media_colab.rb and the seed_media.ipynb
  # it generates. The notebook is committed because Colab opens a notebook from a
  # public repo URL and cannot be handed one any other way, and the generator is
  # committed because the notebook says edits belong in it.
  # 224 -> 138 is a fall, not a raise, and it is the largest one this file has
  # recorded. dilla's engine folded from lib/engine/ into dilla.rb — 81 parts to
  # one file, 129 ruby files to 48 — and the ceiling was never lowered to match,
  # so STUDIO has been carrying 86 files of room the next change could grow into
  # without argument. That is the defect the note at the top of this file names,
  # measured rather than argued: `test_no_ratchet_is_slack` had never reported
  # it, because it skips on a dirty tree and this checkout is always dirty.
  #
  # Recorded from a clean worktree at 1bcb58524, which is the condition that
  # assertion asks for. The next STUDIO file now fails `measure` on the day it
  # is written and wants a named raise here — which is the point, and is what
  # 224 had stopped doing.
  # 138 -> 150 for twelve, in two halves. Six predate the fold that set 138 and
  # were never accounted for: dilla/lib/sample_worth.rb, dilla/scripts/generate_tts.rb
  # and four in dilla/live/ (broadcast.sh, dig_crate.rb, dig_crate.sh, synth.rb).
  # Six more since: live/ambient_pads.als.rb, chord_based_beats.als.rb,
  # sampled_based_beats.als.rb, rack.rb and recall.rb -- the Ableton-facing surface,
  # where a file per project shape is the shape -- plus lora/_toolkit/toolkit.sh,
  # against synth.rb, _toolkit/lib.sh and one fixture removed. Three of the twelve
  # are dilla tests: test_dilla_crate_dig.rb, test_dilla_radio_bergen_study.rb and
  # test_dilla_take_write.rb.
  #
  # dilla/live/ is eight files now and reads like one subject. Folding it is the
  # obvious win and it is not mine to take: these render real audio and this repo
  # says not to reshape a rendering tool on an outsider's judgement. It belongs to
  # the owner, and it is in TODO.md so the next person sees the same eight.
  # 150 -> 149 folds dilla/lib/spectral_audit_run.rb into spectral_audit.rb behind
  # the $PROGRAM_NAME guard MASTER's own tools use. The runner was a second file
  # whose only caller was the usage line in its own header -- nothing in the repo
  # named it -- and the pair is 132 code lines together. It was also the one file
  # in dilla/lib declaring no module or class, so `namespace` falls with it.
  # 149 -> 153 for four files in dilla, and what they buy:
  #
  #   lib/improvisation.rb   twelve progressions the engine writes itself, in
  #                          five composers' languages. It replaced a catalogue
  #                          of 575 with one of 19, so the tree it grew is
  #                          smaller than the tree it left.
  #   lib/improvised_line.rb a lead and a bass generated from the chords, shared
  #                          by the render path and the live one so a take you
  #                          hear is the take you keep.
  #   lib/space_fx.rb        reverb, tape echo, phaser, chorus and a wave folder
  #                          as arithmetic, because live playback never becomes
  #                          a file and has nothing to hand ffmpeg.
  #
  # Three subjects and an entry point, not one subject split four ways: the
  # first writes music, the second plays over it, the third knows nothing about
  # music at all. MASTER/tools/gate.rb's DILLA_SUPPORT_CEILING carries the same
  # reasoning for the same three modules.
  # 153 -> 148, a fall. CATALOGUE.md arrived from TODO.md and six files left:
  # a test asserting render_rand, a method the engine has never defined, and
  # five the sweep found dead. A catalogue of livesets is dilla's work and
  # belongs beside the three sets it was written after.
  # 148 -> 145: the trymbot skin is retired. It was one deletable file by
  # design — the same MASTER process wearing a different host — plus its README
  # and its test, and MASTER/tools/gate.rb no longer registers a subsystem that is not
  # there.
  # 145 -> 143, a fall nobody recorded. postpro/motion.rb and
  # test/test_tools_motion.rb went and the ceiling stayed, so the row sat two
  # files slack -- room the next change grows into without an argument, which is
  # the other way a ratchet dies.
  # dilla/bin, dilla/live and dilla/scripts are gone. The three livesets, recall,
  # the broadcast loop and the bed digger are lib/livesets.rb behind
  # `dilla.rb live`; the sine stream and its player are lib/sine_stream.rb;
  # bin/crate, bin/demo_full.rb, scripts/generate_tts.rb and the librosa script
  # left with nothing reading them. MASTER/tools/gate.rb fails if any of the three
  # directories returns. 117 -> 108.
  # 108 -> 70: dilla lib/ folds forty-four modules into six subjects -- sound,
  # sampling, ledger, harmony, groove, listen -- and radio_bergen_study.rb, a
  # wrapper round a command dilla.rb already had, is gone.
  # 70 -> 69: dilla_live.rb is `ruby dilla.rb live`, and the old live command,
  # which looped a cached render, gave its name to it.
  # 2026-09-25: STUDIO was consolidated into MASTER/tools. Transfer exactly its
  # 69-file allowance into MASTER (646 + 69 = 715); do not absorb any additional
  # growth into this migration. The merged tree currently measures above that
  # ceiling, so the unexplained remainder stays visible to the next /fix pass.

# Executable files directly under each tree's own bin/ — the number CLAUDE.md's
# "two surfaces, no third" makes a claim about while nothing counted it. MASTER
# reached 28 without a single failure, because prose in a doc is not an
# instrument. Twelve of those overlap on "check things": check, gate, ci, audit,
# dogfood, preflight, probe, smoke, smoke-web, doctor, nsaudit, and test-safety
# until it folded into `bin/check --profile=ci`'s superset.
#
# Directly under bin/, so an app's generated bin/rails and a tool's own bin/
# scripts are not counted as surfaces of the tree. The canonical tools now live
# under MASTER/tools and are exercised through MASTER's tool suite rather than
# counted as top-level entrypoint surfaces.
#
# A ceiling at the honest count rather than at the two the prose asks for: a
# target nobody can reach is a ratchet everyone learns to override. It falls as
# they collapse, and a new script fails `bin/operator measure` until somebody argues
# for it here.
#
# 28 -> 27 folds bin/test-safety away. It ran 21 hand-picked spec files from no
# caller anywhere in the repo, 20 of them already inside `rake spec`'s FileList
# and the 21st naming test/test_io_catalog_index.rb, which moved to
# spec/io/ in the lib rename — so every invocation aborted, and nothing noticed
# because nothing invoked it. Its one reader was a bin/doctor check asserting
# the file exists, which went with it.
#
# 27 -> 26 folds bin/preflight away. It checked ruby, bundler, `bundle check`
# and three API keys — each already a bin/doctor check — then `ruby -c
# lib/master.rb` and a kernel/ directory the tree has not had for some time,
# then ran bin/ci. Its only caller anywhere was bin/probe's own table, so it was
# doctor and ci wearing a third name, and the syntax check it added cannot fail
# without bin/ci failing first: loading the runtime is the suite's first act.
# `bin/probe all` names ci directly in its place. Not doctor, though doctor is
# the strict superset of preflight's host checks: doctor is red on a laptop with
# no TTS socket, and a probe that fails on every developer's box is a line people
# learn to skip.
# Names that say which drawer a thing lives in rather than what it holds, and
# names that repeat the namespace they sit in. `ruby MASTER/tools/rename.rb`
# lists them, with the shorter name where that name is free.
#
# A ceiling rather than a ban, because the proposal is the easy half. Dropping
# a category suffix is mechanical; deciding that Shared::DillaProcessor should
# be Shared::Dilla is not, and it should not be — that class processes dilla's
# output and does not stand for dilla. So this number falls by a rename or by
# an argument written beside the name, and rises by neither.
# Every name a person or a model can type: the CLI's closed table, the words the
# router accepts as the pipeline, and bin/operator's subcommands. An alias is a
# name — `through workflow triad sweep scan fix self critique council review` is
# ten words for one pass, and five slash names resolve to two stages.
#
# Counted for the same reason files are: adding a verb costs no file, moves no
# other ceiling, and each one is a thing the next reader has to learn before
# they can be sure which of them writes.
command_surface: 35

name_candidates: 23

# UNIT CHANGED 2026-09-16: bin/ and the tree's own root, not bin/ alone.
#
# The old reading measured a directory rather than a tree, and a move proved it.
# f754501d1 carried 27 operator scripts from OPENBSD's root into OPENBSD/bin and
# this row went 16 to 43 without a script being written. Those 27 had always been
# doors; the census had never opened the directory they sat in. OPENBSD's root
# held 33 executables at that commit, so the honest count before the move was 49
# and after it is 46 — a fall of three, because deploy_smoke_gate, integrity_gate
# and solid_queue_proof went to gates/, and a gate is run by a check rather than
# typed. Three still sit at the OPENBSD root because vm23 runs them from the
# checkout by path: backup_priv.sh, emergency_cpu.sh and ptr_openbsd_amsterdam.rb.
#
# RAILS 2 -> 3 is the same blindness, not a door: RAILS/deploy.sh has sat at that
# root the whole time. MASTER and STUDIO are unchanged, having nothing at theirs.
#
# Still only those two levels. An app's generated bin/rails, a tool's own bin/
# and OPENBSD/usr/local/bin — a mirror of what is installed on vm23 rather than
# anything run from the checkout — are not surfaces the tree offers.
#
# MASTER 26 -> 20, locked 2026-09-23. Seven doors folded by their own commits
# since the 26 lock: audit (52b2fd940, /commit takes paths and bin tests run
# processes), handoff, onboard, playbook, reset-costs, sync-env and
# tts-bootstrap, each commit naming its fold and most of them unused wrappers.
# pub4 became operator on the two-surface decision (b9daa7fd1) — a rename, not
# a fall — and loops joined for the boot film (3959c382e). Net -6, read from
# the census, not from the fold count.
#
# OPENBSD 46 -> 45, locked 2026-09-23. 7452c9837 collapsed the deploy gates
# into one file and bin/vps_deploy_master.sh lost its executable bit — no
# caller ever typed it as a door; every one reaches it through `zsh <path>`
# (agent_map.yml, ssh_vm23.sh), and a script run through another shell is not
# a surface the tree offers. The only net door change since f754501d1 set the
# post-move census at 46.
#
# OPENBSD 45 -> 34, locked 2026-09-25. eef2c0afe: nine executable console
# shims became modes of vps_console.exp, their sourced helper folded in, and
# bin/tree.sh went, since its callers run tools/tree.rb.
pub4_entrypoint_ceilings:
  MASTER: 20
  RAILS: 3
  OPENBSD: 34
`````

### data/state.yml

`````yaml
---
# State — standing orders (event and manual triggers) wired through StandingOrders.
# trigger: event  — fires when bus publishes event: key (currently tool:after)
# trigger: manual — only runs when explicitly called via /orders or its callable
# Every entry needs a callable: key registered in Master::Ground::Orders::Registry.
# Runtime state (state/last_run_at/last_error) lives in .master/standing_orders_state.yml.

- name: architecture_audit
  description: Review data/* for shape misfit (files >200 lines, overlapping keys, misnamed modules). Run via /audit architecture.
  trigger: manual
  command: audit architecture
  callable: architecture_audit
  enabled: true

- name: aggressive_merge
  description: After source writes, scan for merge/rename targets — thin siblings, *_support sprawl, low-density slugs. Rename to Rails-parameterize snake_case (Strunk-clean tokens); default merge before multiply.
  trigger: event
  event: "tool:after"
  filter: "write_file|str_replace|ast_edit|replace"
  exclude: "test/|knowledge/|node_modules/"
  callable: aggressive_merge
  enabled: true

- name: constitution_drift
  description: Scan lib/ against the axioms after any source mutation; emit improved/regressed/steady so regressions are caught the moment they land.
  trigger: event
  event: "tool:after"
  filter: "write_file|str_replace|ast_edit|replace"
  exclude: "data/|test/|knowledge/"
  command: audit constitution
  callable: constitution_drift
  # Disabled: fires a full deep-scan of lib/ on every source write — the exact
  # repo-wide scan HostBudget exists to prevent from OOM-killing the 1GB VPS.
  # The per-write job belongs to Review::Scan::WriteGuard, which judges one file
  # before it lands. What is left here is the tree-wide trend line, and it runs
  # from the boot path under MASTER_DRIFT=1.
  enabled: false

- name: autocommit_post_chat
  description: After any turn that mutated source, generate a Strunk-style commit message and commit.
  trigger: event
  event: "tool:after"
  filter: "write_file|str_replace|ast_edit|replace"
  command: git autocommit
  callable: autocommit
  # Disabled: would auto-commit AND push to the repo after every source-mutating
  # turn. Opt in deliberately rather than have edits push themselves.
  enabled: false

- name: backup_repo_offsite
  description: openrsync the repo root to wingman1.openbsd.amsterdam:backup over SSH.
  trigger: manual
  callable: backup
  # Disabled: pushes the entire working tree to a remote host. Every other
  # callable in the registry is declared here; this one was the exception, so
  # `callable: backup` resolved to nothing. Declared now so it is reachable and
  # visible in data/state.yml — turn it on deliberately, not by default.
  enabled: false

- name: restart_master_on_web_edit
  description: Restart MASTER service when web/ files change so edits take effect immediately.
  trigger: event
  event: "tool:after"
  filter: "web/"
  command: doas rcctl restart master
  callable: restart_master
  enabled: true

- name: availability_posture
  description: Report the interactive capability floor and reachable model ladder without mutating runtime state.
  trigger: heartbeat
  interval_s: 120
  command: status availability
  callable: availability_posture
  enabled: true

`````
