### data/tools.yml

`````yaml
# Tool registry — declarative metadata for built-in tools. The adapters are the
# classes lib/builder.rb's DEFAULT_TOOL_MAP builds, which live in lib/io/; this
# file supplies exposure, visibility and boot state. Operators tune which
# tools a model is handed without editing code.
#
# `elevated` is exposure, not approval. Each adapter's TIER constant (safe,
# guarded, dangerous, open) is what Fix::Governor paces and asks about once a
# tool is called; `elevated` decides whether an unelevated model is handed the
# tool at all. WebFetch is guarded and not elevated: any session may fetch, and
# the governor rate-limits it.
#
# Schema:
#   name        — adapter class name (under Master::Io)
#   elevated    — true withholds the tool from a model until the session is elevated
#   visitor     — true if visitors can call (visitor allow-list)
#   default     — true to enable on boot; false leaves it off until /enable
#   file_types  — optional list of file extensions that should activate the tool
#   description — one-line, surfaced in tool list

---
- { name: AskLlm, elevated: false, visitor: true, default: true, description: Sub-LLM call for nested reasoning, required_context: "A specific sub-question and optional context.", usage_rules: ["Use for isolated reasoning that should not pollute current context."], error_recovery: "If too broad, rewrite as one concrete question." }
- { name: ReadFile, elevated: false, visitor: false, default: true, description: Read a file from disk, required_context: "Specific file path.", usage_rules: ["Never guess path names.", "Read before modifying related files."], error_recovery: "If missing, ask for exact path or run directory listing first." }
- { name: WriteFile, elevated: true, visitor: false, default: true, description: Write a new file, required_context: "Target path and complete content.", usage_rules: ["Prefer patch-like edits when file exists.", "Keep writes minimal and reversible."], error_recovery: "If uncertain, read the file first and propose a diff." }
- { name: StrReplace, elevated: true, visitor: false, default: true, description: Replace exact string in a file, required_context: "Exact unique old string and replacement.", usage_rules: ["Fail if old string is ambiguous."], error_recovery: "If multiple matches, refine old_string with more context." }
- { name: BatchReplace, elevated: true, visitor: false, default: true, description: Replace many files in one call }
- { name: AstEdit, elevated: true, visitor: false, default: true, file_types: [".rb"], description: Prism AST-aware Ruby edit }
- { name: Tree, elevated: false, visitor: false, default: true, description: Directory tree summary }
- { name: ListDir, elevated: false, visitor: false, default: true, description: List a single directory }
- { name: SearchFiles, elevated: false, visitor: false, default: true, description: Glob/grep file search }
- { name: SearchKnowledge, elevated: false, visitor: false, default: true, description: Search knowledge/ snapshots }
- { name: SymbolLookup, elevated: false, visitor: false, default: true, description: Look up symbol via code_index }
- { name: Shell, elevated: true, visitor: false, default: true, description: Execute zsh command, required_context: "Concrete command and expected effect.", usage_rules: ["Prefer read-only commands first.", "Never use destructive commands without explicit confirmation."], error_recovery: "If blocked or risky, suggest safer equivalent command." }
- { name: GitContext, elevated: false, visitor: false, default: true, description: git status/log summary }
- { name: WebFetch, elevated: false, visitor: false, default: true, description: Fetch URL content }
- { name: WebSearch, elevated: false, visitor: true, default: true, description: Web search (visitor allowed) }
- { name: Clean, elevated: true, visitor: false, default: true, description: Remove tmp/build artifacts }
- { name: FeedbackRecord, elevated: false, visitor: false, default: true, description: Record a tool, provider or correction outcome in the feedback ledger }
- { name: MemoryRecord, elevated: false, visitor: false, default: true, description: Append durable context to data/project_context.yml }
- { name: SubdomainOrchestrator, elevated: false, visitor: true, default: true, description: "Inspect or synchronize a pub4 subdomain cluster (marketplace, maps, amber, bsdports, etc.)" }
- { name: PluginObserve, elevated: false, visitor: false, default: true, description: "Observe declared read-only plugin capabilities without granting plugin write authority", required_context: "Plugin id, declared observation action, and optional JSON arguments.", usage_rules: ["Use for browser or local-device observation when the evidence router identifies that capability.", "Never treat it as permission to send, post, remember, or otherwise mutate external state."], error_recovery: "Use status first when capability or runtime is unclear." }
- { name: DynamicHttp, elevated: false, visitor: false, default: true, description: Call HTTP endpoints declared in data/tools.dynamic.yml (name + params) }
# Postpro and Replicate are not adapters: Io::MediaIntent routes them through MASTER/tools.

`````

### data/topologies.yml

`````yaml
# reader: Master::Ground::RuntimeCatalog
# Canonical topologies for the Pixel Field. Each topology names a renderable
# semantic shape — face, codebase, ecology, attention. The registry consumes
# this file at boot; particle_kernel.js renders cells per topology rules.

event_classifier:
  - { pattern: "phantom:(detected|occurrence|recovery|halt)",         topology: ecology, entropy: 0.88, confidence: 0.18, mode: phantom }
  - { pattern: "compaction:(start|done)",                 topology: ecology, entropy: 0.42, confidence: 0.62, mode: compact }
  - { pattern: "pipeline:stage|skills:triggered",         topology: face,    entropy: 0.30, confidence: 0.80, mode: stage }
  - { pattern: "ctx:footer",                             topology: ecology, entropy: 0.22, confidence: 0.84, mode: ctx }
  - { pattern: "agent:end",                              topology: face,    entropy: 0.36, confidence: 0.74, mode: side-agent }
  - { pattern: "llm:escalation|fallback|retry",         topology: ecology,  entropy: 0.62, confidence: 0.46, mode: escalation }
  - { pattern: "llm:request|agent:start|pipeline:stage_start|infer:resolved|route:resolved|llm:routed", topology: face, entropy: 0.32, confidence: 0.72, mode: thinking }
  - { pattern: "memory|retriev|context|compact",         topology: ecology, entropy: 0.28, confidence: 0.76, mode: memory }
  - { pattern: "tool|scan|sweep|audit|rtk",              topology: ecology, entropy: 0.38, confidence: 0.70, mode: tool }
  - { pattern: "error|rollback|failed|failure",          topology: ecology, entropy: 0.78, confidence: 0.24, mode: error }
  - { pattern: "done|complete|success|response",         topology: face,    entropy: 0.14, confidence: 0.92, mode: complete }
  - { pattern: "codebase:topology|fix_loop:pass",        topology: codebase, entropy: 0.28, confidence: 0.78, mode: codebase }
  - { pattern: "rule_loop:cycle|rule_loop:clean",        topology: codebase, entropy: 0.45, confidence: 0.62, mode: fixing }
  - { pattern: "fix_loop:idle",                          topology: codebase, entropy: 0.10, confidence: 0.95, mode: settled }
  - { pattern: "rule_loop:converged",                    topology: codebase, entropy: 0.20, confidence: 0.82, mode: converged }

provider_detect: "claude|deepseek|gemini|gpt|openai|openrouter|mistral"

canonical_events:
  - master:emotion    # arousal, valence, focus, confidence, fatigue
  - master:clusters   # repository clusters with weight + evidence
  - master:topology   # topology switch
  - master:runtime    # runtime pressure, throughput, drift
  - master:attention  # zoom/map/act/targets from attention_context
  - master:pressure   # codebase + memory pressure heatmap
  - master:tooling    # tool dispatch + blast radius

palettes:
  operator: { bg: "#000000", fg: "#ffffff", accent: "#ff3344" }
  review:   { bg: "#0a0a0a", fg: "#cccccc", accent: "#3366ff" }
  visitor:  { bg: "#111111", fg: "#999999", accent: "#666666" }

runtime_modes:
  operator: { palette: operator, motion: 1.0, density: 1.0, topology_exposure: full }
  review:   { palette: review,   motion: 0.5, density: 0.8, topology_exposure: high }
  visitor:  { palette: visitor,  motion: 0.3, density: 0.4, topology_exposure: low }

resolutions:
  small:  { w: 320, h: 180 }
  medium: { w: 480, h: 270 }
  large:  { w: 640, h: 360 }

cell_grammar:
  single_pixel: signal
  block_2x2:    stable_entity
  checker:      uncertainty
  solid_rect:   confidence
  split:        disagreement
  jagged_edge:  risk
  marching:     data_flow
  fading:       memory_decay
  pulsation:    active_attention
  static_tile:  persistence
  spray:        entropy
  collapsing:   failure
  converging:   consensus

emotional_mapping:
  confidence: solidity
  uncertainty: dithering
  pressure: density
  focus: convergence
  overload: fragmentation
  agreement: synchronization
  risk: instability
  memory: persistence
  volatility: flicker
  recovery: gradual_recomposition

visual_fleet:
  field: RAILS/shared/frontend/visual_field.js
  controller: RAILS/shared/frontend/visual_surface_controller.js
  contract: pub4:visual
  surfaces:
    master: { topology: orb, purpose: cognition command center }
    social: { topology: terrain, purpose: city and community ambient field }
    dating: { topology: pair, purpose: proximity and connection }
    luxury: { topology: ambient, purpose: restrained fashion atmosphere }
    mannequin: { topology: mannequin, purpose: garment silhouette }
    radio: { topology: tunnel, purpose: audio-reactive depth field }

topologies:
  - id: face
    label: Cognition Mask
    purpose: Symbolic cognition surface — brows, eyes, mouth, attention vectors, asymmetry, confidence zones
    renderer: face.js
    anchors: [brow_left, brow_right, eye_left, eye_right, mouth, jaw, crown]
    zones:   [eyes, mouth, brows, jaw, crown, attention_vector]
    transitions: [thinking, speaking, listening, escalating, settling, error]
    palette: operator
    cell_rules:
      eyes:   { kind: focus,      density: 0.7, decay: slow }
      mouth:  { kind: speech,     density: 0.5, decay: fast }
      brows:  { kind: tension,    density: 0.3, decay: medium }
      crown:  { kind: memory,     density: 0.4, decay: slow }
    attention_behavior: track_user_cursor

  - id: codebase
    label: Repository Body
    purpose: Modules as clusters, dependencies as bridges, fractures as risk, density as ownership
    # The face draws it. codebase:topology reaches the face as entropy and
    # confidence through visual_bridge.js and as a cluster in cluster_miner.js;
    # a canvas of its own would be a second layer over the face, and what the
    # face looks like is the operator's call.
    renderer: face.js
    anchors: [module_centroids]
    zones:   [districts, vectors, bridges, fractures, field_density]
    transitions: [scanning, fixing, converged, drifting]
    palette: operator
    cell_rules:
      district: { kind: module,     density: 0.6, decay: slow }
      bridge:   { kind: dependency, density: 0.4, decay: medium }
      fracture: { kind: violation,  density: 0.9, decay: fast }
    attention_behavior: focus_on_active_file

  - id: ecology
    label: Runtime Ecosystem
    purpose: Memory, pressure, tools, councils, fix loops, risk, drift as habitat
    renderer: cognition_ecology.js
    anchors: [habitat_centers]
    zones:   [habitats, flows, clusters, storms, dead_zones, growth]
    transitions: [calm, storming, draining, regenerating]
    palette: review
    cell_rules:
      habitat:   { kind: memory,    density: 0.5, decay: slow }
      storm:     { kind: pressure,  density: 0.8, decay: fast }
      flow:      { kind: tool_call, density: 0.4, decay: medium }
      dead_zone: { kind: decay,     density: 0.2, decay: very_slow }
    attention_behavior: drift_with_runtime_pressure

  - id: face3d
    label: Semantic Bitmap Face
    purpose: Anatomical regions as runtime signals — Gmail6 redesign
    renderer: face3d_renderer.js
    status: live
    palette: operator

`````

### data/tts.yml

`````yaml
# Transcendent TTS — emotion-aware multi-engine orchestration (MLX / Replicate).
#
# THIS FILE DECIDES HOW MASTER SOUNDS ON THE COMMAND LINE. Transcendent.load_config
# reads it, `enabled` and `default_mode` are what Speech.synthesis_mode consults,
# and Speech.synthesize hands the text to Transcendent.synthesize whenever that
# mode comes back "transcendent" -- which is what `default_mode: transcendent`
# below asks for. The path is Cli::Session::ResultDisplay -> Voice::Playback.speak
# -> Playback.synthesize -> Speech.synthesize, so it runs on every spoken reply.
# bin/tts-speak takes the same door directly, exporting MASTER_TTS_MODE=transcendent.
#
# The web path now enters the same Transcendent door through
# Speech.synthesize_streaming_to_file. It keeps the TtsJob contract and falls
# back to the proven Edge/espeak path when Transcendent cannot produce audio.
# On OpenBSD, enabled alone forces transcendent mode and engine_chain here is
# overridden by MASTER_TTS_ENGINE_CHAIN or Engines::OPENBSD_CHAIN, so the chain
# below is the Mac's. MASTER_TTS_MODE remains the explicit operator override.
transcendent:
  enabled: true
  # Transcendent is the normal conversational path. MASTER_TTS_MODE=classic is the explicit fast override.
  fast_mode: false
  default_mode: transcendent
  personality: warm_erratic
  # mlx needs Python 3.10+ (brew install python@3.11). Until then: fast Edge voices.
  # English quality chain: expressive local engines first, then the stable Edge
  # route. Native-language routes are filtered in Engines.build_engine_chain.
  engine_chain: mlx, chatterbox, edge_melodic, edge, say
  emotion_enabled: true
  # Chatterbox/MLX already receive the measured emotional controls. Random
  # [laugh]/[chuckle]/[sigh] insertion is an effect, not an emotion measurement,
  # so it stays off unless the operator explicitly enables it.
  paralinguistic_tags: false
  # The pentatonic contour: a stylistic mode, for lyrical text only.
  melodic_enabled: true
  melodic_threshold: 0.28
  # Phrase segmentation and the rests between phrases, without the contour.
  # Separate from melodic_* because it is rhythm rather than style. Costs one
  # Edge round trip per phrase, capped at Melody::MAX_PHRASES. Set fast_mode true only
  # when latency matters more than expressive phrase rendering.
  phrase_rhythm_enabled: true
  # A Norwegian clause is always rendered with Pernille; English uses Jenny.
  # Language routing is a speech rule, not an optional stylistic switch.
  phrase_language_switching: true
  phrase_language_voices:
    nb: pernille
    ms: yasmin
    en: jenny
  # Local MLX (Apple Silicon)
  # The local Apple-Silicon path uses the expressive Chatterbox MLX model first;
  # Kokoro remains a provider fallback rather than the conversational default.
  mlx_model: mlx-community/chatterbox-fp16
  mlx_voice: default
  mlx_speed: 1.0
  exaggeration: 0.45
  cfg_weight: 0.42
  chatterbox_device: mps
  reference_clip: ""
  # Replicate cloud (VPS / OpenBSD primary)
  replicate_model: jaaari/kokoro-82m
  replicate_voice: af_bella
  replicate_speed: 1.05
  replicate_exaggeration: 0.45
  replicate_cfg_weight: 0.42
  # Cost/speed note: ~$0.008-0.015 per 1K chars; superior consistency on server vs local MLX

`````

`````yaml
version: 1

# Conservative regression guards. These are guardrails, not a definition of
# human naturalness. Automatic TTS metrics are useful for regressions but must
# not replace listening tests.
benchmark:
  min_score: 75
  speech_rate_wpm:
    min: 105
    max: 220
  dynamic_range_db:
    min: 6
  clipping_peak_db:
    max: -0.1
  pause_ms:
    min: 70
    max: 700

`````

### data/visual_rubric.yml

`````yaml
# reader: Master::Fix::VisualPass
# Visual judgement is constrained by the house. These are observable dimensions,
# not a generic beauty score.

dimensions:
  hierarchy: "One clear primary action; visual emphasis follows the task."
  alignment: "Edges, baselines, controls, and repeated elements share the established grid."
  rhythm: "Spacing and typography use the existing token scales; no arbitrary one-off values."
  density: "Worst-case content remains calm, legible, and free of accidental crowding or overflow."
  states: "Empty, loading, validation, error, and success states explain what happened and what can happen next."
  motion: "Entry, exit, and feedback motion use existing duration/easing tokens and honor reduced motion."
  content: "Real Norwegian and worst-case strings remain legible; punctuation and dates follow locale conventions."
  affordance: "Interactive elements look and behave like the same interaction vocabulary elsewhere in the product."

judgment:
  first_read: "Describe what the eye notices first and whether that matches the task."
  falsification: "State what observation could disprove the claimed visual defect."
  pairwise: "Prefer before/after or sibling-surface comparisons when deciding between two compliant alternatives."
  anti_sycophancy: "Name the five strongest observable weaknesses before proposing a refinement."

constraints:
  brand: "Use the house's own references, tokens, laws, and observed good surfaces; competitor screenshots are not style targets."
  edits: "Prefer existing primitives and token substitutions; never invent a new visual system inside a refinement."
  evidence: "A screenshot proves a rendered state; source proves implementation; neither alone proves intent."
  stopping: "When evidence is inconclusive, report INCONCLUSIVE rather than manufacture a taste verdict."

`````

### data/voice.yml

`````yaml
# Voice output rules — extracted from rules.yml (scan corpus stays in rules.yml).
# TTS synthesis policy: Ruby (speech.rb, tts_controller) and JS (face_speech_runtime.js) read `tts`.
# Persona registries (personas.yml, soul.yml) affect LLM text/style only when persona_affects_text_only is true.
# Engine chain / transcendent mode: data/tts.yml (not used by web TtsJob). VPS env: OPENBSD/etc/rc.d/master.
tts:
  # English defaults to en-US-JennyNeural. Norwegian speech is a separate
  # declared language route and MUST use nb-NO-PernilleNeural.
  #
  # language_voices is the source of truth for text-to-voice selection. The
  # Policy fallback, CLI Speech, web controller and face all read it instead of
  # embedding a second Norwegian voice choice.
  # English is the default voice. Norwegian is always spoken by Pernille.
  # The language map takes precedence over single_voice; single_voice is the
  # fallback for text whose language cannot be determined.
  single_voice: jenny
  neural: en-US-JennyNeural
  rotation:
    - jenny
  # Language locks are families, not a stylistic lottery. Female is the default;
  # MASTER_TTS_GENDER=male selects the declared male counterpart for that
  # language. English remains Jenny unless an explicit operator policy changes it.
  language_voices:
    en: jenny
    nb: pernille
    ms: yasmin
  language_voice_families:
    en: { female: jenny, male: andrew }
    nb: { female: pernille, male: finn }
    ms: { female: yasmin, male: osman }
  persona_affects_text_only: true
  # ON as of 2026-08-14. pushLiveStreamTts (face.part1.txt) pulls each finished
  # sentence off the model's stream and speaks it while the rest is still being
  # generated. With this false, nothing is spoken until the whole reply has been
  # generated AND the whole thing synthesised — two serial waits before any
  # sound, on a box with one CPU.
  #
  # Measured on the live box, same text, /chat/tts round trip:
  #
  #   idle          four sentences 3.05s   one sentence 2.16s
  #   under deploy  four sentences 19.31s  split by sentence: first audio 1.98s,
  #                 all four done by 8.6s
  #
  # So splitting is never worse and is dramatically better exactly when the box
  # is busy, which is when the wait is noticed. It also removes the whole
  # generation time from the wait, which no synthesis tuning can.
  #
  # It was `false` because it shipped as opt-in ("optional /voice stream on",
  # c129719c2), not because it broke. The guards were already here: listings are
  # not spoken mid-stream (looksLikeListingStream), and fragments below
  # TTS_MIN_CHUNK are held back. `/voice stream off` still turns it off per
  # browser, and that preference wins over this default.
  stream_live_default: true
  # With persona_affects_text_only these two ARE the effective rate/pitch for
  # every utterance (Personality#browser_profile substitutes them for the
  # persona's own).
  #
  # Rate and pitch tuning does not survive a voice change, so a new voice starts
  # from neutral and is retuned by ear. Roughly ±15% rate and ±50Hz is where
  # Azure neural voices stay natural.
  #
  # Small negative rate gives the neural voice room for sentence rhythm without
  # stretching vowels into an artificial drawl. Pitch stays neutral; sentence
  # roles add only a few hertz where useful.
  default_rate: "-5%"
  default_pitch: "+0Hz"

  # What the voice is put through after synthesis, chosen by the operator by ear.
  # Policy.post_chain reads it, Speech#shaped applies it, and browser_payload
  # carries it so the face shapes the same way the server does.
  #
  # Edge returns a bare neural voice at roughly broadcast level and no shaping
  # of its own, so everything below is post. The chain is dilla's, borrowed
  # rather than invented: `MASTER/tools/dilla/dilla.rb:2719` carries a vocoder wash
  # built as three resonant peaks near the vowel formants — 520, 1480 and 2520
  # Hz — and its own comment says it is only the formant HALF of a vocoder,
  # "because a real vocoder needs a modulator the renderer does not have".
  #
  # A speaking voice is the modulator that renderer lacks. Those peaks were
  # tuned for a synth pad and land on speech for the first time here: the
  # formants sit where a voice already puts its energy and lift it.
  #
  # A fixed makeup gain before the limiter, and no loudnorm. The chain runs
  # once per utterance now that a reply is spoken sentence by sentence, and
  # loudnorm normalises per file: measured on this Mac, two clips 20 dB apart
  # both left it at -3.9 LUFS, so a quiet trailing clause was lifted to meet an
  # emphatic opening and the reply spoke in one flat voice. A fixed gain keeps
  # what the synthesiser meant — the same sentence 10 dB down stays 9.3 dB down.
  #
  # +23 dB is what lands nearest the level the chain used to reach: -12.0 LUFS
  # against -9.6, measured through the whole chain on a spoken sentence. It also
  # flattens fewer samples than loudnorm did (astats flat factor 0.31 against
  # 14.73), because normalising first pushed the limiter harder than the gain
  # does. Gain after a limiter would be distortion rather than loudness, so it
  # stays before it. Operator's to re-tune by ear.
  #
  # A reader that cannot run ffmpeg should skip the chain and speak dry. A
  # missing filter must cost the effect, never the sentence.
  # Keep the voice organic: prosody supplies movement; the post-chain only
  # restores speech presence, removes sub-bass rumble and catches peaks.
  # Chorus/phaser were deliberately removed because modulation makes a neural
  # voice sound processed rather than alive.
  post_chain: "equalizer=f=520:t=q:w=1.1:g=2.0,equalizer=f=1480:t=q:w=1.3:g=1.5,equalizer=f=2520:t=q:w=1.5:g=1.2,highpass=f=70,lowpass=f=12000,acompressor=threshold=-20dB:ratio=1.7:attack=12:release=140:makeup=1,volume=17dB,alimiter=limit=0.98"

  # The bed under the speech, so a pause is not silence.
  #
  # dilla renders it: module Bed in MASTER/tools/dilla/dilla.rb, declared in
  # MASTER/tools/dilla/data/bed.yml, played by `ruby MASTER/tools/dilla/dilla.rb bed`. It was
  # a renderer of its own beside the hooks until the operator made it dilla's
  # (2026-09-14), so the whole declaration moved with it and only the level
  # under the voice stays here.
  bed:
    source: MASTER/tools/dilla/data/bed.yml
    gain_db: -14
  # No default_volume. The daemon protocol is {voice,rate,pitch,text} and
  # RbEdgeTTS::Communicate takes rate: and pitch: only, so a volume here was
  # read by nothing for as long as it existed. Adding one back means
  # extending the worker protocol first, and that changes how loud MASTER
  # is, which is an operator decision rather than a wiring one.
  # edge-tts --volume. The browser chain is the other half of "louder"
  # (face_speech_runtime.js: masterGain 1.9 -> 3.4, partial no longer played at
  # 0.85); this raises the synthesised signal itself rather than only its
  # playback gain, so the two do not fight for the same headroom.

voice:
  style: openbsd_dmesg
  # anti_simulation lives once, in soul.yml absolute.anti_simulation. The
  # copy that stood here was a shadow the accessor only read if soul lost
  # the key — and it had already drifted one word from the original.
  banned_output:
    - headlines
    - section_markers
    - bullet_lists_without_content
    - filler_phrases
    - hedging
    - sycophancy
  strunk:
    preambles: ["In summary,", "Consequently,", "Therefore,", "Notably,", "Importantly,"]
    hedges:
      en: ["I think that", "I believe", "will", "would", "might", "could", "perhaps", "seems", "appears"]
      nb: ["jeg tror", "jeg synes", "kanskje", "muligens", "virker som", "det kan hende", "etter min mening"]
    endings: ["as a result.", "for this reason.", "thus.", "in effect.", "accordingly."]
    code_preambles: ["# TODO: clarify intent", "# FIXME: review edge cases", "# NOTE: performance considerations", "# HACK: temporary workaround", "# REVIEW: assess after refactor"]  # scan: intentional — the markers the prompt forbids, not markers
    apply_to: [prose, comments, documentation, strings]
    never_apply_to: [code_logic, algorithms, data_structures]
    safeguards:
      - never_delete_variable_names
      - never_delete_function_calls
      - never_simplify_conditional_logic
      - never_collapse_diagnostic_output
  inverted_pyramid:
    - "Lead with the outcome."
    - "Provide key evidence next."
    - "Add implementation detail last."

  preserve:
    boot_message: "5-line dmesg style, never collapse to one line"
    diagnostic_output: "structured multi-line output is intentional, never compress to abbreviations"
    help_text: "include command name, description, and at least one example"
    spinner_feedback: "show elapsed time and status, do not remove progress indicators"
    refinement_scope:
      streamline: "remove redundancy, not information"
      polish: "refine wording, not delete output"
      minimize: "applies to prompt tokens, not diagnostic output"

`````

### gates/README.md

`````markdown
# Rails gates

This README is the living documentation for the Rails gate suite. Executable gate definitions and runner output remain authoritative.

Assessment date: 2026-08-01. Scope: RAILS family (brgen + verticals, amber,
bsdports) + MASTER web UI.

## Verdict

**Strong professional floor. Not yet “perfectionist complete.”**

What we have is among the denser Rails UI gate suites: source ratchets,
multi-step journeys, full-page inventory sims, geometry/reflow, keyboard +
mobile floors, mutation tests. A perfectionist still needs authenticated
personas, denser residual-EN chrome, reliable CDP under load, and MASTER face in
every browser leaf.

## Coverage map

| Layer | Gates | Adequacy |
|-------|--------|----------|
| Inventory / ports | apps_yml, port_inventory, shared_wiring | Solid |
| Schema / runtime | schema_migration, phantom_foreign_keys, rails_runtime | Solid |
| Design constitution | css_constitution, dialect_purity, payment_honesty, design_metrics | Strong |
| Source UX floor | surface_schema, chrome_i18n/empty lints, human_walkthrough, user_flow | Strong |
| Full-page matrix | **page_simulation** (137 triangle pages + bsdports when wired) | Strong source; live needs warm Falcon |
| Multi-step journeys | **flow_journey** (brgen verticals depth + amber + master) | Strong guest; no auth journeys |
| Phone UX | **mobile_flow**, reflow, geometry mobile | Good floor; CDP flake → inconclusive |
| Keyboard | **keyboard_flow** | Good; desktop-first |
| Pixel / visual | visual_contract, layout_snapshot, visual_quality | Canonical CDP capture + committed geometry snapshots; Council now consumes rendered evidence |
| MASTER web | master_web_assets, production, page_sim face/dashboard | Face OK; static offline soft |
| Integrity | gate_mutation, calibration, constitutional_scan | Solid |

## Gaps a perfectionist would still flag

1. **Authenticated personas** — no signed-in walk of cart checkout, dating
   matches, sell form submit, amber wardrobe mutations.
2. **Residual EN chrome** — measured 2026-08-01 instead of guessed at.
   `chrome_i18n_lint` now has an `aria_label` rule (both `aria-label="…"` and
   `aria: { label: "…" }`) and reports per kind: empty titles 0, search
   placeholders 0, hardcoded aria-labels **172** across the three apps and the
   shared engine. The aria baseline is 172 rather than 0 because closing it
   needs Norwegian copy, not a regex; it may only ratchet down, and
   `RAILS/test/chrome_i18n_lint_test.rb` fails both when a kind exceeds its
   baseline and when a baseline has been beaten and not lowered. Until then, a
   screen-reader user on `:nb` hears English for those 172 labels — which is the
   gap, now with a number on it.
3. **CDP reliability** — long rendered_suite + cold Falcon → timeouts;
   mobile/keyboard must not green-wash (inconclusive when &lt;3 surfaces
   measured).
4. **MASTER face browser leaf** — not first-class in mobile_flow preferred set /
   geometry_surfaces.
5. **Auth + :id pages** — page_sim source-only for show/edit; no seeded live
   IDs.
6. **visual_contract capture** — needs `VISUAL_CAPTURE=1` + running apps;
   it now reuses the canonical CDP session rather than a separate browser driver.
   `/fix RAILS` additionally captures the declared geometry surfaces and feeds the
   render to the same MASTER Council/repair loop.
7. **bsdports** — out of product focus triangle but still a Rails app; must
   appear in family `--all`.
8. **No server-side perf budget** — `web_vitals_budget` ratchets LCP and CLS
   on a real load, but nothing fails on p95 server time or payload bytes per
   route in the crawl manifest.
9. **No screen-reader path** — landmarks yes; no axe/full a11y tree walk beyond
   visual_contract capture helpers.
10. **gate_mutation** does not prove mobile_flow / page_simulation catch defects
    yet.

## Three instrument rules, each paid for

A gate that demands one of several correct outcomes reports the environment as
the tree: amber's `/demo` redirects home without a seeded wardrobe and brgen's
marketplace shows an empty state without listings, so a check that demands the
populated branch reads an empty database as a broken app. Name the set of
correct answers and keep each falsifiable.

A test that runs a gate over this tree and asserts clean proves nothing — it
passes against a gate whose body is `return ok`. Plant the defect, assert red
and named, remove it, assert green, and drive the test once against a gutted
gate.

Check what the instrument opens before believing what it says. A stylesheet
lint that globs a directory misses what the bundle pulls in through `@use` and
`@forward`, and a class extractor that stops at a quote cannot read a Ruby class
value with interpolation in it.

## Perfectionist run recipe

```zsh
# Warm apps first (Falcon), then:
export RBENV_VERSION=4.0.5
ruby MASTER/gates/runner.rb page_simulation flow_journey \
  layout_suite rendered_suite human_walkthrough shared_wiring \
  production generated_asset schema_migration port_inventory \
  constitutional_scan gate_mutation visual_contract

# Optional hard mode (deploy host / CI with Chrome + apps):
GATE_STRICT_INCONCLUSIVE=1 GATE_STRICT_SOFT=1 \
  ruby MASTER/gates/runner.rb rendered_suite page_simulation
```

## What “adequate” means here

| Bar | Status |
|-----|--------|
| Ship without obvious guest dead-ends | **Met** (page_sim + flows + verticals) |
| NN/g floor (status, landmarks, touch, overflow) | **Mostly met** (mobile_flow + reflow + status polish) |
| Pixel-perfect regression on every surface | **Not met** |
| Auth journeys + payment e2e | **Not met** |
| Zero EN under default_locale :nb | **Approaching** (lints 0; residual secondary chrome remains) |

---

Full-matrix user simulation for every full-page Rails surface in the **focus
triangle** (brgen · amber · MASTER web).

ruby MASTER/gates/runner.rb mobile_flow

# Desktop tab order
ruby MASTER/gates/runner.rb keyboard_flow
```

Snapshot: `gates/data/page_sim_inventory.yml` (regenerated each run). Report:

## What each page is checked for

### Source (always)

| Check | Principle |
|-------|-----------|
| Page identity (`content_for :title` / `h1` / `h2`) | hierarchy |
| `shared/empty_state` has `action:` (or opt-out) | NO_DEAD_ENDS |
| Interactive affordance (links / forms / search) | good_design_is_useful |
| Guest surfaces without hard auth-wall copy | clarity / guest_open |
| Form fields with labels / aria-label | accessibility |
| MASTER face + mission-control landmarks | triangle a11y floor |

### Live (when port open)

Soft-guest HTTP GET of every **guest**, **non-parameterised** path:

- Status 200–399
- No Exception / Routing Error chrome
- `main` / skip / face root landmarks
- Guest-open: no “Sign in to continue”
- Title or h1 present

Auth-only and `:id` show/edit pages need a seeded session or fixture id — source
covers their templates; live matrix targets guest browse.

## Multi-step journeys (`flows.yml`)

Beyond single-page GETs:

- Marketplace browse + cart honesty
- Sign-in reachable from home
- Live guest-open
- Nearby ↔ Live loop
- Search empty + query
- Communities, channels, messenger
- Dating discover
- Playlist / TV / takeaway / maps roots
- Amber wardrobe, feed, demo, AI entry

## Geometry / keyboard / visual

`BrgenVerticalSurfaces` now includes secondary apex paths (nearby, communities,
search, channels, conversations, marketplace deals/sell) so `rendered_suite`
walks them when Chrome is available. Amber feed / outfits / demo are in
`geometry_surfaces.yml`.

## Polish loop

Simulation is not report-only. Soft findings (residual EN CTAs, missing titles,
form labels) are fixed in the same pass:

1. `ruby MASTER/gates/runner.rb page_simulation`
2. Address soft/hard findings (i18n keys in `en.yml` + `nb.yml`, wire `t()`)
3. Re-run until source matrix is clean
4. When ports are open, clear live findings the same way

### Polish already landed from the matrix

| Area | What |
|------|------|
| Amber wardrobe hub | Full i18n: chips, lifecycle filters, tool groups |
| Amber feed / analytics / shopping / live sessions / capsule | EN chrome → `t()` |
| Brgen posts index/show/edit | Sort tabs, vote a11y, share, about, form labels |
| Brgen channels, home title, places, messages, dating profiles | i18n + headings |
| Brgen notifications + playlist party | Open/mark-read, party chat form label |
| Shared Edit/Cancel/Open CTAs | Batch `actions.edit` / `cancel` / `open` across triangle |
| Cart | Full i18n + confirm on send-all-offers |
| Status (#1) | live-search + autosave strings via `status.*`; flash `aria-live` |
| Freedom (#3) | Amber archive → flash undo restore CTA |
| Efficiency (#6/#7) | First-visit hotkey coach; i18n help; coach on brgen+amber |
| Errors (#9) | Branded 404/422/500 with home/Live/wardrobe CTAs |
| keyboard_flow | Prefers live/wardrobe/feed over auth-only surfaces |

- **bsdports** intentionally out of focus triangle; still has its own
`````

### gates/architecture.rb

`````ruby
#!/usr/bin/env ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

require_relative "../lib/master"

root = File.expand_path("..", __dir__)
report = Master::Phoenix.check(root:)

if report.clean
  puts Master::Phoenix.line(root:)
  exit 0
end

report.failures.each { |failure| warn "phoenix0: #{failure}" }
exit 1

`````

`````yaml
# Human calibration set for design gates (P5).
# Labels: pass | soft | fail
# Gate agreement keeps scores from drifting into cargo-cult regex.
#
# Process (monthly):
#   1. Add ~20 labeled screens (fixture or captured HTML path)
#   2. ruby MASTER/gates/runner.rb calibration
#   3. Review false positives/negatives + weight suggestions
#   4. Optionally apply: GATE_CALIBRATION_APPLY=1
#
# human is ground truth. Gate scores are hypotheses.

schema: 1
agreement_floor: 0.85
# Soft-band: human=soft accepts gate pass OR soft fail OR score within 15 of target
soft_band: 15
`````

### gates/data/constitutional_budget.yml

`````yaml
# Per-target ceilings for the constitutional scan, in the shape of
# MASTER/data/spine.yml: the number only ever ratchets down.
#
# The gate used to route every finding to result.warn and fail only when the scan
# output matched a crash marker (TODO.md: rails_gates_not_wired —
# "constitutional_scan_gate downgrades all findings to warnings"). Four full
# MASTER scans, twenty-one minutes, and a green result no matter what they found.
#
# Chasing zero is not the goal and never was — these are design-craft rules over
# three shipping Rails apps, and TODO.md's Constitution Scan Debt entry says so.
# What a ceiling buys is the thing a warning cannot: a change that adds findings
# fails, and lowering a number is a commit someone signs.
#
# Recorded 2026-08-01 from a full run (MASTER/gates/runner.rb constitutional_scan).
# Lower one with GATE_SCAN_RATCHET=1 after a run that beats it.
schema: 1
targets:
  # Re-measured 2026-08-02 (full MASTER/gates/runner.rb constitutional_scan, 1095s).
  # amber ratcheted DOWN 214 -> 207 (a real -7 gain, locked in). The other three
  # drifted up by the design-craft cost of this session's legitimate work — the
  # affiliate/partner stack, guest-pruning, and the SSO email_address fix landed
  # in brgen and shared — so their ceilings move to the measured values with this
  # reason, per the gate's "fix them or record a new ceiling with a reason". The
  # deltas are small (+1/+1/+3) and fall in false-positive-heavy categories
  # (DEAD_CODE=48 in shared has zero genuine unreachable code — conditional
  # `return … if` misread; the two flagged `system(...)` calls use the safe
  # arg-array form). Chasing them is explicitly not the goal; the ratchet still
  # guards against the next regression.
  # The four targets below (brgen 329, amber 164, bsdports 95, shared 182) are
  # measured values from a 2833s run over all four, not values anything was
  # fixed to earn. The numbers they replaced came from a run in which amber never
  # scanned. The gate grepped its whole output for LoadError/SyntaxError/
  # uninitialized constant/No such file BEFORE reading the violation count, so a
  # *finding* quoting one of those phrases read as a crash of the scan itself.
  # amber failed that way having scanned cleanly to 79-plus findings. The count is
  # now read first: a run that printed one did not crash. Its true figure is 164.
  #
  # The ratchet also could not write. Its rewrite matched
  # /^targets:\n(?:  \w+: \d+\n)+/, which requires the entries to sit directly
  # under `targets:` -- and this comment is in the way. It reported "brgen -> 329,
  # amber -> 164" and left 411/207 on disk. It now rewrites one line at a time and
  # fails the gate if the re-read does not match what it announced.
  # 1/21/1/1 -> 27/28/3/8 on 2026-08-22, the joined-the-scan shape: ABC_SIZE
  # arrived (the one external-linter signal with no bespoke equivalent,
  # written per scanner_overlaps_two_installed_linters' measured conclusion,
  # ratchet threshold 40) and its 42 RAILS findings were always in the tree,
  # never counted. Nothing regressed; the next GATE_SCAN_RATCHET run trues
  # any overprice downward.
  brgen: 27
  amber: 28
  bsdports: 3
  shared: 8

  # MASTER and OPENBSD, added 2026-09-06. MASTER judges every effect against
  # its constitution; until then the gate that applies the law read only the Rails
  # half, so MASTER and OPENBSD were governed by a law that never opened them.
  # MASTER is here
  # too and is not a duplicate of `rake selfcheck`: that runs error and critical
  # over lib and law, this is the whole registry over the whole tree.
  #
  # Every number in this file is the AESTHETIC profile, which is the first
  # `scan: done` line the gate reads. The full profile in the same run is much
  # larger — the former media/tool corpus was measured separately before its consolidation; OPENBSD 72, MASTER 532 — and re-basing against it is a
  # separate decision with seven new ceilings in it.
  #
  # Measured 2026-09-06 with MASTER_SCAN_DETERMINISTIC=1:
  #   OPENBSD  0  — the same, and both are therefore ratchets that fail on the
  #                 first design finding anyone adds, which is the point.
  #   MASTER  15  — the web face: EIGHT_PX_RHYTHM 8, MAGIC_COLOR 2, and one each
  #                 of FLAT_PIXELS, NO_DECORATIVE_FX, TOUCH_TARGET_MIN,
  #                 PIXEL_EXACT and RAMS_UNOBTRUSIVE.
  OPENBSD: 0
  MASTER: 15

`````

### gates/data/css_budget.yml

`````yaml
# Per-rule ceilings for css_constitution, in the shape of constitutional_budget.yml
# and MASTER's data/spine.yml: the number only ever ratchets down.
#
# All three rules were declared and unread before 2026-08-03. IMPORTANT was a
# constant in css_constitution.rb with no call site. eight_px_rhythm was checked
# by shared/lib/operator/rhythm_lint.rb against design_tokens.yml and the two token
# stylesheets only -- the definitions, never the use sites -- which matters
# because shared/README.md's 2026-07-28 decision made spacing, not borders, the thing
# that separates elements. magic_color_hex_ban_inline had no reader anywhere.
#
# Zero is not the target. These are three shipping apps' accumulated craft debt;
# the ceiling exists so the next change cannot add to it silently. Lower one with
# GATE_CSS_RATCHET=1 after a run that beats it.
#
# Recorded 2026-08-03 from a full run (MASTER/gates/runner.rb css_constitution).
#
# Re-measured 2026-08-09 over 92 stylesheets, up from 82. The gate globbed
# <app>/app/assets/stylesheets and brgen's five verticals are mountable engines,
# so 10 sheets and 1406 lines of dating/marketplace/playlist/takeaway/tv CSS
# were outside every ceiling here — the same blind spot RAILS/CLAUDE.md records
# for the four scanners that stopped seeing 57 views when the verticals moved.
# The `size` rule hard-fails on `_vertical_*` sheets by name and could not open
# one of them.
#
# important 119 -> 126, rhythm 82 -> 102 and magic_hex 132 -> 142 are that, and
# only that: +7/+20/+10 findings that were always in the tree and never counted.
# Nothing regressed to earn them and no new debt is being waved through. Every
# added hit is listed by file:line in the commit that widened the glob, so the
# claim is checkable rather than asserted.
#
# rhythm 102 -> 31 the same day: 65 spacing values snapped to the nearest
# allowed step, ties broken upward. The 31 that remain are the documented
# product pens, two idioms that only look off-grid (`margin: -1px` is half of
# the visually-hidden clip, -1000px parks a node off-screen), and 1px padding on
# inline chips, where the nearest allowed step is 0 and would delete it rather
# than align it. Below the grid is not off it.
# 89 -> 91 on 2026-08-13: brgen/_affiliate.scss in-feed tile labels. `gap: 2px`
# between title and price, `padding: 2px 4px` on the surface chip over the
# photo. Nearest allowed step is 4px, which doubles the hairline, or 0, which
# deletes it. Same class as the 1px chips above — below the grid, not off it.
# Re-measured 2026-08-10 over 94 stylesheets, up from 92. MASTER/web joined the
# scan: ai.brgen.no is reachable from brgen's own top nav, so a visitor crosses
# from three gated apps into an ungated one without leaving the product, and
# every glob here was shaped for a Rails app while MASTER keeps its stylesheets
# in web/public. Two files, 1513 lines, never counted by anything.
#
# important 126 -> 130, rhythm 31 -> 89, magic_hex 142 -> 150, type_scale 8 -> 10
# and weight_ladder 0 -> 2 are that, and only that. Nothing regressed to earn
# them. face.css's own 21 rule violations were fixed rather than absorbed —
# 5 keyword easings to var(--ease-out), 8 uppercase trackings to the 0.15em
# ceiling, 21 physical left/right to their logical twins, and the accent glow on
# #primer-title removed with the reduced-motion override that existed only to
# turn it off. What is left here is the counted debt of a fourth surface.
#
# rhythm's +58 is the largest and the least surprising: face.css positions a
# canvas overlay in device pixels against safe-area insets, which is not the
# 8px page grid and never claimed to be. It is a candidate for the next ratchet,
# not a licence.
schema: 1
rules:
  # 66 -> 60, measured. Nothing targeted these; the count was already 60 when
  # the geometry merge measured it, so six had been fixed by other work and the
  # ceiling had not followed. Left at 66 it re-admits them one at a time.
  important: 60
  # 89 -> 90 (2026-08-22). One line, and it is arithmetic rather than drift:
  # MASTER/web/public/chat_upload.css:30 insets #photo-button's ::before by
  # 13px, which is exactly how an 18px drawn square centres inside a 44px tap
  # target — (44 - 18) / 2. Both of those numbers are themselves law here
  # (--tap-min is 44; the square is the control's existing optics), so the only
  # spacing value that satisfies them is one this scale does not carry. Moving
  # it to 12 or 16 would decentre the square to satisfy a grid it is not on.
  # Traced with a faithful replica of this gate's own tally, which is the only
  # way it was separable from the other 89.
  # 90 -> 91 (2026-08-25). Not absorbed drift: brgen/_marketplace_nav_bar.scss
  # carries 10px, 6px, 6px and 5px across four use sites, all of them from
  # 0c110203b ("the marketplace nav cleared a collision that cannot happen"),
  # which is a deliberate redesign of that bar by the operator. Snapping them
  # to 8/4 moves rendered spacing in a nav that was just tuned by hand, and
  # this repo's rule is restore-or-ask on visual layout rather than invent.
  #
  # So it is banked and named, not waved through. If the bar should sit on the
  # grid, snap those four and run with GATE_CSS_RATCHET=1 — the number goes
  # back down and this paragraph goes with it.
  # 91 -> 90. Not a snapped value: the gate was counting the numbers inside
  # var() fallbacks as spacing literals, so the calc() in
  # brgen/_search_palette.scss scored a finding for using three tokens
  # correctly. See VAR_FALLBACK in css_constitution.rb. One finding, and it
  # was the instrument rather than the stylesheet.
  rhythm: 90
  # 150 -> 151 on 2026-08-11, and this one is a ceiling raise rather than a
  # measurement, so it is worth being exact about what it is.
  #
  # 09664a486 ("flatten the storefront header toward the front page nav") added
  # `border-color: #fff` in brgen/_marketplace_nav_bar.scss, which left
  # css_constitution and layout_suite red on main and took the whole RAILS contract
  # suite with them. The honest fix is a token, and there is no token that is white
  # in both themes -- so choosing one is a colour decision inside that session's
  # own redesign, not something to guess at from outside it.
  #
  # Raised so the suite measures everything else again. It comes back to 150 when
  # that hover border names a token: run with GATE_CSS_RATCHET=1 after.
  #
  # 151 -> 148 on 2026-08-13: bsdports/_jsfiddle_chrome.scss pointed three
  # use-sites at the worn :root tokens they already matched (#0f1a0f search-bg,
  # #1a3a1a border, #0a140a surface-elevated). Same paint; the literals left
  # the count.
  # 140 -> 138, measured, same shape as important above: two literals left the
  # tree without a sitting aimed at them.
  #
  # 138 -> 139 on 2026-09-01: 24c9844e5 ("the Ruby laws were reading a CDP
  # probe's JavaScript as Ruby") added `_search_yep.scss`'s suggestion divider
  # at the pen's own #ccc. That file is in the PEN_ALLOW list, so the literal
  # is counted deliberately rather than treated as palette drift. If the pen
  # is ever re-tokenised, run with GATE_CSS_RATCHET=1 to bring this back down.
  #
  # 139 -> 77 on 2026-09-09, and 62 of the 64 that left were never component
  # colour. This row read 140 and had been the deploy blocker for a week on the
  # recorded reading that the remainder were hardcoded hexes whose reduction
  # would change what is painted. Enumerated: 59 of the 115 in RAILS were the
  # fallback half of `var(--token, #hex)` — the shape this same gate already
  # exempts for `rhythm` through VAR_FALLBACK, because a value inside a fallback
  # is the token's own declared value and not a literal anyone chose at the call
  # site. Every one of those tokens is declared unconditionally on :root, so the
  # fallbacks were unreachable, and they had already drifted apart from each
  # other: --text carried #333333 in shared and #efefef in amber, --bg named the
  # dark #000000 under a scheme that defaults light, and --hover's #232030 was
  # the indigo the one scheme retired. Four more became real tokens
  # (--color-info into _tokens.scss, amber's duplicate success/warning deleted),
  # and one was a contrast defect: amber's second prefers-contrast block
  # restated --border as #2c2824, which is 1.44:1 on #000.
  #
  # Recorded at the measured low rather than left loose. The 77 that remain are
  # 25 in MASTER/web/public/face.css, which this gate also opens, and 52 in
  # RAILS that are all identity or replica — the pen-allowlisted marketplace nav
  # bar's Amazon values, the vertical accent map, the categorical monogram
  # fills, the yep.com recreation, amber's wardrobe gradient, bsdports' status
  # ambers. Reducing any of those is a colour decision, not a wiring one, so
  # this row is now a floor and the next raise needs a name.
  magic_hex: 77
  # Token pairs below WCAG AA (4.5:1) and in the AA..AAA band, as design_metrics
  # counts them. style.yml declares wcag_2_2_aaa; body text earns it (12.51:1
  # dark, 16.26:1 light) and the secondary/accent tier does not. The vertical
  # accent map was never paired against a background at all until 2026-08-03,
  # which is where 15 of these 30 came from.
  # 30 -> 0 on 2026-08-22: the campaigns cleared every below-AA pair without
  # a sitting ever targeting them — the vertical accent re-pairing and token
  # work did it as a side effect. Zero is now the floor, not an ambition.
  contrast_below_aa: 0
  # 65 -> 41 the same day. style.yml declares AAA; body text earns it and
  # the remaining 41 pairs are the secondary/accent band — lifting them is a
  # palette decision (operator), so the band is banked, not forced.
  # 41 -> 43 on 2026-08-24, and the tree did not get worse: luxury gained a
  # light_danger token. #a7473b was already rendered on amber's light grounds
  # and was already below AAA there; it simply was not declared, so this metric
  # could not enumerate it and the geometry gate reported it as a colour
  # "outside design_tokens.yml" instead. Declaring it moved the same two pairs
  # from invisible to counted. Removing the token puts this back to 41 and the
  # debt back out of sight, which is the trade this file exists to refuse.
  # 43 -> 45 on 2026-08-31, and this is a raise, so it carries its reason.
  #
  # The tree did not get worse. Every colour that moved since 969024b7b moved
  # darker or sideways: brgen_old_light.text_secondary #666666 to #545454,
  # openbsd_wscons.text_secondary #63c363 to #499149, vertical_accents.maps
  # light #5b8fd4 to #5585c5. Nothing was lightened; no token added or removed.
  #
  # The two new pairs are brgen_old_light.text_secondary on surface_elevated
  # (#f2f2f2) and on search_bg (#f0f0f0). At #666666 they scored 5.13 and 5.04,
  # already inside this band — but the token did not reach a pixel, so the
  # metric could not enumerate them. Painted pairs go 84 to 88 across that one
  # change. The darkening is what made them countable.
  #
  # So this is the light_danger trade one paragraph up, arriving by paint-reach
  # instead of by declaration: an improvement that raises the number because it
  # brings debt into view. Forcing 43 means lightening secondary text until the
  # metric stops seeing it, which is the trade this file exists to refuse.
  # 45 -> 37 on 2026-09-08, when six colour dialects became one greyscale scheme.
  # The eight that left are pairs no longer expressible: an indigo accent, a warm
  # luxury paper and a 2014 port each had their own near-AAA text, and there is now
  # one #333-on-#efefef and one #efefef-on-#000, both AAA with margin. The gate
  # enumerates 84 mode-matched pairs across the dialects and reports 0 below AA.
  #
  # The 37 that remain are almost all --danger, which is deliberately the one
  # non-grey token: a greyscale scheme cannot say "destructive", and light.danger
  # on bg is 4.96 — AA, short of the 7.0 target. Forcing those to AAA means either
  # a darker red on every surface or dropping the semantic, and neither is a
  # contrast decision.
  #
  # 37 -> 38 on 2026-09-12, and it is accounting rather than absorption. The
  # pair that joined did not exist in this census before that morning: the gate
  # was pairing marketplace_hover as a foreground against the page background,
  # which is text nothing draws, and the pair that IS drawn — the vertical ink
  # on that hover fill — went unmeasured. It measured 3.15 and was below AA.
  # Lightening the hover to #8d7e66 puts it at 4.80, so it left the below_aa
  # count (now 0, its ceiling) and entered this band.
  #
  # It is not pushed to AAA. #ab9c84 would reach 7.07 and is lighter than the
  # accent it replaces, so the hover would outshine the resting button. And the
  # accent itself is 5.45, in this same band: holding a hover to a stricter
  # standard than the token it belongs to is not a contrast decision either.
  contrast_below_aaa: 38
  # These two are what gives design_rules.yml's `typography` block a reader.
  # type_scale counts font-size literals off the --text-* ladder in
  # _tokens.scss; weight_ladder counts font-weight literals off
  # --weight-normal/bold/heavy. Both read their ladder out of the stylesheet
  # that declares it, so a gate copy cannot drift from the tokens.
  #
  # First measured at 154 and 61. The tree was running two type scales at once —
  # this ladder's 12/14/16/18/20 and a hardcoded 13/15/17 borrowed from x.com,
  # 89 sites deep — so the same role rendered 14px in one sheet and 15px in
  # another. The operator picked the token ladder; the 13/15/17 sites moved onto
  # it and the weight ladder was re-cut to an even 400/600/800.
  #
  # What is left in type_scale is nine deliberate one-offs, not drift: brand
  # display type in amber (60/120px), the animated marketplace logo, the offline
  # hero, the swipe placeholder glyph, and `html, body { font-size: 21px }` in
  # _minimal.scss — that last one is the large-screen root scale, and snapping
  # it to a step would rescale every rem in the system.
  #
  # +2 and +2 on 2026-08-10 are MASTER/web joining the scan (see the header).
  # face.css runs a terminal type ramp — 10/11/13px status chips, monospace, on
  # a canvas — and a 700 weight in two places. Neither reads the RAILS token
  # ladder, because face.css has no access to it: it is served from
  # MASTER/web/public, outside the asset pipeline that defines --text-* and
  # --weight-*. Snapping the numbers alone would only hide that; the fix is a
  # shared token source, which is a decision, not a ratchet.
  # 10 -> 12 on 2026-08-21, a raise in the magic_hex-151 shape: f75050a6d
  # ("amber chrome is the Caprasimo mark") set the mark at 200px with a 40px
  # footer variant in _brand.scss — the same deliberate-lockup class as the
  # recorded 60/120px display type, chosen by that session's own redesign.
  # Brand display type does not read the body ladder anywhere in this tree;
  # if the mark is ever cut to the ladder, run with GATE_CSS_RATCHET=1.
# 0 -> 5 on 2026-09-12, and every one of the five was already in the tree.
#
# The legal footer carried its type system as an inline <style> element inside
# shared/_site_legal_footer.html.erb, which all three layouts render. This gate
# reads stylesheets, so for as long as those rules lived in an ERB it could not
# see them. Extracting them to _site_legal.scss changed nothing a reader sees —
# measured on brgen.no/privacy before and after, .legal-prose is 724.397px wide
# and its h1 28.8px/33.12px either way — and it put five off-scale values in
# front of a gate for the first time: 13px, 1.6rem, 0.72rem, 0.85rem, 1.05rem.
#
# They are not new debt and they are not mine to snap: each one is a size
# somebody sees, and the file's own header records that the snap is the
# operator's decision. The ceiling is here so the sixth cannot arrive quietly.
  type_scale: 5
# 2 -> 3 on 2026-09-12, from the same extraction: `.site-legal .site-verify
# strong { font-weight: 700 }`. The other two are MASTER's face.css. Same
# argument as type_scale above — the value is unchanged, only newly visible.
  weight_ladder: 3
  # gap_over_margin and card_padding_px were config keys design_metrics
  # confirmed present and css_constitution never applied to a sheet.
  # First measured 2026-09-05. Documented product pens are skipped, same
  # as flat_ui, so the seven child-margins in the marketplace logo and
  # nav bar are not this number. Zero is the floor: the next `> * {
  # margin }` fails.
  child_margin: 0
  # One hit: shared/_minimal.scss:212 `.card { padding: 1rem }`. 1rem is
  # 16px; the law is 24. Changing it is a look decision, so it is banked.
  card_padding: 1
  # line-height literals not written as var(--leading-*), first measured
  # 2026-09-13 at 85 across the fleet and MASTER/web. Moving one onto a token
  # changes leading unless the literal equals a step, so the snap is the
  # operator's; the ceiling is here so the eighty-sixth cannot arrive quietly.
  leading: 85

# Built-stylesheet weight, in kilobytes, per app. Same ratchet as the counts
# above: measured from the tree, never from another product's published figure,
# and it only goes down.
#
# application.css is measurable after the checked-in SCSS has been explicitly
# compiled. The build output is intentionally gitignored and therefore does not
# exist in a clean checkout until the build step runs. public/assets/ and compiled
# JS are likewise generated output, not source.
#
# Seeded 2026-08-31 from the generated builds: brgen 203.6KB, amber 110.2KB,
# bsdports 64.1KB, each rounded up to the next whole KB. Nothing was measured
# as debt and nothing is being waved through — this is the first reading, and
# what it buys is that the next change cannot add weight silently.
#
# It bought exactly that on 2026-09-08, and this is the record of it. brgen's
# build was 202.0KB and comfortably under on 2026-09-05. Then 42fedd139 (the
# messenger redesign) added 6,129 bytes in one commit and took it to 208.0KB,
# straight through this ceiling; c0a351b05 added 1,263 more and cdb0998b0 181,
# ending at 209.4KB. The gate went red and stayed red, and with it every brgen,
# amber and bsdports deploy — amber sat on a 2026-08-29 commit and bsdports on
# 2026-08-22 while this row was the thing in the way. Read per commit, the
# breach is one change, not accumulated drift.
#
# 3,123 bytes came back out on 2026-09-09, all of it duplication and none of it
# paint. The built file was parsed rule by rule and every byte attributed to a
# source sheet: brgen's _root.scss carried a whole second copy of its light
# theme inside @media (prefers-color-scheme: light) at the same specificity two
# lines below the unconditional one (1,061B); _posts.scss restated the seven
# comment-chrome rules shared/_chat_reactions.scss owns and loads after it;
# _mobile.scss restated .tab-bar and four .tab-item rules that shared/_tab_bar
# owns; _forms.scss restated .btn:hover; .visually-hidden was declared three
# times identically; --feed-max sat in a palette mixin and an app-root mixin
# both; and the messenger's own new CSS repeated one hover state across six
# controls and two list-row cells across four rows. Every cut was checked for
# cascade order first — the merged hover list is stated at the earliest of its
# six so nothing moves past .messenger-rail-room[aria-current="page"].
#
# brgen stays at 206 and now sits AT it, with 89 bytes of room. That is not
# comfort: the next messenger-shaped commit has to carry its own cut, and the
# named places to look are the three PP Neue Montreal @font-face blocks (~1KB,
# pointing at woff2 that do not exist in this app, and a licensing decision the
# operator owns) and the 134 selectors css_coverage_lint records as unused —
# 153 until 2026-09-10, when that census learned to read a class value written
# as a Ruby expression and nineteen of them turned out to be painting.
# What is NOT waste, and was examined and left: the per-file
# prefers-reduced-motion guards, which look redundant under _animations.scss's
# global !important reset and are the deliberate survivors of the 4211c4ebb
# pass — the convention is that a guard lives in the file with the animation it
# guards, so that moving a sheet cannot orphan it; and _coverage_fills.scss,
# which is real styling for real classes and holds undefined_class at 0.
#
# amber 111 -> 109 and bsdports 65 -> 64, measured the same day. Both fell
# because the shared engine stopped restating what it already declared, so the
# saving is real rather than a build artefact, and a number that may fall and
# never rise is recorded when it falls.
weight_kb:
  # 206 -> 207 on 2026-09-12, named rather than absorbed. 0574a3ecc added
  # 1,598B for the two-band phone chrome — the wordmark over the nav, icons in
  # one corner — across _nav_swiper.scss and _root.scss. That is a deliberate
  # design change, so cutting it would undo the work rather than pay for it.
  #
  # 210B came back the same day and are subtracted from the raise: the three
  # PP Neue Montreal @font-face blocks each carried a url() for
  # /fonts/pp-neue-montreal-latin-<w>-normal.woff2, and public/fonts/ holds one
  # file, which is Bricolage. Each was a 404 as well as its bytes, for a face
  # whose licence forbids serving it anyway. local() stays, so a visitor who
  # owns the font still wears it.
  #
  # The reserve the note above named is smaller than it looked. Those font
  # url()s were most of the "~1KB" it offered, and the 134 unused selectors are
  # not spendable without reading them: the census counts `woff2`, `type`,
  # `nth` and `ProseMirror` among them, and the last is applied by the editor
  # at runtime.
  #
  # 203 -> 215, 108 -> 110 and 64 -> 66 on 2026-09-25, named rather than
  # absorbed. The committed builds were Sass error pages from 2026-09-23 to
  # 09657e7c9, so nothing weighed the design work that landed meanwhile: the
  # Radio discovery surface (51c257ec7, 269 lines, brgen), the storefront
  # promotional art system (2e0b2ad3d, shared, so all three apps), the three
  # marketplace layout variants (b954ac84f, 5abc353b9), the ambient chat's
  # desktop surface (c4801541a) and the Material 3 message bubbles and typing
  # pulse (80be5eb12). Each was a deliberate design change, so cutting it would
  # undo the work; the rebuild is the first measurement of it.
  #
  # brgen 215 -> 235 on 2026-09-25, named rather than absorbed, in two parts.
  # 234KB is what origin/main already compiled to: the marketplace bol storefront
  # (6f96f26cb, dc061e474, dd5e32b7a, 8cf08ce6d, 4611d264a, bc6cbaab7, 9379e4112)
  # landed its SCSS without rebuilding, so the committed build weighed 215 while
  # the source weighed 234, and the first rebuild measured it. The last 1.5KB is
  # the antigravity.google treatment the operator asked for the same day: the
  # display page header, the black sign-in pill, the quiet footer and the
  # section rhythm. Each is a deliberate design change.
  #
  # 235 -> 236 the same day for the marketplace commercial layer the operator
  # authorised: the gated sale red, pill CTAs, the accent retint. 195 bytes of
  # it were paid back by folding the listing row's two duplicated action
  # rules into one; the rest is the layer.
  #
  # 236 -> 215, amber 110 -> 102 and bsdports 66 -> 61 on 2026-09-25, paid for
  # without touching a painted value: rules no template, engine, shared partial,
  # helper or script names; brgen's second copy of the promotional art;
  # var(--token, fallback) where the token is always declared; declarations a
  # later same-selector rule always outranks; unread custom properties; the
  # layered palette, luxury tokens, drawer chrome and .btn base brgen outranks
  # or never renders (switches in _tokens, _shell and _buttons, off only in
  # brgen); and prefixes allow_browser :modern does not need. Proven by nine
  # pages at 390 and 1440 screenshotting identically and by computed custom
  # properties matching in eight theme states. The badge pill and main's
  # unbuilt SCSS came in after and fit: brgen is 219,871B, 289B of room.
  brgen: 215
  amber: 102
# 64 -> 65 on 2026-09-12. Mobile-first costs bytes: stating the phone case
# unconditionally and restoring the wider one at a min-width edge writes each
# value twice where a max-width block wrote it once. Seventeen queries were
# converted across the three apps to satisfy MOBILE_FIRST, which is law in
# MASTER/law/css.rb, and bsdports' sheet went 64.2KB -> 64.8KB.
#
# It is a real raise, not a rounding one, and it is the price of the directive
# rather than of new features. brgen and amber absorbed the same change inside
# their existing ceilings. 64 -> 66 on 2026-09-25 is the shared promotional art
# and chat styles, named with brgen's raise above.
  bsdports: 61

`````

### gates/data/exemplars.yml

`````yaml
# Structural exemplars for design skill scoring (P3).
# Not pixel clones of Newegg/Hinge/Jodel — document-order + marker grammar
# that encode "what good looks like" for each dialect.
#
# score: points awarded when pattern matches (max per exemplar = sum of parts)
# required: hard fail if missing (severity hard)
# weight used for total quality rollup

exemplars:
  marketplace_tile:
    label: marketplace product tile (Tise/Bol/Newegg grammar)
    dialect: marketplace
    principle: hierarchy / catalog_retail
    target_score: 85
    parts:
      - id: root_card
        pattern: 'class="[^"]*deal-card'
        points: 15
        required: true
      - id: whole_card_hit
        pattern: 'deal-card-hit'
        points: 15
        required: true
      - id: media_before_body
        order: ['deal-card-img|deal-card-media', 'deal-card-body']
        points: 20
        required: true
      - id: price_before_title
        order: ['deal-price', 'deal-card-title']
        points: 25
        required: true
      - id: meta_row
        pattern: 'deal-meta'
        points: 10
      - id: no_social_feed_card
        forbid: 'class="[^"]*feed-card'
        points: 15
        required: true

  dating_card:
    label: dating swipe card (Hinge/Raya face-first)
    dialect: dating
    principle: hierarchy / face
    target_score: 80
    parts:
      - id: root_card
        pattern: 'class="[^"]*swipe-card'
        points: 20
        required: true
      - id: photo_first
        order: ['swipe-photo|swipe-placeholder', 'swipe-body|swipe-actions|swipe-bio']
        points: 25
        required: true
      - id: primary_actions
        pattern: 'swipe-action'
        points: 20
        required: true
      - id: like_and_pass
        pattern: 'swipe-action--like'
        points: 10
      - id: pass_action
        pattern: 'swipe-action--pass'
        points: 10
      - id: low_chrome
        forbid: 'navBar|deal-grid|compose-box'
        points: 15

  live_card:
    label: live hyperlocal note (Jodel grammar)
    dialect: social
    principle: clarity / hyperlocal
    target_score: 80
    parts:
      - id: root_card
        pattern: 'class="[^"]*live-card'
        points: 20
        required: true
      - id: anon_author
        pattern: 'live-card-author|>anon<|anon'
        points: 15
        required: true
      - id: body
        pattern: 'live-card-body'
        points: 15
        required: true
      - id: vote_or_actions
        pattern: 'live-card-actions|feed-action|post_vote'
        points: 15
      - id: no_identity_chrome
        forbid: 'avatar_url|compose-avatar|author-handle|@\w+'
        points: 15
        # soft-ish: @ in content is rare in structure
        required: false
      - id: no_retail_dialect
        forbid: 'deal-card|navBar|deal-price'
        points: 20
        required: true

  marketplace_first_screen:
    label: marketplace catalog first screen
    dialect: marketplace
    principle: reading_patterns / catalog
    target_score: 85
    parts:
      # The claim is that the nav comes before the catalogue region, and an empty
      # catalogue is still a catalogue region. order_ok? fails a step it cannot
      # find, so on a checkout with no listings the marketplace rendered its
      # empty state and this required part reported the page as structurally
      # broken — an empty database read as a defect, and the live probe has been
      # red on it. empty-state-title rather than empty-state, because the
      # wrapper class also appears in chrome that can precede the nav.
      - id: nav_before_grid
        order: ['navBar', 'deal-grid|deal-card|empty-state-title']
        points: 25
        required: true
      - id: search_present
        pattern: 'marketplace-nav-search|name="q"'
        points: 20
        required: true
      - id: single_h1
        # scored in visual_quality; here require at least one h1
        pattern: '<h1\b'
        points: 15
        required: true
      - id: cart_or_sell
        pattern: 'Cart|Sell|listings/new'
        points: 15
      - id: guest_open
        forbid: 'Sign in to continue'
        points: 25
        required: true

# Page-level visual quality rubric (HTML structure; not pixel baseline).
quality:
  # 100, on the operator's instruction of 2026-09-12: every Rails surface scores
  # full marks on every design measure, no exception. All ten do today — brgen
  # and its six verticals, amber and bsdports, measured live.
  #
  # A target equal to the maximum means the first point lost is a failure, which
  # is the point. It is affordable only because the rubric was corrected the
  # same day: cta_budget counted every <button> in the document, including a
  # collapsed composer's toolbar, two dismiss buttons and a PWA install prompt,
  # and took 9 points off all three live surfaces for chrome. No design work
  # could have paid that back.
  target_score: 100
  weights:
    landmarks: 20
    hierarchy: 20
    cta_budget: 15
    guest_open: 15
    dialect_purity: 15
    density: 15
  rules:
    landmarks:
      require_any:
        - 'skip-link|Skip to main'
        - '#main-content|<main\b'
    hierarchy:
      max_h1: 1
      min_h1: 0  # warn soft if 0
    cta_budget:
      # The peer-choice limit is MASTER's: rules.yml UX_LAWS.hick
      # max_visible_choices. It is not restated here, because it was, as 4
      # against the law's 7, and the private copy won for months.
      max_btn_primary: 3
    guest_open:
      forbid: 'Sign in to continue'
    dialect_purity:
      # surface-specific overrides applied in code
      marketplace_forbids: 'swipe-card|feed-card'
      live_forbids: 'deal-card|navBar'
      dating_forbids: 'deal-grid|navBar'
    density:
      # soft: extreme short pages with almost no structure
      min_bytes: 400

`````

### gates/data/flows.yml

`````yaml
# User journeys as state machines with postconditions on state.
#
# The existing user_flow_gate probes a list of URLs and asserts a regex appears
# in each body. That cannot tell you whether add-to-cart changed the cart, or
# whether a "guest-open" surface quietly redirected to the sign-in page and
# returned 200 from there. These flows assert relations between steps:
# counts that must move, redirects that must or must not happen, final paths.
#
# steps[].count captures an integer from the body by counting regex matches;
# assert[] then compares captures to each other or to literals. No expression
# evaluation — {left, op, right} only, where right may name another capture.

flows:
  - id: bsdports_search_narrows
    app: bsdports
    description: Searching a catalogue must return fewer results than browsing it, and not zero.
    requires_data: [total]
    steps:
      - name: browse_all
        get: /ports
        expect_status: [200]
        count: { pattern: 'href="/ports/[^"]+"', as: total }
      - name: search_git
        get: /ports?q=git
        expect_status: [200]
        count: { pattern: 'href="/ports/[^"]+"', as: hits }
    assert:
      - { left: total, op: ">", right: 0, why: "browsing the catalogue shows something" }
      - { left: hits, op: ">", right: 0, why: "a common term finds matches (search is wired to data)" }
      - { left: hits, op: "<=", right: total, why: "a query narrows, never widens" }

  - id: bsdports_empty_state_has_next_step
    app: bsdports
    description: A no-match search is a dead end unless it offers an action (NO_DEAD_ENDS).
    steps:
      - name: no_match
        get: /ports?q=zzz-no-such-port-exists
        expect_status: [200]
        expect_body:
          - '(?i)no (results|ports|matches)|nothing|empty|try'
        count: { pattern: 'href="/ports/[^"]+"', as: hits }
        expect_any:
          - '(?i)<a[^>]+href="/ports"'
          - '(?i)clear|reset|browse|all ports|try again'
    assert:
      - { left: hits, op: "==", right: 0, why: "a nonsense query returns no rows" }

  - id: brgen_guest_marketplace_browse
    app: brgen
    description: Marketplace browsing must work without an account and without a redirect to sign-in.
    steps:
      - name: listings
        get: /
        host: markedsplass.brgen.no
        expect_status: [200]
        expect_final_path: /
        forbid_body:
          - "Sign in to continue"
        expect_any:
          - 'navBar|deal-grid|deal-card|listings|Markedsplass'

  - id: brgen_cart_is_honest_about_auth
    app: brgen
    description: >
      The cart requires a session (carts_controller: require_user_session). Whatever it
      does, it must not answer 200 with an empty shell — either it shows a cart, or it
      sends the visitor somewhere that explains what to do next.
    steps:
      - name: cart
        get: /cart
        host: markedsplass.brgen.no
        expect_status: [200, 302, 303]
        expect_any:
          - '(?i)cart|handlekurv|sign in|log in|logg inn|session'

  - id: brgen_sign_in_reachable_from_home
    app: brgen
    description: A visitor must be able to reach sign-in from the front page by following a link.
    steps:
      - name: home
        get: /
        host: brgen.no
        expect_status: [200]
        expect_any:
          - 'href="/session/new"'
      - name: sign_in
        get: /session/new
        host: brgen.no
        expect_status: [200]
        expect_final_path: /session/new
        expect_any:
          - '(?i)password|sign in|logg inn|vipps|google'

  - id: amber_wardrobe_browse
    app: amber
    description: Wardrobe index must render for a visitor and link to individual items.
    steps:
      - name: home
        get: /
        expect_status: [200]
      - name: items
        get: /items
        expect_status: [200]
        count: { pattern: 'href="/items/[0-9]+"', as: items }
    assert:
      - { left: items, op: ">=", right: 0, why: "index renders whether or not it is seeded" }

  - id: brgen_guest_nearby_and_live
    app: brgen
    description: The hyperlocal loop is one surface now and stays guest-open.
    steps:
      - name: nearby
        get: /nearby
        host: brgen.no
        expect_status: [200]
        expect_final_path: /nearby
        forbid_body:
          - "Sign in to continue"
        expect_any:
          - '(?i)nearby|location|live|share'
      # /live is a redirect to the geo room since the Jodel feed was folded into
      # the front page. A visitor with no coordinates cannot be in a geo room, so
      # #room sends them back to /nearby to turn location on -- two redirects,
      # landing where they can act. What this step proves is that neither hop
      # puts a signup wall in front of the hyperlocal layer.
      - name: live_redirects_to_the_room
        get: /live
        host: brgen.no
        expect_status: [200]
        expect_final_path: /nearby
        forbid_body:
          - "Sign in to continue"

  - id: brgen_guest_search
    app: brgen
    description: Global search is reachable and honest when empty.
    steps:
      - name: search_empty
        get: /search?q=
        host: brgen.no
        expect_status: [200]
        expect_any:
          - '(?i)search|søk|query|result|empty|try'
      - name: search_term
        get: /search?q=bergen
        host: brgen.no
        expect_status: [200]
        forbid_body:
          - "Sign in to continue"

  - id: brgen_guest_communities
    app: brgen
    description: Community index/browse works without signup.
    steps:
      - name: index
        get: /communities
        host: brgen.no
        expect_status: [200]
        expect_final_path: /communities
        forbid_body:
          - "Sign in to continue"
        expect_any:
          - '(?i)communit|community|explore|join|create'

  - id: brgen_guest_messenger_inbox
    app: brgen
    description: Messenger host and apex conversations stay guest-open.
    steps:
      - name: apex_inbox
        get: /conversations
        host: brgen.no
        expect_status: [200]
        forbid_body:
          - "Sign in to continue"
        expect_any:
          - '(?i)message|conversation|messenger|chat|compose'
      - name: vertical_inbox
        get: /
        host: messenger.brgen.no
        expect_status: [200]
        forbid_body:
          - "Sign in to continue"

  - id: brgen_guest_dating_discover
    app: brgen
    description: Dating discover is guest-browsable (swipe may soft-prompt later).
    steps:
      - name: discover
        get: /
        host: dating.brgen.no
        expect_status: [200]
        expect_final_path: /
        forbid_body:
          - "Sign in to continue"
        expect_any:
          - '(?i)dating|swipe|oppdag|profile|match'

  - id: brgen_guest_playlist_tv_takeaway_maps
    app: brgen
    description: Vertical roots render without hard auth walls.
    steps:
      - name: playlist
        get: /
        host: radio.brgen.no

      - name: up
`````
